We weren't thrilled or ecstatic after eating this chocolate, but we have nothing bad to say about it.

Taste is subjective, obviously, other reviews have detailed the product. I'll just add my subjective evaluation. It tasted good to me and I was not bothered by the texture. I prefer a darker chocolate and, at 54%, this bar was sweeter than one that I would buy for myself.

The Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate is one of the best dark chocolate bars I've ever eaten. My son felt the same way about it too. The flavor was excellent and it was neither overly sweet nor was it bitter like some dark chocolate candy. I would definitely buy this product after trying the sample from Amazon Vine.

Newman's is a brand that I'm used to hearing on fig bars, prunes, and other things much healthier than chocolate, so I wasn't sure how good their chocolate was going to be. I was very pleasantly surprised to find that not only was their chocolate very fancy, but it was also very smooth and not as bitter as other dark chocolates.

The packaging, as you can see from the picture on the description page, is very ornately designed, and the bar is the same. It is divided into sixths, and on each sixth there is an engraved N.

The taste, which I was very surprised at, wasn't bitter like Hershey's dark chocolate tends to be, but it wasn't too sweet. It was just the right bittersweet mixture! Also, on top of this, it had a very creamy texture, much like milk chocolate would.

In one 2.25 ounce bar, there are 330 calories, so I wouldn't necessarily describe this as a healthy snack, but all of the ingredients are organic, making it more nutritious than your average chocolate bar.

Overall, it is a deliciously different type of dark chocolate bar that I recommend to all chocoholics (like me).

I've been a fan of Green & Black's Maya Gold, Organic Dark Chocolate with Orange & Spices, 3.5-Ounce Bars (Pack of 5) for many a year, so I was delighted to be offered Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar, 3.25-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12) for review. (There is currently no link availble to the Pack of 12 2.25 ounce bars) I've been anxiously waiting for my package to arrive, as I had discovered a few recipes on the Newman's Own site, one of which is for a Chocolate Angel Cake that sounded just delightful - and a great way to use up some of that chocolate! Imagine my surprise when that Pack of 12 turned out to be a single 2.25 ounce bar!

As a result, I really cannot comment on this particular product other than to say it has a nice, smooth chocolate taste, though it is fairly low in cocoa solids. Any other properties that Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate might have as a candy or confection coating or baking ingredient will remain untested. Strictly as a chocolate bar, this is one I can take or leave. Green & Black's - long involved in the organic, sustainable rainforest movement - will remain my go-to dark chocolate bar.

I don't usually eat bars of plain chocolate but I found myself going back to this one, breaking off piece after piece.  It was smooth and not at all bitter.  There was no strange after taste, which I've experienced with some other dark chocolates.  I had planned on saving some to share with my husband but I'm not sure it will last that long...

I am a big fan of the Newman's Own products, and especially the Organics line -and a decent fan of dark chocolate as well :), but I would have liked this bar more if the cocoa content was higher than 54%.  I found the taste to be comparable to some other 65-70% cocoa bars (not too sweet-not too bitter).  The bar size is approximately 4.5"x2.75"x1/4" thick, and easily divided into 6 sections. Good tasting overall.

The dark chocolate flavor of this NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK CHOCOLATE BAR is mild, compared to dark chocolate bars manufactured by specialty candy makers (for example, See's Candies). But the flavor is quite good, especially for a "commercial" candy bar designed for general sale in grocery stores. Unlike many health food store "organic" products, this "organic" chocolate bar leaves no unpleasant aftertaste.

The bar (approximately 2.5" x 4.5") breaks into six large snack pieces. One bar (one serving) weighs 64 grams, has 330 calories (200 fat calories), and 22 grams total fat. There are 5 grams sodium, 37 grams carbohydrates, 4 grams fiber, 28 grams sugar, and 3 grams protein.

The label warns that the bar is manufactured on equipment that may have been used to process other products containing peanuts, other nuts, milk powder, wheat, soy and egg (although the bar itself contains none of these). The bar is 54% cocoa (Rainforest Alliance Certified).

Because I'm a big fan of "Newman's Own" products, I was eager to try this offering from the "Newman's Own Organics" line. It did not disappoint.

My wife and I independently taste-tested this product. My wife is a regular consumer of dark chocolates while I tend to prefer milk chocolate, and/or chocolates with fillings. After trying it out, we both decided that we would not purchase this product in the future, though for different reasons. Here are our independent reviews:

My wife: I am confused by the labeling of this product. It is called a 'dark chocolate' but has a 54% cacao content. Most dark chocolates that I buy have upwards of 65% - 75% cacao. When I first opened the package, I noticed a smoky aroma. I eat a lot of dark chocolate, including raw chocolate, but I never noticed such a smoky aroma before and found it pleasant. My first bite was disappointing. It is a bit too sweet for me, and is certainly significantly sweeter than the dark chocolates that I buy. It is smooth, which I like. While I appreciate the fact that Newman's own is producing an organic, minimally processed, chocolate I will not purchase this again.

Me: From my first bite I knew that this chocolate was not for me. It had a distinctly waxy feel that I usually associate with inferior chocolates - this was an immediate turnoff. There was absolutely nothing distinctive about this chocolate - no fruity notes, no particular bitterness, nothing that sticks out. While this chocolate is better than a lot of what constitutes the mass market, I cannot recommend it.

I started this review process on a bad note: I was under the impression that I was destined to review "Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar, 2.25-Ounce Bars (Pack of 12)." In fact, I received a pack of one. You can see the problem right off, particularly since I had recruited three other tasters to help me evaluate the product and then had to tell them they each only got a quarter of one bar.

The bar is smaller than most other organic chocolate bars on the market (at least in my market), so I'm hopeful it will be a bit cheaper. (Many run from $3.50 to $4.50 apiece.) It has a somewhat lower percentage of dark chocolate than my favorite brand, as well.

Like all of Newman's products, this is a perfectly fine product, and the charitable donation included with each purchase is always a winner.

I'll keep it short: I like chocolate, especially good chocolate.  While this bar may be organic, with great texture (not waxy), the flavor seems to have been left out.  It's labeled "dark chocolate", which it is, but it's also very, very bland.  I ate most of the bar, just broken into pieces, trying to decide if it's something I'd use for baking.  I wouldn't.  I'm not a big fan of Ghiradelli, but I'd use their chocolate in baking before I'd use this.  If you're looking for a mild dark chocolate bar with great texture, this is for you (not as bitter as Hershey's Dark).  But if you're looking for a good, strong-flavored, dark chocolate - keep looking.

This was pretty bad for dark chocolate or any other chocolate for that matter. The consistency was sort of like chalk, extremely crumbly and way too sweet/milky to have that great punch that dark chocolate has. I would like to say that the overwhelming sweetness was due to the lower cacao percentage that I like, this comes in at 54% where I prefer around 72% and up. But it is just way too sweet. I ended up breaking it up and making a small batch of muffins and not a soul noticed.

Overall, this is a nice chocolate bar with the benefit of being organic and rainforest certified. The chocolate dissolves quite smoothly and evenly - we compared it against a number of other dark chocolate bars we purchased from Trader Joe's and other places, and it dissolved more smoothly than any others. It isn't as bitter as many other dark chocolates, and hence, it may appeal to some people who don't really like other dark chocolates. The appearance of the bar was great - it had clean, dark surface, and there were no white blemishes or other marks that sometimes mar chocolate bars. The bar breaks with a nice "snap," and the aroma is quite nice. Overall, both my wife and I found the taste to be excellent.

On the downside, the bar has fewer cocoa solids than the other cocoa bars we tasted - 54% cocoa solids. Most of the others we sampled had 70%-80% cocoa solids - a couple were even higher. This _could_ be important to some health-concious consumers, because many studies examining the health benefits of dark chocolate have defined "dark" to mean 65+% cocoa content. That should be taken with a grain of salt, because some recent studies also have found merit to chocolates with lower cocoa content, but the majority of studies to date have focused on dark chocolate.

Another possible concern related to this chocolate could be the price. A twelve pack of bars comes in at $25,85 (possibly plus shipping); Trader Joe's has a number of bars that, although sometimes not as tasty, are certainly not as expensive.

In sum, for taste, aroma, and presentation, this is a really good chocolate bar. The negatives are price and a lower cocoa solid content.

I don't usually like anything other than milk chocolate. But I do know that the benefits of dark chocolate are good, so I thought I would give this a whirl and I'm really glad I did.

Much to my surprise I found this to be an altogether pleasant experience. This chocolate has a rich, creamy texture when allowed to melt slowly in your mouth. It also was wonderful just to down-right gobble, but I don't recommend it. (Gobbling that is) This product is just too good to gobble willy-nilly!

It had no unpleasant bitter aftertaste that I've come to expect with certain darker chocolates. I sometimes like my chocolate to be a bit on the softer side, so I also tried the candy a tiny bit melted and found that it was even better. There is no waxy taste to this bar and it melts well, it is rich, creamy and full bodied. And I had to really restrain myself from gobbling this up in one sitting.

I'm not one who likes European chocolates; I have a love of Hershey's and always will, so this product is right up my alley, and if I find myslef looking for something a little different...this will be it from now on.

This is nothing like the Newman's Own chocolate I've had in the past! I don't know if they are changing all their chocolate products, after trying this I hope they are!

Usually I'm not too crazy about dark chocolate & find that even the lesser percentage dark chocolates are still too strong for my liking. This simply is not the case with this Signature Series bar! It melts nicely in the mouth & isn't too bitter or too sweet. The flavor is very well balanced & very satisfying. After the first sniff & taste I thought I'd devour the entire bar; it was so good! However, I enjoyed about half the bar & was amazed that my chocolate craving was soothed!

Imagine that - chocolate left for another day!

Last, I'd like to mention the ingredients because to me they are very important. I would like to think that if you are considering Organic Chocolate, you care about the ingredients too.

A big problem I have with the majority of Organic chocolate is the soy lecithin. Ever notice that it's hardly ever organic? Soy is a huge crop & I believe something like 80% of of it is GMO! Big time Bad! Thankfully this bar is ALL Organic:
Organic evaporated cane juice, organic chocolate liquor, organic cocoa butter, organic soy lecithin, organic vanilla. The Cocoa butter is Rainforest Alliance Certified.

(A few Organic chocolate bars on the market contain NO soy lecithin! Even better!)

I really enjoyed the (alas, all too small) sample of Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate provided to me by the Amazon Vine Program. Make no mistake, it's a serious, rich, and elegant chocolate, perfect for those times when you want something better than the goodies on the rack next to the register at the supermarket. But more playful adjectives, like "yummy" and "scrumptious" also came to mind while enjoying it.

I don't eat many sweets and desserts these days, so when I do I make sure it's the good stuff. And this complex, nuanced (yes, yes-- and yummy, too) dark chocolate certainly qualifies. With this new addition to its product line, Newman's Own continues its reputation for delicious, healthful, and environmentally responsible food products.

I love dark chocolate , when I first started I wasn't picky, I always grab the Hershey special darks when they are on sale and stock up, have  tried a few expensive ones and found many to be to bitter for me. But I really like the newsman's own, I love it's organic, I try to eat organic when possible. This chocolate is not as sweet as the Hershey brand and I like it more, it tastes thick and delicious without to much sugar and yet not bitter, a winner in taste now if they could just work on the price.

"Silky" is the word I kept coming back to as I tried this chocolate. It's smooth, rich, and ... well, "silky" is just the right word. Everything about this chocolate is decadent, but also feel-good insofar as it bears the 'organic' and 'rainforest certified.' What does this mean in a practical sense to consumers? From the Newman's Own site: "The USDA Organic Seal assures that at least 95% of the ingredients are organically certified." and "The Rainforest Alliance Certified(tm) seal guarantees that the cocoa in our Signature Series was grown on farms that meet comprehensive standards for sustainable farming, protecting soil, waterways and wildlife habitat as well as the rights and welfare of workers, their families and communities."

Seals and certifications don't mean much in the mouth, however, and that's where this chocolate excels. It's rich without being excessively bitter. Smooth without lacking depth and substance. It's easy to eat (and that comes from someone who struggles with chocolate, at times), and it's a very accessible dark chocolate. A very adult alternative to the over-sweet milk chocolate one might find in a more pedestrian alternative.

I don't know how better to celebrate this product than to just list the ingredients: Organic Dark Chocolate (organic evaporated cane juice, organic chocolate liquor, organic cocoa butter, organic soy lecithin, and organic vanilla). This stuff is as feel-good as it is taste-good. Can't wait to try the other varieties.

Vine sent me this to review - I LOVE chocolate, especially dark chocolate so I was quite excited. Now if you order this product you will get a pack of 12 - I got 1 so my only option was to simply consume it. And I enjoyed that oh so much. It had a harder texture than your hershey's special dark, but had a very similar flavor and sweetness. It was very very tasty. I would have liked additional bars to try things like baking with to fill you in on things like does it melt well in chocolate chip cookies or to make chocolate covered strawberries... I will have to guess on this as I didn't have enough to do that experiment. Due to the harder nature of the chocolate I believe it would work well in cookies but not so much on strawberries.

I like the idea of my chocolate being organic - I like where Newman's is going with their product line... I hope that they keep the word "Organic" meaning something other than just another sales pitch tactic.

Anyway - if I'm in the market for Dark chocolate - I would pick this up without a second thought.

First of all, I love dark chocolates tried a wide variety of them.

For Dark chocolates to taste good - they typically need to made from the finest ingredients and manufacturing processes - else they are going to taste bitter and rough - leaving an unpleasant taste.

I had high expectations about Newman's own Organics, but utterly disappointment.

As you slip a square of the chocolate into your mouth - it feels smooth and good - .... When you are done with 3/4 of them, thats when you realize that there is something kind of an aftertaste/not so smooth taste about this. I do not get this feeling when I try a Lindt or dark chocolate truffles from Central Market/Whole foods.

Overall - they are made of pure organic ingredients - but for whatever reasons - the cocao/manufacturing ... - the taste did not go over well with me.
Good taste, but more sweet than I expected. Also, the texture could have been a little creamier.  But overall, it hit the chocolate spot.

Wish I could have rated this higher. I respect the Newmans and their philanthropy and appreciate the fact the product is premium organic ingredients. I was looking forward to trying this 54% chocolate bar.

I eat a little dark chocolate daily and found this was too sweet for my taste. (To be fair I have had the same problem occasionally with a couple of other brands I've tried over the years.)

I usually buy Green & Black's 85% Dark Chocolate or Endangered Species 72% Dark Chocolate. Someone who is used to milk chocolate might like the Newman bar better than I did.

As for comparing nutrition facts, all three bars use different portion sizes...so I didn't find it worth the effort. Newman's 2.25 oz. bar is considered a single serving. Green & Black's 3.5 oz bar is considered 2.5 servings, and Endangered Species 3 oz. bar is two servings.

I love chocolate and was really disappointed by the weak, almost non-existent chocolate taste of this bar. Since there are no milk solids in dark chocolate, it is supposed to provide a deeper pronounced chocolate flavor. However, this bar doesn't provide much in the way of chocolate flavor. There's no immense pleasure derived as the chocolate melts in your mouth which makes the bar not worthy of its caloric content.

Break off a piece and hold it against the roof of your mouth and run your tongue over the bottom of it. It feels sort of waxy, and it takes a bit of work before the chocolate flavor starts to come through, and when it does, it's nothing to really appreciate. Flat tasting is a good way to describe this bar.

I wouldn't buy this, and I don't recommend it.

I didn't get to each much of the bar I received, as my husband purloined most of it, sadly. But what I DID have was absolutely silky-smooth and delicious, without the harshness that some dark chocolates can have. (I'm actually more of a milk chocolate girl, but I LOVED this.)

My husband particularly liked it because he's very concerned about the ethics of cocoa plantations, so he felt like this was something he didn't have to feel guilty about eating. We'll definitely repurchase!

First off, I like dark chocolate, I really, really like dark chocolate and I also like the Newman's Own products/foundation. However, I did not like this one. In fact, I spit it out. I don't think I've ever done that before..
It is much closer in taste to a milk chocolate, but even at that lacked any real flavor. There was no depth to this at all, none. It was bland, yet too sweet for dark chocolate, lacking any real chocolate experience at all.
If you appreciate dark chocolate, I recommend you check out Chocolove products, or Endangered Species brand. I've never been disappointed in either of those brands.

I've tried my fair share of different milk & dark chocolate brands. In the end, there are two simple categories for me in the affordable chocolate range:

(1) Cheap, too much factory taste/feeling, not really worth the calories - Hershey's, etc.
(2) Memorable, usually more expensive but when you bite into it you agree it's worth it - Green & Black's, Lindt, etc.

I'll eat from either category depending on my budget and level of chocolate neediness. My impression of this Newman's Dark Chocolate is it is priced as if it belonged to category #2, but tastes more like it belongs in category #1 (I suppose high end of category #1). Still, I would skip the Newman's and buy something from category #1 to get something that tastes like category #1 and save some money.

Sorry, I know it's organic, I know it's Newman's Own, I know it comes in a wonderful expensive package and all... but I'd rather actually taste Cadbury dark chocolate, or the dark chocolate made at my local candy store.

Nice packaging, nice "real" cocoa flavor... but it doesn't make me want to eat more.

I'm not the chocolate connoisseur some are, but this didn't really get my motor goin'.

I generally like items from other Newman's product lines as they always seem to have a great, borderline decadent flavor.  So I was genuinely surprised at how disappointing this bar was.  I love dark chocolate and when given a choice will always choose it over milk chocolate, but I found this bar to be bitter, almost burnt tasting, and the texture was exceptionally gritty.  To be fair, dark chocolate isn't going to have the silky texture of milk chocolate, but that doesn't mean it should crumble in your mouth.  All in all a very disappointing experience.

Unlike the other members of my family, I'm not a chocoholic. I'm a take it or leave it consumer and in general, I go for the good stuff. This sample bar was my introduction to the Newman's Own Organic Chocolate line, and in order to get a variety of opinions, I shared this taste with several co-workers.

My immediate impression was that the bar had the nice, crisp snap of well-tempered chocolate, and also that it had a lovely texture, melting quickly and smoothly in my mouth. The "dark" chocolate bar has a slightly smoky flavor, but only 54% cocoa, which is less than what many may be looking for in a dark bar. (Newman's Own also has a super dark bar with 70% cocoa.) All of us felt that this bar was sweeter than we would have ideally preferred, more akin to bittersweet chocolate than a true dark chocolate. It was suggested, for that reason, that it might be a nice high-quality bar for baking--though as noted previously, it is not a standard baking bar size.

The other thing that all of us noticed was a very subtle orange note to the flavor, to the point that we searched the ingredients for an explanation. The ingredients of this organic bar are very simple and straightforward. In fact, there are only five, none of which would explain this undertone. And it wasn't a problem, overt, or unpleasant; it was simply commented upon. Further perusing the Newman's Own offerings, I see they produce a dark chocolate orange bar, and I have to suppose there is some minor cross "contamination" of the flavors. Mystery solved.

A quick survey among my cohort revealed that there was only one of us who really cared that the product was organic. Yeah, the rest of us are Philistines. Based on the high price point and the low percentage of cocoa, even though we'd enjoyed the treat, none of us was inclined to purchase the product again. Your mileage may vary.

I love dark chocolate so Newman's own naturallly appealed.  It has a clean taste, but lacks the depth and complexity tthat you expect from a premium dark chocolate.  I do like that it is not overly sweet -- know it would be great to bake with.

Chocolate is by definition a Good Thing, dark chocolate doubly so. And organic, Rainforest Alliance Certified dark chocolate? Very nice. It has a good flavor. At 54% cocoa, it's not nearly as dark as some of the other bars on the market, and so is rather smooth on the tongue (I will dispute that it's waxy as one reviewer reported.) It's true that it's not silky the way really fine chocolate is, but it doesn't purport to be. It's the sort of chocolate you could find at your local supermarket. High end there, but nowhere near the price or quality of a bar of Vosges organic dark chocolate. Nor should it be compared to something like Vosges or even Godiva. It's a good, affordable organic chocolate bar that has some good credentials in the environmental department.

The bar is smallish, but I also debate the assertion that it's too small to share with a friend. There are six good-size squares in this package, which are more than enough for two assuming that no one is being a glutton. (That said, I admit I ate the whole bar myself today, but if there'd been anyone else here I'd have shared.) Yeah, more is better when it comes to chocolate, but it's by no means necessary.

Enjoy this chocolate bar for what it is.

I am not a chocolate connoisseur but I occasionally buy a bar of Hershey's Special Dark to enjoy and this tasted very much the same.  For me, that's a good thing.  For a gourmet chocolate aficionado, maybe not so much.

first off, the size of the box this bar of chocolate arrived in was ridiculous. it could have fit at least 50 bars or more. c'mon, amazon, you can do better.

now to the real review, which i should qualify by saying i prefer my chocolate 70% dark. this is only 54%, which i failed to notice when i requested this vine product. that said, this tasted too much like milk chocolate. milk chocolate in a bland, mass-produced, thoughtless way. this is just boring chocolate. it's ersatz chocolate. basically, once you've gone dark, you can't go back. and this, for me, was back.

I love dark chocolate, so I was excited to try this Newman's Own Dark Chocolate bar. First, I was impressed that the bar, which is smaller than other specialty chocolate bars but still a generous six squares, is just a single serving size. At 330 calories, 22 grams of fat, and 28 grams of sugar, it is still an indulgent treat, but if you choose to share the bar (as I did), you can satisfy your sweet tooth without feeling too guilty about it.

I definitely enjoyed the taste of this bar as well; I found the chocolate to be rich and smooth. At 54% cocoa, it is definitely not as dark as many other dark chocolate offerings out there--in fact, I found the taste to be a bit sweeter, more reminiscent of semi-sweet chocolate than true dark chocolate. Although this was fine by me, some dark chocolate lovers may be disappointed. So, unless you need your dark chocolate to be of the extra-dark variety, I would definitely recommend this product.

If you are used to waxy mass-produced chocolate, Newman's Own Organics might take a little getting used to. This is the real deal, 100% premium organic dark chocolate. The texture is a bit different from the run of the mill waxy chocolate that most people are accustomed to, but the flavor is very good and the rich dark chocolate melts in your mouth! Ingredients are: "Organic Dark Chocolate (Organic Evaporated Cane Juice, Organic Cocoa Butter*, Organic Whole Milk Powder, Organic Chocolate Liquor, Organic Soy Lecithin, Organic Vanilla). *Rainforest Alliance Certified(Tm) Cocoa." I enjoyed this dark chocolate but not everyone may appreciate the texture. Give it a try and see what you think!

I found this bar rather lacking in chocolate flavor.  At 54%, it might be possible that I am used to a higher cocoa content (60%+).  While some other reviewers have mentioned the mouthfeel as "grainy", I found it more chalky.  It melted well in the mouth without any grainy feel, but when chewed, became a rather gummy mass of chocolate.  It wasn't awful by any stretch of the imagination, but it was a little strange.  If you don't like dark chocolate, you would probably enjoy this bar--it seemed more like semi-sweet chocolate to me.  If you like dark chocolate, however, prepare for disappointment.

When reviewing one of the Newman's Own products, it's always tempting to let one's opinion of the goals of the organization temper one's review of the product. I try to avoid that as I figure that the reader can decide those issues and is reading this to see what a reviewer thinks of this particular product.

I like this product, but got it to try as part of the Vine review program and I don't know that I'd actually buy it because there's no price info available yet, so you can't compare it.

On the upside, I like the taste. Until the last few years, a 54% chocolate was considered 'dark' and I like dark chocolate of about this percentage (up to about 60%). I think it's robustly chocolate, without the bitterness of the extremely high chocolate you see these days. This bar seems a nice balance of chocolate and sweet.

One the downside, I find it just a bit on the grainy side. It's subtle, and didn't stop my enjoying it, but I noticed it compared to other high-end brands of chocolate bars. It's just not as smooth.

Would I buy this compared to others? It's hard to tell without being able to price compare, but given that I don't consume enough chocolate for the price to really matter, probably not.

Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar, 2.25 oz.

I'm a firm believer in the Newman's Own corporate objectives and enjoy many of their fine products. I appreciate the facts that this chocolate, according to them, "is formulated with some of the finest Certified Organic chocolate we've ever tasted, made from cocoa beans grown on Rainforest Alliance Certified(tm) farms." While the New Organics Dark Chocolate is very good, it has a slightly grainy texture which, for me, spoils the mouth-feel a little. A small point, I suppose, as it is excellent chocolate with a 54% cocoa content. I certainly recommend it for its rich chocolate aroma and taste.

Wow! As with virtually all Newman's Own products, this is the best. I've tried just about every brand, including a number of organic chocolates, and this beats them all. Naturally, such and assessment is subjective, but I'd suggest that in a blind tasting (i.e., without the suggestion of a brand name), Newman's Own chocolate would always be at or near the top of every list. Do yourself a favor and get some--it's good for you, too! You won't regret it.

I love dark chocolate, but I found this bar too bland for my tastes. It has one note of flavor and not very interesting. Funny thing is, when I handed the remaining squares out, everyone who usually only liked milk chocolate loved this bar. So if you like milk chocolate, but would like the benefits of dark chocolate, this may be the perfect compromise. However, if you like the bracing complexity of dark chocolate, you may find yourself giving this chocolate away.

I usually really like Newman products and like supporting their business, this is the first item I will not be repurchasing.

NOTE: The bars are as tall as an iPhone and a little wider than one -- just a heads up if you think this is a large bar, it is not. You will want to note the weight of the bars if using for a recipe.

So, I'm a guy. I like chocolate, sure, but I am not into dark chocolates. I even used to date a chick who was into wine and tried to get me into the whole dark-chocolate-with-wine thing, which I never got. I got into wine, sure, but dark chocolate was never anything I really cared for.
So when I got this, it was with much hesitation. I don't even LIKE dark chocolate, why on earth would I want this?
-
I cannot explain what this bar did to me. I took a small bite and was hooked! It's just wonderful. How do I describe this - it was ultra smooth without any of that bitterness which I detest in dark chocolate - not even a hint! It was pure excellence. I did see other people here mentioned that it seemed "grainy" and I can say I felt none of that. I thought it was gorgeous. I literally could not stop eating it. And that never happens - I am very much into food but it's rare that anything grabs me like that. I did put it down halfway through - and I was transformed from a guy who hates dark chocolate to a guy who now knows what real dark chocolate is. I put it down because I was on my way out the door - but you can bet that as soon as I got home, I ate the rest. It was just so fine. I would absolutely get this again, and I look forward to a time when I can buy this for someone else, so they too, can experience the luxury of this fine dark chocolate.

Its hard to describe taste especially since I'm not a connoisseur of chocolate but of the brands that I have tasted, this one sits in the middle for me, not of the highest taste pleasure sensation but a great deal better then others I've tried.  I love the Newman's Own Brand and every product I've tried from this brand has been excellent.  I think this one might be best used for baking rather than eating straight out of the package.

I'm a big fan of chocolate and of Newman's Own products, so I was very excited to try their chocolate. This bar is 54% cocoa, which I consider somewhere between milk and dark chocolate (but more towards dark), and this is right in my personal sweet spot. This is high quality chocolate with a complex flavor, but it was not as smooth as I usually like. My favorite chocolate, the Scharffen Berger 41% extra rich milk, is obviously much more of a milk chocolate bar, but I have had 60% cocoa chocolate that was smoother than this 54% chocolate. I do recommend that you try this chocolate because I think it would appeal to many chocolate lovers.

There is a immediate taste corresponding to the chocolate content. Although my preference is for chocolates with a bit higher content--60% or more--it is close enough. It is rich with some sharpness, but does _not_ have a "burnt" taste that several other brands have. It melts nicely in the mouth to a smooth texture, without becoming overly buttery. And it has a good aftertaste.

I've always been a fan of Newman's Own products and this dark chocolate bar did not dissapoint. I like my dark chocolate bars to have a bit more cocoa (70% at least) but for those who shy away from the bitter flavor, this bar offers a good balance with a hint of sweetness the higher cocoa bars lack. You won't mistake this for a Hershey bar by any means. The product is certified organic and uses Rainforest Alliance Certified cocoa so you can feel good about what you are eating. A great bar at a very reasonable price that holds its own against the more expensive offerings from Europe.

NOTE: Guest review from my chocolate-loving friend LW:

I almost missed the 2.25 oz. bar at first, wedged as it was, in its brown and black wrapper, alongside the inflated-to-full-size plastic air cushion in its Amazon book box. But once I'd extricated it and opened it, it was substantial. All 22 grams of fat (13 saturated) of it. Sorry, I looked. But not to worry -- that's for the whole bar. With a modicum of discipline, you can easily spread that shame across six nights by breaking off one generous carefully scored square each night (bigger squares than the one on your hotel pillow). That's all you need at a go anyway -- the taste is very rich with a subtle liqueur-like finish -- just what you'd hope its 54% cocoa content would deliver.

[Bar provided as part of Vine review program might have been smaller than bars available here for sale.]
I usually am a fan of Newman's products, but this chocolate left me cold.  Just didn't taste creamy or chocolatly. Sort of tasted chalky.  Ick

I am a chocolate lover and it was the first time I tried an organic dark chocolate. It tastes alright but it does not seem to have the same smoothness and bitter taste which come with the typical dark chocolate.  It is also a little pricey for over $2 dollars a pack. I would prefer the Ghirardelli Dark Chocolate over this.

This is one great dark chocolate bar!  It is organic and when comparing this to a nestle special dark I can definitely tell the difference.  The Hershey's tastes more sugary and artificial.  While this chocolate bar isn't cheap it does taste great!

I admit that I am not a big dark chocolate fan. I first noticed that the chocolate does not have that sharp bitter taste that most dark chocolate has. Then again, it doesn't really have any taste. By the time I was done eating the chocolate bar, I kind of felt like I ate some wax. From there it did not agree with my system. It might be organic and dark chocolate, but give me a Hershey's bar any day.

Shawn Kovacich
Author of the Achieving Kicking Excellence book and DVD series.

I didn't find anything remarkable about this candy. It's not more tasty, it isn't smoother, and it generally just isn't any better than other dark chocolates. I passed bites around to my office mates and everyone came back with the same reaction. Newman's brand is known for being a cut above everyone else; this isn't anything to write home about.

I do appreciate the environmental aspect, though.

Not smooth enough or distinctive enough in flavor to compare to many high-end chocolates and with more chalkiness/waxiness than I expected, this simply was not a big enough step up from mass-market semi-sweet chocolate to be that interesting to me as a purchase in the future, even after getting this (single-bar, not pack of 12) free taste test from Amazon's Vine Reviewer program.  Not terrible, just underwhelming.

I must admit that I have never eaten an organic chocolate bar so I was excited to taste Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar.  Unfortunately, I found the taste to be bland.  The texture is nice and I liked that it didn't melt in my hand while I was eating it but this bar has the distinction of being the first chocolate bar to enter my house and not get completely eaten.  Newman's Own is a fantastic organization that donates generously to charity so I feel guilty saying this but I would not purchase or eat this chocolate bar on my own.

This is so dark it smells and tastes like baking chocolate. When it melts in your mouth it is smooth and creamy.

Organic Dark Chocolate (Organic evaporated cane juice, organic chocolate liqour*, organic cocoa butter*, organic soy lecithin [an emulsifier], organic vanilla).
*Rainforest Alliance Certified Cocoa.

The flavor of this chocolate reminds me of Hershey's Special Dark from several years ago (the classic formula), only considerably milder. And it's not just me; the first reaction of those who I shared it with was, where's the flavor? The most charitable adjective I can think of is 'inoffensive', but that's not a good thing. Not something I would ever seek out again. Forgettable.

Received only (1) - 2.5 oz dark chocolate bar,and we were expecting (12 bars) as stated in advertisement, so that was a disappointment to start with.  My husband and I shared the 2.5 oz bar, and we both felt that the quality was just average.  It was good, not too bitter, but not the best dark chocolate I've taste either. Based on the price, we would probably not purchase these in the future, as there are cheaper choices that are of the same quality, in my opinion.

In the last year or so I've really developed a taste for dark chocolate. I've liked dark chocolate for years but I started eating a bit more recently. I've tried several different brands from the store. All were at least good with some being a little better than others.

So. While not scientific my personal taste experience says this dark chocolate bar taste terrible.

If you are looking for that silky smooth deep rich dark chocolate flavor that sort of infuses your whole body starting with the tongue and culminating in a very pleasing feeling in your nogging look elsewhere. My God.

On the other hand, if you are really into organics and go out of your way to eat all things organic then perhaps this is your chocolate bar. 54% is not a very dark bar and I think it shows in the taste of this bar. The taste could also be due to the organic nature of the bar. That being the case, if you prefer that organic experience, that taste that organics typically have I don't think you'll be disappointed.

For everyone else, the flavor is off with strange undertones. Not inedible just not very tasty.

The bars are fairly small at 2.25 ounces. That isn't really a knock since moderation in all things is a good habit.
This is a delicious chocolate bar.  But for the additional cost, I was expecting something extra special.  It tastes no better than a standard Hersey bar and has a very slightly rubbery texture.

With all the organic, single-origin, Fair Trade, 80% + dark chocolates available even in discount stores, I am not quite sure why Newman's Own brand wanted to get in the chocolate business. Anyway, this is a very light-weight entry into the fray, and at only 54% pure chocolate (in the Vine sample I received, anyway), a quite weak entry at that. It tasted okay, but definitely too sweet and lacking the earthy bitter-sweet taste of the more cacao bean-heavy chocolates available. Not much different than a decent Hershey dark chocolate bar, and likely much more expensive.

I was excited to try this chocolate as I'm such a fan of Newman's Own products in general.  It was good, but I found it a little disappointing.  It has a rich chocolate taste, but the texture is a bit too dry for just eating (which is what I intended to do with it).  It might work well for baking, but I haven't tried that yet...probably would work to chop up in pieces for cookies.

I really don't know what else to say except that it's moderate - not too bitter, not too sweet. The texture is not rich or exceptional in any way. It seems to be just a conglomeration of the ingredients listed on the package, so I would choose (or not) to get it based on whether you like that list.

I am not a big fan of dark chocolates (Milk Chocolates for the win!), but these tasted surprisingly milky. For the price Amazon is selling them though, I would definitely suggest you to stick to your convenient stores' Hershey bars.

Newman's Own is my favorite brand and I try all of their products.  However, this one is a failure.  The bar is bland and I guess 54% cocoa is not enough.  I am sure as chocolate bars go, this is nutritious, but frankly, it is hard to find a nutritious chocolate bar.  If you want nutrition it would be best to go and  get an apple.  When I want chocolate, nutrition is not even on my mind.  Decadence is.  This bar is not decadent enough.  Keep looking.
Newman's Own organic chocolate is pretty good. It may have a little waxy taste than other dark chocolates, but it has a nice consistency.

As a true connoisseur of chocolate, I was interested in this new dark chocolate bar from Newman's. In truth I've always thought the Newman chocolate bars to be overly sweet and not particularly rich tasting. I thought from the hype that this new line of products would be different but I sad to report that is simply not the case here. In fact these new gourmet bars taste much the same as the standard line of Newman's own chocolates. There is still the problem of being overly sweet and considering how dark these are supposed to be, they don't have that deep rich dark chocolate flavor and texture that I am always looking for.

n summary I just want to be clear and say that if you are looking for that killer concentrated rich dark chocolate flavor I'm sorry to report that you won't find it here.

The newmans own organic chocolate was very good. Although it is dark chocolate, it had a rather milk chocolate smoothness and flavor to it. If you are a fan of Dark Chocolates on the bitter end of the spectrum then you would not care for this chocolate necessarily.

Overall, I felt that the quality was very good, it was pleasant to eat. It had, perhaps, a slight aftertaste that reminded me of oranges.

Good stuff, if you like mild dark chocolate, you wont be disappointed.

I am a big fan of Newman's Own Dark Chocolates. I've tried all the "percentages" of dark chocolate, and this is another good one. I like the texture of the chocolate: solid, but still creamy--and NOT crumbly (which I hate). The chocolate is mild, yet very flavorful and without any bitterness. Another solid chocolate bar from Newman's Own!

Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar has a good mouth feel, a rich flavor, and just enough sweetness to eat on its own or to use as part of a snack. It's perfect for pain au chocolat, where a lesser chocolate would not be sufficient for such simple treatment.

The taste is chocolate, pure and simple: very pure, and very simple. Try it alongside your current favorite; it should hold its own.

I love dark chocolate but sometimes the bitterness is a bit much. Newman's Own had a nice balance and flavor. I love the Newman's Own brand and their commitment to raising money for charity and using Organic ingredients. I'll happily be buying this product again. Highly recommended!

Great tasting dark chocolate bar by Newman's Own.  Paul Newman's company generally makes good food with natural ingredients and this tastes like another winner.  A nice, soft sweetness with no indication of bitterness, Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar doesn't taste like the typical store bought, processed dark chocolate bar.  Fresh tasting with real chocolate/cocoa and is very satisfying for a bar its size.

I was intrigued by the tide of enthusiasm surrounding dark chocolate. Apparently, chocolate can be healthy. Well, it can also taste terrible too. Those high cacao bars from far off lands my qualify as health food but they tasted like dirt.

This new bar from Newman's Own is a different story. It smooth but not overly creamy. Sweet but not cloyingly so. This is a really tasty dark chocolate bar. Much better than Hershey's or the stuff you find at the exotic farmer's market.

I'd suspect most people who try this will like it, at least enough to finish a bar. I prefer dark chocolate, typically with a higher % rating then this has but hey chocolate is chocolate so I wasn't going to turn down trying it. It reminded me far more of a bittersweet (think chocolate chip) then of my typical dark chocolate bars. It wasn't bad by any means but it didn't stand out as amazing either. It's obviously worlds above your typical "candy isle" bar but I wouldn't pick it out when compared to other organic dark chocolate options at a specialty market. For those interested in moving into dark chocolate for health benefits this might be a good transition bar into those with a higher % if you're used to milk chocolates.

This is an acceptable chocolate bar, but probably not worth what they're charging for it.  It's pretty mild on the dark chocolate scale and has a slightly odd texture--definitely not melt in your mouth.  I wound up using most of my trial bar to make hot chocolate, and it served that purpose quite well--better than eating it out of hand.

I am a fan of dark chocolate, but I find some of the 70% and up bars to be bitter. The Newman's Own bar has 54% cocoa. It has a strong chocolate flavor without being bitter or harsh.

One 2.25-ounce bar has 330 calories. The flavor is rich enough that when I need a chocolate fix all I need is one square (1/6 of the bar). That's just 55 calories so it makes a satisfying treat without busting my diet.

The texture is smooth and somewhat creamy, although not as creamy as Dove dark chocolate (for whatever that is worth).

I would definitely purchase Newman's Own chocolate bars again.

Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar is much more like milk chocolate than dark chocolate, rather sweet and somewhat milky for a dark chocolate, though it contains no milk. In fact, "organic evaporated cane juice", better known simply as sugar, is listed as the primary ingredient by weight.

There are no unusual or notable flavors detectable other than chocolate and a hint of vanilla but the ingredients taste fresh. The tablet is not too thick nor is it too thin.

Overall, a good but not notable and rather nondescript 54% cocoa bar for people who enjoy a higher cocoa content than milk chocolate but who don't like the taste of 70%+ dark chocolate.

Each 2.25 oz. bar has 330 calories including 200 from fat.

This "second generation" of Newman's Own is dedicated to producing products that are certified organic by Oregon Tilth.  (The "first generation" company gives all of its after-tax profits to charities.)  But in both cases, these two companies produce high-quality foods that are usually the best in class on the store shelves.  This NEWMAN'S OWN ORGANICS DARK CHOCOLATE BAR is no exception.  Pricey, yes.  Tasty, very.  The taste is, in fact, a smooth, semi-sweet dark cocoa flavor, with no acidity,  but with a slight roasted-coffee after finish.  This is not an afternoon pick-me-up candy bar.  This an after dinner treat to be shared with a cup of coffee.

Really, the title of my review *is* my review.

I'm a fan of dark chocolate. I like dark chocolate with a bit of bite to it: slight acidity and slightly bitter. With that as the yardstick, Newman's Own 54% Dark is somewhere between dark and milk chocolate.

But oddly enough, I really like this chocolate. It has a REAL chocolate flavor without being too "earthy", but isn't as smooth and tame as milk chocolate.

A small piece works really well with dried fruit or peanut butter as a small but satisfying snack.

Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar is a must for any lover of dark chocolate.  I really enjoyed the strong taste of the dark chocolate.  The not-as-sweet-as milk chocolate taste was to die for.  Not a lot of people really appreciate the taste of dark chocolate and those that do will definitely want to try this newest product from the Newman line.  Over the weekend I bought a carton of Newman's Virgin Lemonade (no HFCS) and it was delicious.  So if you feel that you're a connoisseur of chocolate then you'll want to buy a bar of Newman's Own Organic Dark Chocolate today.

Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar is a pretty good chocolate bar that has more going for it than just taste. First, it's USDA certified organic. I try to use organic products as much as possible, particularly on less costly products and those where organic matters. Second, the product is Rainforest Alliance Certified cacao. So the cacao is produced using sustainable growing techniques. These are the things about the product that I like best. And sometimes, it's these factors that make the difference between buying product A or B.

As far as the taste ... well, it is not the best chocolate bar I have ever tried, nor is it the worst. First, the bar is about 7 mm thick ... moderately chunky as bars go. There is a classy-looking N emblem embossed in each piece. The nutritional panel says that one bar is a serving, but that one serving is going to provide about 330 calories ... actually 1/3 of a bar is a serving for me. The chocolate is not very melty. This is more common in higher cacao content chocolate bars; Newman's Own bar is about 54% cacao, so I was a little surprised. The bar was also a little sweeter than I expected. The chocolate was not unpleasant, but it just seemed to lack a "smack your face" slap of chocolate flavor that you expect in good dark chocolate.

So, bottom line time: Newman's own is a decent but unremarkable chocolate bar. It's organic and Rainforest-friendly, and earns the product bonus points in my book.

I eat all types of chocolate, from the cheapest to the most expensive I get as gifts. Dark chocolate is my favorite. Recent medical studies are now showing dark chocolate can help prevent heart attacks and strokes, and help keep those individuals who have already had heart attacks from an earlier death. It also is suppose to make you happy, although I think that theory is being debated.

Dark chocolate definitely makes me happy! I wish I had a whole crate of Newman's dark chocolate bars. It has a nice sweet taste, without tasting like milk chocolate. (Not that I have anything whatsoever against milk chocolate.) It also does not leave a bad acid aftereffect as some chocolate bars do. And if you only eat a small amount a day, there will be no bad weight aftereffect, either.

I have not yet experienced a strikeout amongst the Newman's Own line of products, and this is no exception. Smooth, delightful, with just the right balance of bitter and sweet, this is the perfect capper to a light dinner or late coffee...or even just as a quick boost or snack. It was difficult to do, but I rationed myself to one small piece a night until it was gone. And when it was gone, I immediately went and bought another one. And of course, charity benefits from the profits.

I'm a big fan of Newman's and wish I could say this is the very best of the best...but...It is very good and I could eat a truck load of it but I compared it side by side with my Hersheys dark chocolate and I'd have to give a bit of an edge to the Hersheys'..  I can't say anything bad about it but  it's not quite there for me...Perhaps you'll disagree????

Newman's Own is not known as a chocolate brand. They make organic stuff like lemonade and pizza, so I was a bit skeptical.

What I really like about this chocolate bar is its balance: it is not as silky smooth as a Lindt or Dove, it is not as bitter as you would expect from a 56% cacao bar. It is dark but not too dark, Sweet but not too sweet. Smooth but not too velvety. I could not help but finish the entire bar in one sitting.

I prefer dark chocolate to milk, but I do eat both. I shared this bar with my kids: a daughter who loves dark chocolate and my some who will only eat milk chocolate.

Me: I do not consider 54% cacao to be dark chocolate, that's a bit of a mislabel. The flavor was very bland. I'm glad it's organic and all that, but if it doesn't taste that great, why buy it?

My daughter: Kinda waxy, like a Hershey bar, and it's too sweet. This bar is about the same size as a Hershey bar too.

My son: I'd rather have a Hershey bar, this is too dry.

I am surprised to see so many strong negative reviews for "Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar". Personally, I find the taste to be delicious; it (the taste) is rich in chocolate flavor, while also avoiding the overly-sweet sugar taste that is common with lower-end chocolate confections. "Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar" also manages to minimize the bitter taste that is common for dark chocolate, which is a huge plus for me, considering that I am not a big fan of dark chocolate in the first place.

In all, highly recommended.

As a fan of chocolate I couldn't miss the opportunity to taste test Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate.  Probably the only drawback was that I was going to have to share some with my wife.  The chocolate doesn't have a strong aroma when you open the package, but the taste is excellent.  The chocolate breaks nicely, doesn't crumble.  It isn't waxy and has a great feel in the mouth, very creamy.  While it has a good taste, the chocolate doesn't overwhelm your taste buds.  I was a little disappointed in the "finish" - there wasn't a long lasting flavor in the chocolate, and that, perhaps is the one drawback I had from eating the chocolate.

I really didn't think that this dark chocolate could be that much different than any of the other fine dark chocolates I've had recently.  How could it seriously compare to La Maison du Chocolat, at ten bucks a bar?  But I have to say, it is, and it does...  in a very good way!  In particular, my wife LOVES this chocolate, and usually she eats just milk chocolate.  But it still tastes like dark chocolate.

The package was a lot smaller than I expected, but I'm a nut for dark chocolate. This particular bar tastes great, and I kept wanting more than the wrapper could hold.

Very much recommended, and this is coming from someone who is a dark chocolate fiend, but also very particular about the nuanced taste in each variation.

I love dark chocolate; I vastly prefer it over the overly-sweet milk chocolate, so when I saw this organic dark chocolate, I knew I had to try it.

It's delicious! I will admit that I like my dark chocolate somewhat bitter, and this isn't terribly bitter the way some darks can be. However it does have a unique, somewhat "earthy" taste that is all its own. I ate my test bar in three different sittings in order to gauge its taste in three ways:

1. With coffee... after a bitter cup of coffee, this chocolate is just sinfully delicious!

2. After Italian food... after some garlic, again, this stuff is just sinfully delicious!

3. After some chocolate ice cream... after this, the dark chocolate did have a less sugary taste, and "seemed" more bitter just because of that difference. Again, it really hit the spot here too.

Overall I will definitely be trying some more of this. It is REALLY good stuff!

I let the bar sit on the counter for a couple of days after it was delivered (Vine Program) I split the bar with my 17 year old daughter and she agreed with my assessment. The bar had good dark chocolate taste, typical aftertaste, a bit of grit (not a bad thing)and generally an excellent experience. The difference between this bar and most other dark chocolates I have tried was how creamy the texture was as I was chewing it. Reminded me more of a Hershey's bar in consistency... Perusing other folks' reviews, I saw several mentions of the taste being bitter. Assuming that folks weren't eating these right after dinner - I am wondering if there are any issues with quality control - since I only had the one bar to try, that is only a thought!!!

All in all... I thought the bar was excellent, uniquely creamy and soft versus my normal dark chocolate bars, and left me wanting more. With the varied reviews, I will probably pick a bar or two up at the store and try again before buying 12 packs...

All the best,

Jay

There are so many dark chocolate bars out these days from all over the world. Many claim to be delicious as well as healthy. Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar seems worthy of praise even though the percent of dark chocolate is somewhat low compared to others. However, it has a creaminess and flavor that are above some dark bars.

The waxiness of some chocolate bars is overly apparent, but Newman's is soft without the waxy feel. It melts nicely in your mouth and because it's organic, it makes you feel like you're eating something that may be good for you. People worry about additives, pesticides, etc. and this product, being organic, seems to avoid all the bad stuff. Of course, it is a bit higher in fat than most dark chocolate bars, but if you don't mind that, the taste is good.

The size of the bar is a bit small, 2.25 ounce, the price is about the same for other similar products. On the other hand, a smaller bar is probably better than buying a large size one and devouring all of it. I think it's a delicious tasting dark chocolate and I would probably buy it again.

We love dark chocolate here so we waited eagerly to try the Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar.  It was something of a disappointment:  kind of waxy, too sweet, and the intense flavor of really good dark chocolate was missing.  You can really tell how good something is around here by how long it lasts -- and we still have about 1/3 of the bar left after about two weeks.  I'd skip the chocolate bar, but the Newman's Own "oreo" cookies are fabulous.

MMMM chocolate. Can you ever actually give a bad review of chocolate? In my opinion, no. Even bad chocolate is still pretty good, because, well, it's chocolate. However, this chocolate was exceptionally good.

Consistent with the Newman branding, this product is organic and takes into consider the impact it's purchases make by using cocoa purchases certified by the Rainforest Alliance.

This dark chocolate, made with real sugar, was slightly sweeter than I expected, but still had a rich depth to it. Although it was 54% cocoa, it tasted like more. Honestly, I've had better, but considering that this is both organic and sustainably produced some sacrifices have to be made. This is a high fat and high calorie product, so be careful not to eat too much. This probably comes partially from their use of whole milk but the percent of milk and chocolate liquor weren't specified so it's unclear what the technical classification of this product should be: dark chocolate or milk chocolate.

Overall a tasty treat that is great choice for those concerned about organic and sustainable products. If health or taste are your primary concern, you'll find better choices elsewhere.

We love lots of different Newman's Own products, and have been devotees of Sockarooni pasta sauce and the mint chocolate chip cookies and the Caesar dressing for years. So we had high hopes for this chocolate. But sadly, those hopes were not fulfilled. The chocolate is good, not overly sweet, but just does not seem to rise to premium grade. The mouth feel was not as silky or smooth as we would like, and frankly a bit waxy. And there was something just not very distinctive to the chocolatiness of it all.

I'm a chocolate lover and I passionately dislike "Hershey's" kind of fake Chocolate.
I usually eat 70% and above dark chocolate, but my daughter doesn't like sour taste of very dark chocolate. She really likes this Newman's Own 54%.

I think it has OK taste. I don't love it, but I don't dislike it either.
I'd recommend this to someone who doesn't like milk chocolate so much, but don't like very dark chocolate either. It's a good "between" chocolate.

Maybe it's because it was the end of a long day and I was hungry, but this is easily some of the best dark chocolate I've tried (and some of the best chocolate period)!

I had some Rocky Mountain Chocolate and Russel Stover's truffles leftover from Valentine's day, and after eating those, I found myself wanting more of the Newman's Own stuff!

I am a fan of the Newman's Own company, and its philanthropic mission. Some of their products are quite good, such as their spaghetti sauce and oreo-type cookies. This chocolate bar was not quite what I anticipated - sweeter and more buttery than I expect from a premium dark chocolate bar. The flavor does not linger on the palate and each square seems "over" far too soon.  Still, one thing I've learned from reading and writing reviews on Amazon is that there's an enthusiastic audience for just about anything, so I'm sure other folks will enjoy this more than I did.  Still, I think Newman's would do well to butch this bar up a bit, and let those with sweet tooths go for their milk chocolate instead.  Each to their own, I suppose.

Let me preface my review with this confession: I'm a chocoholic. There's no such thing as "too rich" or "too much chocolate" or "too decadent." I love me some chocolate goodness. Milk chocolate, dark chocolate...not so much white chocolate and none of the fruit flavored chocolate. My personal favorite is dark chocolate, but not that too dark chocolate that seems to be popular lately. Now on with the review...

I'm a huge fan of the Newman's Own brand and have a complete appreciation for organic products. I had very high hopes for this chocolate bar. Unfortunately I was a bit disappointed on several levels. I found the chocolate to be drier than what my palate prefers, resulting in chocolate crumbles when I break off the pieces. I don't like when chocolate (even the crumbles) goes to waste. After all, any chocolate is good chocolate.

I could tell, however, that the flavor of this chocolate was very pure. It didn't have that "additive" flavor to it that some chocolate brands have.

My last beef with Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate bar is that the squares are too big and don't break off easily. I like bars that have smaller squares/rectangles to break off. Because of the dry nature of the chocolate, there was never a clean break on the pieces. It's a small, nitpicky thing, I know, but still something that matters to me when selecting a chocolate bar.

And what made me ultimately give this chocolate only 3 stars was that after I broke off a few pieces and tucked the rest back in my purse, I COMPLETELY forgot I had any leftover. This never happens to me. I always break off a piece, and then save some for "later." Later meaning about 3 minutes. Newman's Own Organics Dark Chocolate Bar had me forgetting I even had any accessible chocolate for several DAYS until I happened to spot it in my purse again. That should tell you something.

I love chocolate, and indulge in it regularly. When I buy bar chocolate, I always buy dark. Now I don't go crazy and get the 85 or even 90% cocoa, but usually anywhere from 50-70ish% is great. Normally I love Newman's Own products, from their salad dressings, to lemonade, and even my dogs like the dog snacks. However, this chocolate falls short.

It's VERY sweet, much sweeter than regular dark chocolate. I found the texture a little lacking, also-- somewhat crumbly and unappealing. (It brings to mind the episode of "Friends" when Monica had to work with a product called "Mockolate" and she said she loved the way it crumbled in her mouth.) I have to admit I was expecting a little more from this brand, and am let down.

I'm not a fan, and don't see myself finishing the bar. I might just give it to someone who enjoys milk chocolate.

You call this dark?!

I love dark chocolate--the darker, the better: anything in the 80%+ cacao range is just dandy, as far as I'm concerned. Admittedly, it should have been obvious from the 54% designation on the wrapper that this was in another category altogether--call it "dark chocolate lite," for people who would really rather just have a Hershey bar. But I guess I had hoped that the fact that it was organic and fair-traded would somehow make up for the missing cacao. In general, I really support what Newman's Own is trying to accomplish.

Alas, it was not to be. My main objection is that it tastes mass produced, like a so-called high-end chocolate bar you'd buy in a supermarket but that really is just a run-of-the-mill bar imported from Europe. In particular, there's a subtle but annoying undertaste that I don't detect in the other dark chocolate bars I'm fond of. I don't know if it's the soy lecithin or something related to how it's processed--there really are very few ingredients, which is good--but each bite has elicited nothing more than "eh" from me. I shared some of it with a chocoholic friend who also has a fondness for the really dark stuff, and her reaction was the same as mine.

As a taste test, I bought one of Newman's Own's 70% cacao bars, which was the darkest I could find in that line in my local health food store, and it was somewhat better--at least the undertaste was missing. But it too falls short of what I seek in my empty calories, so I won't be buying any more of these, at least not until I see cacao content of 80%+.

If you enjoy very dark chocolate, try Equal Exchange's 80% (lovely texture), Endangered Species 88% (with the black panther on the wrapper) or Valrhona's 85%. There's really no comparison.

Two stars for an organic, fair-traded but otherwise insipid product.

In terms of the chocolate spectrum, I usually fall between dark milk and dark chocolate. This bar was good, but fell a bit too far on the dark side for me. It has a very rich dark chocolate flavor. It's good, but was a bit much for my taste buds. It's probably best eaten in smaller doses.

Newman's Own dark chocolate is labeled as 54% cocoa. This percentage indicates how much of the natural cocoa butter and cacao solids are in the chocolate bar. Lighter chocolates typically contain more milk and sugar (and/or other ingredients) by weight. The higher the percentage of cacao in a chocolate bar, the darker and more bitter the chocolate becomes.

At 54%, I'd have to rate this as a medium dark chocolate. I've eaten 70% chocolate and I think it's just too bitter for eating out of hand. This Newman's dark chocolate strikes a nice balance: it's dark enough to get some of the health benefits from the flavonoid content of dark chocolate without having the bitter flavor. But it's not sickly sweet like some cheap national brands of chocolate. I like that the ingredients are organic so I can avoid artificial flavors, high-fructose corn syrup, and the other icky ingredients some brands add to their products. Newman's has a nice flavor and doesn't leave a bitter aftertaste. It's got a rich mouthfeel without being too heavy and doesn't leave my teeth feeling fuzzy.

The nutrition facts show 330 calories for the entire bar, but the bar is divided into six segments so you can easily break off a piece and only consume 55 calories at a time. I'm not into eating huge bars in one gulp, so I appreciate this. The chocolate makes a nice after-dinner treat with coffee.

Not a bad candybar it tastes just fine, but I won't be giving up Hershey's or even Cadbury's Dark chocolate bars anytime soon.

What you are really paying for is the name & the opportunity to be politically correct. The candybar itself is half the size and more than twice the price of other dark choclate bars that are so similar in taste that the real bitter after-taste will be in your wallet. I would be more inclined to eat this more often if the pricing were more reasonable. Even if you are trying to do the right thing ecologically all the more reason you should not be punished by paying more for it.

If you like dark chocolate this is good, but I find it no better than any other dark chocolate so I would go more with price. This is organic though so it does command a higher price, I prefer organics but I also have to watch the budget too. If you have the extra money, you won't go wrong buying this.

As product lines go, Newman's is tough to beat. Organic, all natural, and money goes to charity. What's not to like?

For this product, however, it's a swing and a foul ball. It's not a miss. The 50+% cacao stands out, with rich dark chocolate flavor similar to other bars. However, the mouthfeel and texture of this bar is all wrong. It's not creamy in the way chocolate should be, instead it leaves a thick coating on the inside of the mouth that is both unpleasant and ruins the flavor. I'm not certain what it is, but perhaps the type of fat or the fat content they used doesn't mesh with the chocolate bar. I found it rather unenjoyable to eat the entire thing.

I like a little taste of dark chocolate as a sweet treat, that isn't quite as unhealthful as, say, a Hershey's bar... Newman's gets the balance just right for my taste.  It's dark not milk chocolate which I gather is somewhat better for you.  But its not disgustingly bitter tasting to the point that you don't feel like you're eating chocolate at all like some dark chocolates taste -- it still tastes pretty much like a good old chocolate bar (maybe slightly more "dark" / bitter).

I'm a big fan of organics as well as dark chocolate. When the Newman's Own Dark Chocolate bar arrived, I was going to pace myself and have just a little and save some for the next day. Ha! After I took the first bite, that wasn't going to happen. This chocolate, unlike other dark chocolates I've tried, was creamy and totally delicious. There was no bitter aftertaste. Best chocolate I've had in a long time.

I'm a serious chocoholic, but I tend to stay away from dark chocolate, because it's often too bitter. The Newman brand produces so many other good food products that I thought I would give this a try. What a treat! The texture is smooth, and the flavor is just right for my taste. It's just a little bit darker than semi-sweet. Not too sweet and not too bitter. So good that I wanted to eat the entire big bar in one sitting, but I forced myself to show a little (very little) restraint. Once again, the Newman brand comes through. Excellent dark chocolate bar!

I love chocolate, and especially dark chocolate, which to me has an exceptional taste. It's therefore no surprise that I really enjoyed this new chocolate bar. It has the crisp flavor of dark chocolate (it's 54% cocoa) but there is a sweetness to it that you usually don't get in dark chocolate. According to the label, all of the ingredients are organic, which is good news to those who appreciate that kind of thing. Bottom line: it is an excellent chocolate bar which I think will be enjoyed by anyone who is a chocoholic such as myself.

This is an excellent dark chocolate. Very nice quality. Smooth. Not too sweet. It is a dark chocolate (54%). I really like dark chocolate better for treats than milk chocolate as the flavor is more enhanced. This is one of the best dark chocolates generally available. The fact that I can snag some anytime from Amazon is fantastic.

I am planning to make a gelato this weekend with slivers of this chocolate mixed in for a kinda chocolate chip variation. It should be really good.

Good things:
1 The thickness is a plus, it is nice to bite a thicker piece of chocolate.
2 It is all organic.

Not so good things:
1 The initial aroma is a bit off putting somewhat like a cross between coffee and ashtray.
2 Takes a while to actually taste this product, it's overall weak on cocoa flavor but at least it doesn't taste like it smells!
3 Has a waxiness to it, even though there is no paraffin in it, not sure why.
4 My initial reaction to this supposedly dark chocolate was that it was way too sweet and not at all complex in flavor.
5 Anticlimactic chocolate lacking any particularly distinguishing notes.

I am a big fan of Lindt chocolate, especially the very dark high cocoa percentage bars with their rich, wonderful, full spectrum of complex flavors and fruity notes. This product was just plain bland and nothing special. Three stars instead of two because I didn't hate it but I wouldn't buy it.

There isn't much not to like about this bar, except that it seems kind of small for the price. The chocolate is organic, it's difficult to top that. No guilt about pesticides, etc.

This bar is 54% cacao mass. Sometimes with a super-dark chocolate the taste is very bitter. This one is not, it has a nice mellow taste. It's not sweet, but definitely balanced. I am a mass-quantity chocolate eater, so that usually means milk chocolate for me. I do like dark chocolate, but if I had the choice, it would be milk as first choice. This one is really perfect for me because I can eat this a little bit at a time without feeling like I want to eat it all at once. In fact, one bar lasted me about five days, which is a seriously long time in my pantry. At this time of the year, I really need to re-think my chocolate consumption so perhaps this is the way to go, so I will eat less and perhaps enjoy more.

The squares on this bar are kind of large, but easily broken up into smaller squares without wasting chocolate. Yes, I worry about wasting my chocolate, even if it is tiny amounts! Enjoy!

This was nothing special. It reminded me a lot of other commercial chocolates I've tried. I was disappointed that it was relatively waxy, and it didn't have enough of a dark chocolate flavor. It was a lot sweeter than what I expected. I would choose this over Hershey's or Ghiradelli, but there are a lot of other organic brands that provide a better chocolate experience (Dove Dark is even better than this).

I did appreciate that it came wrapped in foiled paper. It might make for a nice alternative to other commercial bars if you're looking for something wrapped up more like the old Hershey bar design. I can see someone removing the outside wrapper and putting a custom paper wrapper around the foil as a favor for a baby or wedding shower or maybe a special anniversary party.

I love chocolate in general and dark chocolate in particular. But this chocolate bar is just ok. It has kind of a waxy character to it and isn't what I'd call smooth. Really kind of a slightly harsh cocoa flavor to it, which is probably due to it's high 54% cocoa content.

It's certainly not bad. I don't think I've ever met a chocolate bar that I didn't like. But it's not especially good either.

Organic chocolate in my experience can be pretty hit-or-miss, especially if it's American-made. This is a perfect example -- while the Newman's folks probably liked it, it just doesn't do much for me. It's too sweet for my taste (though that may be more a factor of the 54% cacao content -- I'm used to more), and it has a weird solventy aftertaste to it that just ruins it for me.

I wouldn't buy it. If you like sweet dark chocolate, though, you might.

Whatever your preference, this is excellent chocolate: rich, smooth and sweet on the tongue. It kicks like a cup of coffee and serves to brighten a dull afternoon. However at 54% cocoa, it doesn't really qualify as dark chocolate.

I'd draw the line for dark chocolate at about 60% cocoa content. Still rate this as a quality product, easily superior to Dove or Hershey. Newman's Organic label consistently strives for the best in their line of food products. I think they have gone for the "best" flavor here and have created a chocolate bar that is sweeter than my personal preference.

If milk chocolate is for kids, then this is merely teenage chocolate...it still has some growing up to do. Real dark chocolate doesn't get by on sweetness alone. Real dark chocolate comforts because it has known adult sorrow but has managed to overcome it without becoming too bitter. Real dark chocolate knows about sin but winks at guilt. This may be too philosophical for a review about a candy product. Have some more chocolate and don't think too much about it...

I would certainly choose this bar over lower quality chocolate like Hershey's or Dove. However, among the better quality chocolates like Dagoba, Lindt, Ghirardelli, etc., there isn't much that makes this bar stand out.

There is a strong chocolate flavor (not at all bitter), and I also detected a hint of fruit. I was surprised that the cocoa content is only 54%, since it has the taste and texture of a much darker chocolate. I do appreciate the fact that it is made with real vanilla.

Ever since I saw on TV how much work the cocoa farmers have to do to get their product into the sack and to market I have tried to purchase chocolate that treats the farmers more fairly. Rainforest Alliance Certified Cocoa used in Newman's Own Organics products meets this requirement.

As for this product, 54% cocoa is a nice step up for people who normally do not like dark chocolate. While it may be a bit tame for those who like really dark chocolate, I thought it was quite good. It has a nice smooth texture that didn't have the waxy feel of standard store-bought chocolate. It melted smoothly without any off flavors or nasty aftertaste.

So what's not to like? The price is a bit steep even for premium chocolate. Given a choice, I will stick to Divine (certified Fair Trade) for the few times I give into the chocolate urge.

"Newman's Own" products are generally very good, with high quality ingediants and perfect execution. This Organic Dark Chocolate bar (54% cocoa) was perfectly sweet, without being bitter or too rich. Two of us spent an hour slowly munching through one bar, savoring every bite.

A real treat of high quality dark chocolate. Definitely worth a try!

I thought my review from the single item listing would carry over to here, but it didn't. I've got to warn guys off of this useless "tool."

This thing was obviously designed by a woman. Trying to be "proper" with my comments, women don't have the same "hardware" to be cleaned.

It doesn't fit your hand. When you're slick with soap the plastic shell makes it hard to hold onto. It's useless for building lather, even with our soft water. Both sides are too small. Because of the shell, you can't run it between your toes, nor use it even on ground-in dirt between your fingers.
