The packaging is superb with lots of information on the company and its ethical trade practices.  I also went on their website to read about Dilmah and found that the Company runs various programs to help their own workers.  A very noble cause!!!  I mean I applaud Dilmah for doing this human service when it's most needed in today's world.  We need Company like Dilmah who puts humanity and their workers first.  Thank you Dilmah for the lovely product and keep up the good work.

and not worth the premium price. I had seen this tea before and when Amazon offer the $10 off I decided to try the Yata Watte & the Breakfast teas.

Twinings Ceylon has a distinctive - as they call it - "bright" flavor, but I can't detect any taste that comes close here. On the can Yata is described as "It tastes round, full almost muscular and juicy, with elements of ....spices and bay leaf"......? Our friend B.P. describes it as "very light" which comes closer to the truth as far as I can taste. This tea isn't that different than from PG tips, Yorkshire gold or any decent quality black tea.

Second issue is the packaging, If you go to the Dilmah site you see the owner patting himself on the back about what a good guy he is for the way he runs his plantations. He should try producing a little less waste for us consumers to throw away, first a shrink wrap holding the 3 cans together, then each can is shrink wrapped, an outer lid, an inner lid, and then last a foil & plastic bag. Not only does it gripe the conscientious consumer in me to see so much waste, but it is adding 2-3 dollars for something that may get second use or second best goes to recycling.
I've tried other root beer popsicles before, but they were not as close to being as good as A&W's. It was very easy. I just put them in the freezer, and then after dinner my family eats them.
Smaller tubes than I expected, and honestly, flat root beer turned ice pop just isn't that tasty. Next time I'll pass.

These make a great and tasty treat and only 50 calories in 3 popsicles.
The cost here is much too high. We purchase them at local supermarkets for
0.75 to $1 per box of 10.

I like A&W root beer. Years ago our household had a blind taste test of the major root beers and we concluded A&W is the best tasting brand, by far, with a great creamy texture. So, if these frozen pops tasted like the beverage, I'd have rated them highly. Unfortunately, they do not. Somewhere in the translation from frothy, fizzy cold soda to flat, frozen stick, the essence of A&W was lost leaving an oddly flavored unenjoyable confection.

Also these pops are much smaller than I think they should be or at least how I remember similar sleeve enclosed treats being.

Having said all this, my children ran through these like ravenous monkeys, so maybe children's taste buds can find something to like.

I ordered this product because I really enjoyed the A&W freezer pops.  Throughout the past 2 summers my local Target store carried these in 10 pops per box for $1.00.  I had seen adds on-line for 150 pops per boxes for $10.  I ordered these and, MUCH to my surprise, received five 10 pop boxes for over $5.00 per box!!  This guy is nothing but a thief!

I just opened the tiny pack and made a bowl of their miso soup. The good things is that the tofu, green onion and seaweed arent small. The taste is good with not a lot of salt content ---- 510 g. However the little plastic box that houses the block of miso tends to crush up so you have to make sure when you take it out you get all the stuff that has fallen out. The other problem I had was that they say put block in bowl and add 160 ml of hot water. Well I dont know how much that is so I just put in 8 ounces. It is very mild and does have a good taste with nice bits of stuff. I gave it four stars because of the packaging (the block should have a cover) and it would be nice to know how much 160 ml is?

UPDATE: It has been some time now and I still love this little package of miso soup. I have learned to deal with the packaging. I have this practically everyday. My only other complaint is that the seaweed is huge, so I take some scissors and cut it up.

I HAVE A QUESTION FOR ANYONE THAT CAN HELP ME -------------------? In looking at the nutritional value, I noticing that vit A and C, calcium and Iron has no value at all. I know Miso soup is good for you and I do enjoy it. Does anyone know if this packaged soup gives one any healthy benefits? Thanks ----
This soup is easy to make, ready in a minute, and reasonably tasty if you take it for what it is. Don't expect a gourmet experience, however.

The title says it all. This soup is delicious and makes a great snack.
This soup is even better than the Miso soup that I have had in Japanese restaurants.

This is easily the best Miso Soup I've had, either at home or in a restaurant. Beyond tasting great, the ingredients look wholesome and definitely *not* processed.

Each individual serving package contains the ingredients pressed into a rectangular block. The block is held together on five sides by a plastic box. I guess that is what allows the soup to be reconstituted with large pieces of tofu, sea weed, and other good things.

I LOVE this soup. Its great to take to work with me. Miso soup is one of my fav soups, and I havn't found any other brand that gives off the flavor that this soup does, with such big pieces of tofu, onion and seaweed.. Very excited about this!!

All you have to add are eggs and water to make this quick mix, so it's very hard to get this wrong. Each box is enough to bake a cupcake/muffin tin or a 8x8x2 pan.

Tastewise, this is definitely much more "traditional" than I am used to. Most cornbreads I've had are very sweet and slightly moist--even other spicy blue cornbreads I've had. This was not something I achieved the first time trying this at even the lowest bake time. My brother described it akin to a tortilla chip. Ouch.

Additional sugar and butter and lowering the baking temperature has alleviated this quite a bit, but I will probably continue to make some changes to the mix.

Lastly, this mix is indeed quite spicy, and I normally handle spicy foods very well. As a product itself it is not overwhelmingly spicy, but this definitely has a little bit more kick than I was expecting. I will be experimenting whether this can be changed as well and will update my review accordingly.

My rating of 4 stars goes mostly for ease of using the mix. Rating would probably be lower if my taste preferences were of higher weight, but this is what happens when everything is already in the mix!

I was disappointed in the limited amount of mushroom pieces found in this large, 26 ounce can of mushroom soup.  I'll go back to the small cans that at least have enough mushrooms in them to impart the mushroom flavor and have a bit of mushroom in every spoonful.  Had I known that this was really just cream of chicken soup with the mislabeled name of mushroom attached, I would not have bought this product.  It's still way too high in salt too.  I don't recommend this size can of Campbell's mushroom soup even if it does feed a larger group of people at the dinner table.

This Campbell's Cream of Mushroom soup is so easy to use and tastes wonderful.  I use it in a lot of casseroles and it adds not only taste but moisture and the best texture for any dish.  The family size cans work perfect for my family.  I keep my pantry stocked with this grocery item.
It seems like I am always sampling new coffee for my K-cup brewer, but for consistent good taste this is one of the best. It makes a quality cup of coffee with real coffee taste.

Tully's French Roast is my favorite morning coffee. This supply is unusually bitter.  Since I have been buying locally in smaller quantities, I feel I have been dumped upon with old product in this purchase - and will likely toss it. Advice:  buy nearer home and check "use by" dates.  This box comes with loose K-cups inside and no date whatsoever.
When I was opening the boxes I noticed there were some Tully's House Blend KCups included in each box. Besides that issue - I enjoy the Tully's Frnch Roast.
My wife tried quite a few brands of K cup coffee, and finally decided on Tully's French roast as the one she wanted. Saw the great offer on Amazon, and couldn't pass it up.
This is my favorite coffee.  I like a strongly flavored brew and this fills the bill and the "smokey flavor" is an enhancement I like.

I didn't think I was a Green Mountain Coffee Roasters fan - I usually think their coffee is mediocre, at best - but this is excellent.  I make one cup per "small" Keurig serving - and it's almost an espresso.  I love it, and I am very fussy about coffee.

This is a great option if you are looking for a bold roast K-Cup. This is my new favorite. Coffee People Organic used to be a favorite but they seemed to have quit making it or the new replacement is not as good.
having trouble finding a k kup with right strength, either too weak or too strong, but this one is better than most.
strong, not much flavor, very little aroma. I tried it once, will not purchase another time. I have other similiar brands that met the standards i expected.
Best tasting coffee. Love dark roast with a bit of a bite. Can't go wrong with Tullys. Well worth the money.

I prefer my coffee to be a bold Flavorful roast and this Tully's French Roast does that, and then some. I've tasted a number of different K-Cups and Tully's seems to satisfy the boldest tastes, their coffees always seem to be a little bit of heven.
Excellent flavor-properly done French Roast. Smokey and rich. Sufficiently strong,  though I always think k -cups need more coffee in them.
This coffee has turned out to be my very favorite in K-cups.  It is the best of the "bolds"- full-bodied, rich tasting and is a great way to start my day.

I was given a keurig B70 as a gift and was asked which coffee sample type(s) I wanted with it.

I decided to take a chance on this one. It was a good choice.

The coffee was smooth and full bodied.

An excellent french roast.

There is none of the pale, steak-like, albacore consistency in the tuna in these cans at all.

It is literally the worst quality of albacore tuna I can ever remember buying.

(Meanwhile, if you care about quality, I would suggest the Sustainable Seas albacore as an alternative. It's not much more expensive and the quality is terrific. I know, not a terribly original nor creative title BUT it happens IMO to be *true*.

Ingredients: water, mustard seed, vinegars (white distilled, red wine, white wine), sugar, salt, white wine, garlic, spices, xanthan gum, tumeric, citric acic, artificial and natural flavors, annato.

This is great to keep your puppy or older dog busy. We have 3 dogs ranging from 18 month, 8years and 12years.  Our mistake was only buying 1 bone which we will soon rectify.  They all love this. It will keep the puppy busy for at least 30-45 minutes. I would definitely recommend this product.

I previously bought the medium size of this product. I don't put it in it's bristle boy, my chihuahua loves the rings just a they are. For such a tiny dog, she's a powerful chewer. The picture of the smaller gnawhide rings looked like they were the same diameter just thicker. NOT--they are teeny-tiny. She'll be eating them, but I'm pretty disappointed in their size. Personally, I'd love the medium rings to be thicker so they'll last longer than 10 minutes!

This was a big shocker. I got one a piece for my two dogs. They went absolutely nuts over these things, as if they were getting a hot dog. I used to buy them all the time until we left the toys behind on a vacation. The dogs loved the jerky rings but not so much the cornstarch rings. I would put the cornstarch rings on the outside and the jerky rings on the inside. Somehow they would eat the jerky completely without touching the cornstarch.

Its a good toy and treat to keep them busy and out of trouble. The treats a fairly cheap as well as the toy. These might be a bit big for small dogs but I strongly recommend them. Great treat/toy.

Our two 65 pound Dogs just love this treat on their bouncy bones. Wonderful when you have to leave them and they need something to keep them busy. They just love them and we have used them for over two years now. Our daughter is using the product for her new boxer mix.

My dog loves to chew on these, but dang, they give her the worst gas I've ever smelled in my life, and it goes on for hours. They probably don't cause the same reaction in all dogs, but I won't buy them anymore.

This toy keeps my 7 month old husky/german shepherd mix fully engaged for about 20 minutes. We have to prevent her from running, jumping and playing while she recovers from a soft-tissue injury. It's very hard to keep this highly energetic and curious puppy from running around the living room out of frustration and boredom while she heals. The Busy Buddy Bouncy Ball really holds her attention and seems to burn up some of her excess mental and physical energy. She seems calmer afterwards. I can shower, get the laundry and do other chores out of her sight as long as she has her Buddy to play with. The rings are a little pricey, so I don't know if we'll continue to use it after she has healed. But for the next 3 weeks, we are devoted to this toy. I'm going to order a bunch of refill packs right now, so we don't run out! (Caution: 4 rings in 1 night seem to cause loose stools.)
My Scottie loves this toy!!!!  It keeps him busy for about a half hour and by then he has both of the rawhide thingies off of it...he goes nuts when you give this to him...it's like doggie catnip!!!

My dog Brooklyn loves this doggie chew. He's now master it, and it would take him about 10 minutes to take it apart.

As a CAUTION, these rings must be used with the Busy Buddy Toy. Dogs can swallow this ring as a whole and it can lodge into the esophagus or intestine.

This is my dog's favorite toy.  The rings are edible and not the least bit "bad" for him.  The Busy Buddy was actually recommended to us by his trainer since he's a "strong chewer", and she was right!  It's durable and keeps him occupied for at least 30-45 minutes when he has his fresh rings.  We'll be continuing to buy these as long as he can chew.  :)

Our vet friend gave Busy Buddies to my dogs for Christmas. What a life saver. These things keep them busy for hours. They love chewing on them and they drag them out in the yard to chew on them some more.
When I need to be busy and can't keep my eye on the dogs, I give them their Busy Buddies and it keeps them out of trouble while I do what I have to do.
Thanks for creating such a wonderful product.

This product makes a chew treat last longer when it is used withPremier Busy Buddy Bouncy Bone, Medium. The combination keeps my dogs active for an extended length of time without the need to treat often.
My pet is extremely satisfied with this product and I have ordered again and will order in the future.
The Gnawhide Rings are an excellent distraction for your Jack Russell; also works as a healthy (relatively) snack.
Excellent product. My dog loves these rings and devotes his full attention to his Busy Budy Bone when I put the rings on it.

We picked up the first Busy Buddy Bone at a Greyhound meet'n-greet in Philadelphia, although our boy is a Beardie. It became his favorite immediately. By itself, it's just a good little chew toy, but the edible "Gnawhide" rings make it "new" each time. Beardies need a lot of grooming; daily in fact. This is his reward for enduring his nightly torture.
My one year old pup absolutely loves these things with or without the Busy Buddy Bone.  Of course, he spends much more time with it when they're on the Busy Buddy Bone.
My dog loves these rings, he'll work and work to chew them off until their gone usually with in ten minutes.
These are great to distract/redirect chewing puppies but they like the "rough" type one way better than the smoothe one

I don't write reviews very often -- only if I'm either very thrilled with a product or very disappointed.  In this case, I'm thrilled! :)  We just got two German Shepherd puppies -- and have tried numerous chewtoys, Kongs, etc -- but the Busy Buddy is the favorite!  I found that the pups like the rough rawhide rings better than the smooth ones... but they just chew the rough ones first & then go for the smooth.  This bone keeps them occupied for quite a while -- and they'll keep gnawing at it to get the last little bit of the ring off.  I found it lasts longer if you screw the toy together tightly -- that makes it more challenging for them to get the rawhide off.  Great toy!

When used with the Premier Busy Buddy Bone, these rings are great for keeping the dog busy! The bone can also be used alone, but adding these rawhide rings provides a lot more fun. My dog loves them! And Amazon is a great store to find them for low price and free shipping over $25.

I purchased the Busy Buddy Bone over a year ago for my hound dog (puppy at the time). I've purchased the inserts more than once because of her teething and it's a lot less expensive than buying rawhide bones every day.  It seems to calm her.  She is now over 60 lbs and when it's time for her to sleep she always has her bone with her.  I like the product, but I can't find it anywhere but on line in the area I live.
My dogs love the Busy Buddy Gnawhide bones.  The bones keep them occupied and happy for a while when I'm busy and can't give them the attention they want.

My dog is the brainiac type.  No stuffed animals or balls for him.  He'd rather take apart a plastic bottle or a remote control.  I knew I'd have a hit on this toy and I sure do!  He's built up his speed to get the rawhide rings off the spools, but he's still interested in it and can't wait until I reload it.  Just be sure to remember which size toy you purchase...I accidently bought the wrong size replacement rings.  Luckily, they work at all sizes, but the treat after all the effort on his part is not the same.  Better than a Kong, which I'll probably be donating to the shelter dogs who would settle for less.

These Premier treats are made for the Buddy Bouncy Bone. We call them the pepperonis and my puppy gets one on the Bouncy Bone every night before bed to calm him done a bit and he just loves them!! In fact after two nights he really started craving them before bed and asks to get down to our bedroom not to sleep but for his pepperoni!!

Doing two at at time can be expensive but one on one side to the bone is just right!!

I love Tito's premium vodka from Austin, TX mixed with Hansen's and a wee bit of Manhattan's key lime juice (available here) over very clean ice like Arctic Glacier. Try it - you'll be commenting favorably on this review! Very clen, crisp and refreshing in moderation.

French Breakfast radishes are a real garden treat. I plant them every year and am rewarded with fresh radishes from the garden each spring. This is an early spring crop, so plant as soon as the frosts are over. I plant a row each week for 4 weeks to get a continual supply of radishes. French Breakfast radishes have a red body with white tips. They are about 3-4" long and take about 28 days to mature. Do not leave them in much longer than this or they will get pithy (hollow). Water regularly to ensure even growth and prevent spliting. These are easy to grow and very mild and tasty. They are generally not a "hot" radish. Fine for eating whole or slicing on salads. Grubs tend to enjoy these radishes, so you may want to consider a grub killer before planting.

konedog

The French Breakfast Radishes are awesome, tasty little guys.  And they're not just for breakfast anymore... snacks, salads, even plate eye candy.  I really appreciate Amazon's "long tail" in supporting specialized vegetable items.

Also well liked by my Team in the office.
Excellent product, amazing shipping speed and great customer service...I always enjoys their products...
Trappey's Navy Beans With Jalapeno. Not much flavor, the beans old tasteing. I won't buy again. I would give these beans zero stars if I could.

Manufacturer Luck Chen has shuttered the facilities that produced this product due to quality concerns in China. Beware of products that feature $40 savings... Especially if it is a food product.

EDIT 12/17/2011
Due to my concerns, I phoned Luck Chen and spoke at length about my apprehensions. The noodles Luck Chen LLC produced were manufactured in China. The MannaSoy product is manufactured in Israel. My over critical mind assumed that because on Luck Chen's website (the LLC that is at the 'top' of the business structure, at least as product description reads "Manufacturer: Luck Chen') then I felt all products under that name would be suspect of quality as well. My concerns were fostered by lack of distinction on either Luck Chen's or Manna Soy's websites detailing the different countries of manufacture and lack of highlighting this applies solely to the noodle bowls; the Luck Chen representative said he hadn't considered how that may play out in a customer's mind and said he would work on clearing up that distinction on the websites.

I now feel confident in ordering some of the MannaSoy product and giving it a spin in my wok. Hopefully if anyone should have concerns similar to my initial ones, they will be rested by my experience and Luck Chen's explanation to me.

Thanks to Daniel D. STEIN-FREER for challenging my initial comment.

If you do not like curry chicken DO NOT PURCHASE. You will have to use this in a chicken curry dish, maybe a sweet and sour dish would be a good dish to lower the curry flavor, but its still there. I love the texture, this could very well be mistaken for real meat. I love it!!

Vegetarian for 18 years, so I'm not new to this rodeo.  Purchased the product with high hopes on the basis of Amazon customer reviews.  Mistake.  Product seems greasy to the touch and feels the same in the mouth.  Overly spiced--but most importantly, to this consumer at least, it simply tasted terribly.  4.4 lbs(!)  of inedible gloppity glop.

I like this because it can be stored on the shelf for long periods, a good way to always have some protein on hand. Once opened, it lasts up to 5 days in the fridge. It can also be frozen for a 2-3 months. The texture is good, firm and chewy, but not tough. A 2 ounce serving has 63 calories, 9 g protein, 3 g fat, 1 g carbohydrate, 4 g fiber, and 367 mg sodium. The package has 63 (2 ounce) servings.

The curry flavor is mild but tasty. It's not hot, has little or no chili, tastes mostly of turmeric, with a little cumin (another reviewer called it a "strong" curry flavor, so reactions will vary). It has a bit too much salt for me. This dish could be improved by allowing those who want it to add salt on their own. It's better with rice, veggies, etc., than eaten alone. If mixed in with unsalted foods, the salt can be balanced.

This is a good value, it's better than OK. Rounding up to 5, I'd give it 4.5 stars, detracting only because of the salt. Worth a try, especially for vegetarians and vegans who want pantry stock.

First off I think the texture is great it seems like real chicken. BUT the curry flavor is way way too much. My husband didn't seem to mind it but I thought it was way too strong. I am gonna try to soak the chicken for 30mins to reduce the curry flavor. It comes with a ton of chicken, way more then I expected.

I was skeptical about ordering this product due to the extremely reasonable price per pound compared to most other meat alternatives.  I was concerned that the stated 4.4 lb. product weight would be composed mostly of liquid.  But, the shipping rate was very reasonable, so thought I'd give it a try.  After recieving the product (extremely fast shipping) I was pleasantly surprised at the quality of the product texture, density and ease of handling (the size of the "chicken" strips is perfect for most recipes).  The heavy, sealed bags were crammed with product with just a little broth to keep moist. Awesome meat substitute. Great taste and texture. Very easy to prepare. Seasoning is not overwhelming and you can add your own to change the flavor. Great, great product. I highly recommend.
we watch at home but feel like in the movies.great purchase. large capacity. quality product. i highly recommend this product

Rip off! I am so disappointed.  Not worth half the price charged.  I made the mistake of thinking I was getting the jumbo and two smaller ones as pictured.  Cute design but not much different than an icecream bucket.

Campbell's Chunky Beef with Country Vegetables (BCV) is my favorite, but this was such a good deal on subscribe and save that I decided to try it as an alternative. It's okay--I'll be finishing all the cans--but every time I open one I wish I just bought BCV instead.

A note about Campbell's Chunky soups in general... they all have their names "mixed up" and you should swap what is before and after the "with" in the name to know what to expect in the can (e.g., BCV is really more like "Country Vegetables with Beef"). That said, I still prefer Campbell's Chunky soups to any other brand. And... this flavor is pretty good, as long as you like rice and you're not trying to substitute it for BCV.

I have 5 cats, and all 5 just love Soulistic. My cats have always been dry-food cats. After my princess got sick, I started researching cat food and came to the conclusion that wet food is better for them. I've tried every brand out there. My goal is to have my cats on a grain-free, high protein diet made of natural ingredients, and minimal by-products. I've tried Wellness, Natural Balance, etc. But my cats are just so finicky that they'll stop eating a brand after being served the same thing more than 2 days in a row. But with Soulistic, they're still loving it, and it's been close to a year. I notice they like the gravy ones better than the gelee ones. I also try to switch up the flavors so they're not eating the same flavors every day as I find that they will be less enthusiastic if I keep giving them the same thing. This brand is a bit watery compared to other premium cat foods. But if you look at the "meat", it seems to be unaltered natural fish/chicken. I don't know for sure though. I think the watery gravy actually makes it easier to blend and tricks my cat into taking in more fluid. Unfortunately, this brand is only available from Petco. I was thought they would be softer than they are, therefore I was disappointed when trying them.

Ok, while I didn't like this one as well as Davidson's other peach offerings, I did think it was decent, and totally drinkable. And this is coming from someone who doesn't really like tea, but is trying to develop a taste for it.

The overall taste of this tea is a bitterness slightly spiced. I didn't really taste the peach at all, but that was ok. It was a good kind of bitterness, one that combined with the actual heat of the drink warmed you up and it was very calming. The spices were hard to identify if you don't look at the package, but they reminded me of winter and fall, and getting ready to settle into the harvest. The same kind of spices you would find in a cookie. Although the clove did really stand out.

The ingredients are good in this tea. Organic black tea, organic orange peel, organic cinnamon and organic cloves with some natural flavor. So almost everything was organic, which I wasn't expecting, but was pleasantly surprised by. I do have to say the orange peel surprised me, I would have never guessed it was in there. But I was a little disappointed peach wasn't actually listed, which is probably why I didn't taste it. And the one teabag was sufficient enough for a large mug of tea after steeping for several minutes. I added no sweetener to the tea either.

A nice tea by Davidson's but not my favorite. Still, the ingredients alone make it worth getting.

2011 has seen a new wave of Korean ramyuns coming. Shin ramyun black, Kkokko myun, and Nagasaki jjamppong are the three "premium" ramyuns and Nagasaki jjamppong is the best among those by far. Kkokko myun has same white-colored chicken-based soup as Nagasaki jjamppong and actually is pretty good, but not as good as Nagasaki jjamppong. Shin ramyun black seems to be a little bit better than ordinary Shin ramyun, but that's about it. Nagasaki jjamppong has very clean and freshening taste, a bit spicy but not too extreme. Ordinary ramyuns such as Shin ramyun usually have red-colored beef-based soup which sometimes can easily make you fed up whereas Nagasaki jjamppong is much less likely to do so. I hope its price in Amazon drop soon so that I can order it often.

Again noted the tendency of the filling to become very hot when they are done in a microwave. I also compared them to other brands- Hopper's, and Mr. Kipling's, and I think these are the best of the lot. I also prefer them to the the Glenfiddich ones, by a smaller margin.

Absolustely wonderful, tasty and scrumptuous. I purchased two boxes of these and one is in the freezer for that special treat. These are so good, you don't want to share them. Hide them and treat yourself to a treat once in a while LOL. Cannot go wrong with Walkers. Pastry is to die for too.

Seller shipped this product fast and I received it well-before christmas.  Pies were fresh and delicious.  I have ordered from this seller several times before and never had a problem. Highly recommended seller.

Heat these up in the microwave for about 15-25 seconds and they're ready. Too bad there's NO MEAT inside! Mince pie (or mincemeat pies) are a traditional festive British sweet pastry, usually consumed during the Christmas and New Year period. Mince Pies normally have a pastry top, but versions may also be found without the top in which case they are known as a mince tart.

The name 'mincemeat' comes from the original recipe. Up to the Victorian era the mince(meat) pie would actually have been a spiced meat pie with some dried fruit. Today the only remnant of the original meat is (sometimes) the inclusion of suet. Typically fillings today consist entirely of fruit-based mincemeat containing dried fruit such as raisins, currants, glace cherries, apricot, candied peel; spices such as cinnamon or nutmeg; nuts such as walnuts or chopped almonds; suet; and some kind of alcohol, usually either brandy or rum.

Walkers Mince pies are suitable for vegetarians because the suet is replaced by vegetable oil. The pie is often finished off with a delicate dusting of either castor sugar or icing sugar on top.
One bite was enough the package went in the trash. Used to buy these in England family favorite this product tasted old

My husband always complains that he doesn't get mincemeat pie at Christmas. So, this year I bought him Walkers. He loves them, and still has one each night after dinner with whipped cream. He says that they remind him of the mincemeat pie his mother used to make when he was a child.

I'm not quite sure what happened to the other reviewers of the Chow Mein Kung Pao Chicken Noodles... I just ate one and found it to be quite delicious. Perfect savory flavor, a light to moderate amount of spice (I picked out some of the peppers but I'm sure I would have been fine even if I had left them in) and everything cooked very well. I will be buying many more of these to keep as a backup lunch option at work.

Like the title says it's smelly it will probably smell up your entire room, so open a window or door if you can. The taste itself is alright but the price they sell it on the internet is a joke, you could get a bunch of packets for a lot less at some dollar/second hand store if you looked hard enough. The change was nice I suppose but I'll probably just stick to the shrimp and chicken flavors the next time I'm in the mood for some convenient noodles.

One of my favorite flavors.  The peppers in the seasoning packet are pretty spicy but for the price it's a decent easy meal option.  I buy them at my 99 cent only store and honestly for the amount of what you are getting I wouldn't pay more than a dollar each for these things but they are tasty and a bit different than your "usual" cup of noodle.
Love Kung Pao flavor! I couldn't find it in the local grocery store and glad that Amazon has it. Taste might be too strong for some people but this is just right for me.

Very tasty! More spice than I would've anticipated. Cooks quickly (~4-5 mins). Impressed with overall quality and flavor of these instant noodles. Used to Top Ramen, but these are above average, that's for sure. Premium ingredients packet contained a good mix of chicken, spices, and peppers, much to my delight. Perfect for a quick snack/meal. Would recommend to others!

I got this noodle I was so excited to try them but after I ate two bite going to sink and nasty after taste so awful smell too...noodle is bad taste and too salty sauce in there. No more buy or eat again.
The best flavor in my opinion is the original chicken. Seeing the Kung Pao flavor I was excited, after trying it, however, I was not impressed. It was not good at all. I ended up throwing it away.

I received a free sample of Planters NUT-rition Cinnamon Raisin Granola Nut peanut butter by mail. This is by far the best peanut butter that I have ever tasted! I've been eating it right out of the jar and enjoying all of the flavors and textures from the add-ins. I never thought to mix cinnamon with peanut butter, but it's delicious. If I can find this at a decent price, I will be buying more of it for myself. Sorry, Amazon, but $35 for four 12-ounce jars is NOT a decent price, not even with free Prime shipping. Not even close! I would consider paying around $3.50 per jar, but I won't ever pay $8.75.

This product was not HORRIBLE, but I feel cheated. It looked so good, and the price of $4.99 for a small jar suggested there were some great add-ins. NOT.

The berry nut flavor is basically average-tasting crunchy peanut butter with some tough, dried cranberries thrown in. I was hoping the "nut" was a walnut, pecan, or almond (or all of the above!), but it's merely an unimpressive sliver of regular old peanut. After I got done picking the hard cranberries out of my teeth, I decided I would never by this flavor of overpriced, disappointing peanut-butter again.

Just got home from the grocery store, where I purchased a cannister of these for the first time. We have tried many of the others by Emerald, but, until today, not these. I thought I was hooked on the Cashews with Sea Salt and Pepper......until today. These are So, SO gooood!! I, personally, have no issue with the Splenda in them, as I am one of those people constantly doing battle with the bathroom scales. Better a little Splenda than a lotta calories. And they taste Deeeevine! Definitely worth trying if you haven't!
Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds, 11oz Canister (Pack of 4)

These are nice tasting and a nice change of pace -- I eat almonds daily and was looking for something new. However, I find that the almonds have an aftertaste to me. After closer inspection of the ingredient list, I found out that the product contains sucralose (Splenda). That is the aftertaste.

I doubt that I will be buying these again.

I just discovered these. They are GREAT for me because I am trying to cut back on "bad" carbs due to insulin resistance and PCOS. I have been craving sweets so badly (fell off the wagon during holidays and trying to get back on again!).

The chocolate taste IS subtle but it is noticable enough for my 4 year old to say "mmm chocolate nuts!". He's really picky and he loves these.

I didn't find them too dry or burned tasting. They tasted great to me. I bought the 100 calorie packets and they are great to keep in my purse. The 100 calorie packs have 4g carbs and 2g fiber.

A chocolate candy coated almond this is not. It's basically almonds dusted in dark coccoa powder -- and sucralose is listed in the ingredients. The cocoa does not get messy on my hands and that is another huge plus !
These are so good.  They taste like a hershey kiss covered almonds, with less chocolate.  Yummy.

Twenty five dollars for 4? I bought these at Stop and Shop for 2.50 for an 11 0z. package.

I would have enjoyed more chocolate but still enjoy them the way they are. I don't feel as guilty grabbing a handful of these as I would grabbing a candy bar. Very yummy and great to munch on at games, in the car, etc.
Deliciously sweet and chocolate-y, while having essentially the same nutritional bang for your caloric buck as plain almonds. A great product.

I really liked this product! The almonds had just the right amount of chocolate "dust" on them to add flavor and sweeten up the experience. No need to worry about melting in your hands, etc... I kept this in my car and ate a couple each day on the way home from work... you know, to stave off starvation until dinner time.

Highly recommended!
These nuts have a subtle cocoa taste, nothing too overdone. They are very enjoyable and the flavor is quite unique. They are lightly salted.
The cocoa covers almonds are just the ticket to stave off the afternoon hungries.  Balance of protein and a jolt of chocolate is just right.

As someone who must seriously limit the amount of carbs in my daily diet, these nuts are the perfect snack.  They are perfect for that "chocolate attack" that comes on, and satisfy my hunger at the same time!

I love these almonds!  Apparently some reviewers thought these were and should be almond M&M's.  Thankfully, Emerald made these for adult palates, but kids seem to like them too.  The subtle chocolate flavor is wonderful.  The chocolate is roasted onto the almonds and is dry to the touch.  Can't melt and create a mess as milk chocolate does.  A box of 4 canisters didn't last as long as I thought they would.  Amazon has apparently has sold out!  Arghhh!  Do me a favor and buy 300 calorie chocolate bars and leave more of these for me!

I love these because they're not coated with sugar and dairy - just plain old dark cocoa powder. They will taste a lot like chocolate if you eat them right - put them in your mouth, let the chocolate mix with your mouth juices, then start eating the almond. Crunch crunch yum yum. If you're used to a sugar-and-dairy loaded almond, you probably eat too fast anyway - no wonder we're all so fat! Slow down and enjoy it, they really are great!

Ben

I love almonds and eat many different varieties for snacks. These Cocoa Roast Almonds from Emerald *sounded* terrific, so I ordered them right away. The first two or three tasted pretty good, though not as good as I had expected, but soon after, the cocoa left a really unpleasant, bitter aftertaste that I could've gone all day without experiencing. I'm not sure what it is because, on paper, these should be great, but in execution ... they're just not.

I think what I had in mind when we opened the canister was either the soft chocolate layer you might find in Raisinets, or the layer covered by a shell in M&Ms. Instead, we found almonds that had just been powder coated in a fine layer of cocoa. We found this a positive, in the sense that we could see the size and quality of the nuts, and that they took the center stage, with the cocoa as a subtle backdrop.

I am not a chocolate fan, but loved these. The cocoa is a secondary taste layer that doesn't build cumulatively the more of these you eat. The end result is a terrific almond snacking option, with enough variation from other approaches to keep your taste buds thinking. The almonds are crisp and of high quality. Emerald has done a fantastic job of selecting premium quality, enough so that even Alton Brown might consider going back on his rule of only buying nuts in clear containers that you can see.

With reasonable evidence to suggest that almonds represent some measure of improvement to cholesterol health, we can even toss a few of these back relatively guilt-free. Will be buying again.

It's hard to believe that Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds have the identical calorie count per serving as plain roast almonds, because the flavor of this product is so much more intense.

The texture is light and crunchy, and the sweet nutty flavor is accented by the cocoa. This is an awesome little snack with a cup of coffee, and it is also quite filling.

The word seems to be out on these fabulous little nuts, because every time I search for them in the supermarket, the Cocoa Roast Almonds are totally sold out! Buy them on Amazon and stock up. Once you try them, you won't want to be without them.

Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds are quite tasty, but be advised that the description is accurate: They carry no more than a hint of cocoa flavor. If you're looking for rich chocolate flavor, you may need to go to a candy store. However, they make a nice, light, and somewhat addictive snack, particularly if you're watching your calories, as there's only 150 per serving.

Emerald Almonds with a chocolate-powder coating are an interesting concept.  It offers the opportunity to enjoy both healthy almonds as well as the flavour of dark chocolate at the same time.  The problem is that the flavour is so strong that you cannot eat very many at a time.  Good, but not great.

These chocolate-flavored almonds were suprisingly delicious.  They are not chocolate-covered but have a chocolate flavoring.  This brings me to my only negative comment...the ingredients are only listed as natural and artificial flavors without specifying what they are which would be nice to know.

I thoroughly enjoyed these almonds. They were not sweet, so I could really taste the chocolate. The best way to describe it is almonds lightly dusted with high quality bakers chocolate powder, but not as bitter as that would be.

This is NOT a typical "chocolate covered" nut product. The dusting of chocolate is very light. If you're expecting a lot of sweet chocolate with a little nut inside you will be disappointed. However, I have to say that this product is exactly what I've been looking for; a reasonable healthy source of both almonds and chocolate.

Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds give you a satisfying snack with no health drawbacks.
Don't expect something chocolate-coated. The cocoa is more an evocation of chocolate than a candy experience. There's not too much sweetness, just a hint of cocoa.
This means your hands won't be messy when you eat them. That fact, together with the container's screw-top lid, makes these great for the car, camping, and keeping near your computer.

Emerald nuts always set the standard for nuts. These are great!!

They have great Cocoa flavor that doesn't cover up the wonderful flavor of the nuts themselves. The combination of dark chocolate and expertly roasted nuts makes for a great satisfying snack that isn't too sweet and just right.

These are not chocolate coated, but have a fine dusting of cocoa powder/cocoa flavoring that makes them satisfying and delicious!

If you expect these to taste like chocolate covered almonds, you will be disappointed. However, if you want a tasty snack with a subtle chocolate flavor, Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds might be just right.

Nuts are one of my favorite snacks, although I usually eat raw almonds or pecans rather than roasted nuts. The dry roasting gives these almonds a nice toasty flavor and extra crunch, and the cocoa powder adds just a hint of chocolate. A small handful of almonds make a nice between-meals snack to take the edge off any hunger pangs.

Do have a glass of water handy while eating these. The dry roasting and dusting of cocoa powder make them especially dry, and you will want something to drink with them.

I liked these so much I have already bought more. I plan to keep a supply on hand for those mid-afternoon munchies. A handful of cocoa roast almonds make a more healthful snack than a candy bar or chips.

I love almonds and I love chocolate, but when I eat chocolate covered almonds I always feel like the chocolate is too rich and overwhelms the taste of the nut. If you have also had this experience, then you need to look no further, since these almonds covered in dark chocolate powder perfectly combine the flavor of the two ingredients. Not to mention that you avoid consuming the saturated fat present in regular chocolate covered almonds.

I am hooked, and will keep consuming this product for as long as I can find it!

Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds are most definitely a quality, worthwhile snack item for the almond lover. My main concern with this product is that these do not have much, if any, "cocoa" or "dark chocolate" flavor like they advertise. It's just a very light dusting of powder on each almond, and the taste really doesn't stand out. The almonds themselves are fine, and I've never had any real issues with any of Emerald's line of canned nuts. So if you're looking for a relatively healthy snack item, these would satisfy your cravings. Just don't expect a burst of chocolate flavor.

I enjoyed these nuts.  I found that a handful (approx 10 - 12 nuts) curbed my appetite when I was looking for a snack.  The cocoa flavor is nice because it is not overly sweet, but was able to satisfy me when I had a craving for chocolate.

I really believe this product lives up to its manufacturer's claims: tasty, sweet, chocolaty, but sans all the extra fat and calories. The nuts were roasted with cocoa powder, which is indeed an excellent idea! In fact, I like the idea so much I'm planning to experiment with this method in my own cooking. The almonds are quite high-quality too, they are fresh and with no irregularities. I would heartily recommend these almonds to any almond-lovers.

I liked how the almonds were dusted with chocolate and didn't have that plastic-like sheen of cheap chocolate that so many chocolate almonds have. These were true to their description with the cocoa roast. I loved them and based on how quickly they disappeared, so did everyone else.

Remember that old Double Mint gum ad- double your pleasure, double your fun?
That is exactly what you get with Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds. The richness of the almonds, and the smooth taste of chocolate powder. Who'da thought to put these two together? A genius. One you start eating it is difficult to maintain control, but I did it. I took the recommended amount for one serving and used this as my treat for the evening.

These cocoa powdered almonds will be a part of my diet from hence forth.
Highly recommended. prisrob 06-12-08

Almonds are a very healthy snack, but I have to admit that most almonds taste a little like cardboard to me. These, however, were a notable exception. The dusting of cocoa was a perfect complement to the taste of the almonds without being overwhelming or cloyingly sweet. In addition, the chocolate was about as healthy as chocolate can be with very little added fat or sugar.

Yes, the chocolate taste is subtle, and if you are having a serious craving for chocolate you would be far better off with a chocolate bar. But, these nuts are healthier and better for you! I, personally, liked the combination. But, I suspect this is a matter of your personal likes and dislikes. I tend to like my almonds roasted, and my chocolate dark and with very little sugar, so for me the resulting flavor pairing was perfect. I have tried almonds with a heavier milk chocolate coating and I have never liked them, nor wanted to eat more than one or two. My family finished an entire 11 ounce canister in one sitting and I (I am embarrased to admit) could have finished the entire thing myself.

Some of the almonds DID taste a little on the burnt side, but this is pretty typical of roasted almonds in general. The price, however, is rather high. By my estimate, these would run abour $7-8 a pound, which is rather steep for roasted almonds even when you add the cost of the chocolate. The price alone is what would keep me from buying them on a regular basis.

If you get this expecting dry roasted almonds--emphasis on dry, crunchy--rather than regular almonds, it is a fine snack in a casual group. A pleasant surprise was that although it is dusted with cocoa powder, they are really not sweet.. Although I personally found the after-taste not very appealing,,  I served them to ten other people. One didn't like them at all, but the others gave them either 4 or 5 stars--particularly enjoying the smallness, crispness and lack of sweetness.  I probably wouldn't get them again for myself, but defnitely could put a bowl out for guests, as a casual alternative to greasier and sweeter snack foods.

If you like crisp roasted almonds, but also want a bit of chocolate and sweetness, these are for you.  They have only 3 net carbs in a one ounce serving after the fiber carbs are subtracted out.  I love them.

If you like almonds, and you like cocoa, then try these!  If you don't like almonds run to another aisle in the store and get something you do like.  The smoked almonds are pretty good, too.  They taste like they've been barbecued.

I'm a big nut eater; I make my own peanut butter every couple of days, experimenting with a variety of nuts to combine with the main course, peanuts. Regular almonds are notoriously hard and can even be a little hard on the grinder. But not Emerald's Marcona Almonds.

Emerald's cocoa nuts are just a tad harder, but still not as hard as almonds you get in bins or even packaged. The chocolate dusting is just the right amount to give you the cocoa flavor without losing the nut taste, as is the case with some coated versions.

I'll probably not make peanut butter out of this flavor but as a healthy snack for the heart - eight to ten nuts a couple times a day - they are perfect.

The combination of cocoa and almonds is good, making this a tasty snack. Unfortunately, they felt compelled to make it sweeter, so they added sucralose, also known by the brand name Splenda. If you're trying to avoid this artificial sweetener, then don't get this snack. But if you want some cocoa almonds, these are pretty good.

These fantastic dry-roasted almonds offer up all the chocolate-y taste of dipped almonds, thanks to their generous dusting of cocoa powder, without any of the higher-fat guilt.  Nice crunch with a hint of salty-sweetness (or would that be sweet-saltiness?)  We recently served them at a dinner party and everybody couldn't stop talking about how great they were.  Good luck stopping at a small handful!

I was a bit hesitant since they are dark chocolate and I'm a milk chocolate type of guy, I do like almonds though, so I decided to try them.  They're rather good.  Unlike other Chocolate nuts, these have a thin layer of chocolate that gives them a nice balance between the almonds and the chocolate.  Even my wife who doesn't like chocolate likes these quite a bit.

I was hesitant about these chocolate covered almonds thinking it's just a gimic.
I can say I am hooked ! The chocolate gives the nuts a little something unexpected and extra. I found myself eating a handful the first time. I am not a huge fan of almonds but these are absolutely delicious. They are not really sweet but the dark chocolate give a hint of sweetness and richness that i think plain almonds lack.
They are addictive. It's a good thing almonds are good for you !! I would highly recommend these as a snack. I also really like the twist lid. It makes it so convienent to grab a handful. yes, these almonds are the perfect snack !

Emerald's Cocoa Roast Almonds make a great on the go snack. I especially like the container as it fits nicely in the cup holder of my car and stroller. It makes a nice take-along snack during the day when running around and not having time for a meal always. The almonds have a hint of dark chocolate flavor. By the time you realize there's chocolate flavor, poof it's gone and you're onto the almond taste. For a person who enjoys almonds and the dark chocolate flavor is a bonus-this is still a nice snack. If you are purchasing this thinking it will be more dark chocolate and less almond, then you will likely be disappointed. I did not give 5-stars only because when I gave the almonds to my children who normally eat plain almonds and other nuts, they did not care for the dark chocolate roast. Hey what do kids know!

I am a lover of nuts in general and almonds in particular. My tastes are also strongly in favor of chocolate, so the combination is one that I like very much. Even better, the chocolate is in the form of very lightly sweetened cocoa powder. As someone who has a slight blood sugar problem, this feature is also one that I applaud. I received the package in the mail and by the end of the next day, I had consumed every nut. They are very good.

Great taste, great snack. Very fresh, tastes good, has a light cocoa dusting of dark chocolate on them. Not messy.  Great for keeping at your desk at work and munching on through out the day.  I really liked the flavor and freshness of this item.  I highly recommend.

Almonds may be the healthiest nut there is.  Indeed, famed psychic Edgar Cayce stated that eating 5 almonds a day will prevent cancer.  So, eating them is a nice, healthy & tasty insurance policy--hard to beat.  Adding the  cocoa makes them far tastier too.  Not overly chocolatie, sweet without being cloying, they satisfy my sometime craving for a sweet.  They go well with some fruit (I tried fresh apricots)--but CAUTION, like a certain potato chip they're hard to stop eating.  I went through half the container before stopping.  I don't think they'll last too long on my shelf.  On the other hand, if you have a big sweet tooth (or maybe all of them are sweet--if you have any left after eating tons of chocolate), they may not be sweet or chocolatie enough for you.  They are for me.  Enjoy!

I thoroughly enjoyed these almonds;  the almonds are fresh and crunchy, the cocoa not too messy or overpowering. The chocolate flavor is subtle, these are NOT milk chocolate covered almonds, and they are unlikely to stave off a true chocolate craving.  They're not really addictive either -- unlike salted nuts - I will plow through salted nuts until they are gone.  Nevertheless, they are still quite filling and satisfying.  A tasty change of pace.

Okay I have to admit it I am hooked on these almonds. The cocoa flavor is subtle, and delicious. The packaging is clever, and easy on the hands. The fact that almonds are also beneficial and good for you doesn't hurt either. The unique lid allows me to keep up with portion control which is a good thing, otherwise I would probably empty the can. These Cocoa Roasted Almonds are like eating an almond candy bar without the guilt.
Highly recommended.

This is a very tasty and very good snack. I absolutely love these. I am a fan of almonds anyway so it wasn't a stretch when you combine almonds with another one of my favorites, dark chocolate, and you have a winner.

The almonds taste fresh and as always they are meaty and filling. I can enjoy these at about 7 or 8 at a serving which seems to me to be about the serving size at ¼ cup.

Although these aren't unhealthy in the sense that there is a lot of junk added they certainly are not a weight loss tool. At 150 calories per serving and 110 of that from fat you would be in serious trouble if this replaced baby carrots on your menu.

All in all a very tasty treat. I give it four stars instead of five only because of the high fat content even if it is healthier fats.

All of the chocolate lovers loved these nuts!!A great alternative to candy and junk foods. My daughter grabbed them and claimed them as hers, so I's say this was a good deal!!!
The only thing one mAY or may NOT care for is this is not a soft, chocolate
covering but a dry, light covering.I think it tastes better as such and my daughter did not even notice.
The nuts were very good themselves.
This will go over well for the health and for the weight conscious persons.
For me, while I liked them, I am NOT a sweet lover and found them very sweet FOR ME. but I still would buy and eat them ...a few daily ...to get the benefits of dark chocolate and almonds.

I was pleasantly surprised by how much I liked these nuts. At first I thought they were chocolate coated and sweet, but that's not the case. They are dusted in dark chocolate powder. That adds flavor but not a lot, if any, calories. A one oz. serving is 150 calories and yields 3 Weight Watcher Points instead of the usual four because of the high fiber count. Good deal. It satisfies two cravings in one serving. A very good way to get your nut goodness with some chocolate too. Enjoy!

These almonds are one of my favorite snacks. If you're trying to eat healthier but still crave a little sweetness or chocolate, this is the way to go. It can be a little dangerous to your diet if you eat TOO many at once but it makes you feel less guilty than some other snacks. I like that they aren't too sweet or too chocolate-y. You still taste the almonds despite the sweet coating. This is a product that I'll be buying again.

Imperial is the brand I choose when buying nuts in the Dollar General store because it costs less than the others and the quality is good.  I had no idea they made such a gourmet treat as these Cocoa Roast Almonds but I'm certainly glad they do.  I was wondering if the coating of cocoa powder could be inhaled and cause choking (I've choked on dry cocoa powder dusted on the top of other foods) but they've added some potato start to make the coating stay put.  The dry roasted almonds are of a nice size and quality and the flavor is very good.  I think maybe they could be a bit less sweet and more dark-chocolately but still they're good and once you start eating them it's hard to stop so beware there.  These go great with a glass of Yellow Tail Cabernet Sauvignon.

Oh My Goodness. Finally the taste of chocolate covered almonds that are actually good for you. I could not believe how yummy these are. The chocolate is dry covering and baked into the almond. The dark choc doesn't up the calories or fat, infact it is lower than others.

These are a great source of protein and fiber. The only warning I would give is to measure out a 1 serving size and put the container away or you may be in trouble, they are hard to stop once you get started.

I plan on chopping some and sprinkling over fat free ice cream for a real treat without the guilt.

You will not be disappointed with these almonds, if you love dark chocolate or any chocolate for that matter give these a try.

Amazon has the best deal on them also. Take these to the beach and on vacation this year instead of unhealthy chips and candy..they fill both cravings, sweet and salty.

If you're a nut lover this may be just what you are looking for. After all, once you get beyond proper roasting, there isn't a whole lot you can say about nuts other than what you add to them. If you bury them in salt, or immerse them in chocolate, you are getting more flavor, but the trade off is unwanted cane sugar, and/or salt; so these make a pleasant bridge.
Extra added flavor with the thin coat of dark chocolate cocoa powder (that doesn't get on your fingers by the way), while only ingesting 25mg of sodium in a single 1/4 cup serving.
When I first started to eat them, I thought the dry unsweetened cocoa powder didn't add anything desirable to the flavor, but as I progressed to finishing about a 1/4 cups worth, I began to realize that this could very well become a strongly acquired taste.
If I had to be critical of the entire presentation, I would note that the plastic "jar" has a threaded top with 2 half circle single threads partially overlapping each other that results in a not so very snug closure. With very little effort you can snug them at closure and skip right past snug to loose again, so much so that if you dropped the container the lid may pop off, spilling the contents.
I am not commenting on the way they are sealed though, they did an outstanding job of that. You have to pop open the plastic seal over the top of the lid edge, just to remove the screw on top, and then once open, there is an internal air tight seal to keep the contents fresh, and they are. Overall highly recommended, especially if you are nuts about nuts.

Emerald Cocoa Roast Almonds are almonds roasted with cocoa rather than covered with chocolate, which makes them healthier and less fattening than traditional chocolate-covered almonds. This is is an advantage if you don't want to have to wear clothing made in Indonesia, a highly laudable goal considering that country's trumped-up 2005 drug-smuggling conviction of a young Australian tourist. What's more, they taste excellent, too. In fact, these are chocolate-flavored nuts for people who care about watching their weight.

The dark chocolate flavor of these airy almonds makes this snack something to look forward to.

The flavor is mild. Just enough chocolaty flavor for chocolate lovers but not too overpowering or sweet. The texture of the almonds seem airy. They are lighter than what I'm used to. It's a nice touch to the flavor. Not too heavy.

One 11 oz container holds 11 servings. Each serving approximately 1/4 cup. For 150 calories per serving this snack also packs 6g protein, 8% iron and an impressive 35% Vitamin E.

Overall, my entire family enjoyed this snack and I plan to stash one in my office at work as well as in my tote bag.

Excellent snack!

As a dedicated chocolate and almond lover this is exactly the sort of thing that would appeal to me. And I wasn't disappointed. The fresh, crisp almonds are beautifully complimented by their coating of cocoa. They're lightly sweet, too. Just enough to give you the full flavor of both chocolate and nut. The only problem I have with them is that they're sweetened with sucralose, which is an artificial sweetener, and which may or may not be good for us. There doesn't appear to be a great deal of it in the mix -- it's the last listed ingredient -- but for some it might be a problem.

As with the Marcona almonds I tried earlier, these nuts have persuaded me to think of Emerald as a better brand than I originally thought. They have some interesting offerings, and the quality of the ones I've tried has been consistently high.

If the flavor combination appeals to you, and you don't mind a bit of sucralose, then by all means give these nuts a try.

Could a thin cocoa coating satisfy a chocolate almond craving? I was pleasantly surprised with these almonds. With a big chocolate aroma, delicate dark chocolate flavor and exceptionally crunchy texture they are great as is or I also like to put out a bowl of them mixed with dried cherries.
Not as sweet as a chocolate covered nut, these are really good snack. It tones down that "roasted" flavor of the almond with just a hint of chocolate. Great snacks, lots of protein.

The Other Brother and I realized the other day that we've somehow been posting these reviews for ten years already.  Suffice it to say, The Wife has long since lost any sense of excitement she may ever have felt at the piles of free books that have come our way.  At this point, each thud of a package dropped on our front porch produces at best a cringe, at worst a snarl.  Best, that is, until the other day, when we received samples -- through the Amazon Vine program -- of two new nuts from Emerald: Cocoa Roast Almonds and Marcona Almonds.  I like the Marconas, which taste kind of like Macadamias, but don't have the almost soapy texture that has rendered them inedible to me since childhood.  She loves the dark chocolate one, which, "satisfies both the salty and the sweet urge in one snack."  These latter are most notable because they manage to leave a pleasant chocolate aftertaste--not always the case in flavored foods.  Big thumbs up!

These Emerald "Cocoa Roast Almonds" are a low carb snack that bring a bit of dark chocolate flavor to good tasting almonds. These do have artificial sweeteners, but for those of us that have to watch our sugar intake, this is a very viable treat.

Highly Recommended!

CFH

I have started eating almonds as a healthy alternative to fatty or high-carb snacks, but wanted something to satisfy my sweet tooth on occasion. These Cocoa Roast almonds fit the bill nicely. They just have a dusting of cocoa, so there's no more fat or unhealthy stuff than you would find in regular almonds, but you still get a nice chocolate taste. They are just a little bit sweeter than I really want (I like dark chocolate, semisweet or bittersweet) but still a great once-in-awhile snack!

I was quite excited to try these cocoa roasted almonds out. I love almonds and I love chocolate. And most reviews of this product imply that you get your fix of both, without the extra sugar.
Well there's definitely a whole lot less sugar in this thing - it tastes pretty bad to me. And I was quite shocked. I guess I need at least a little more sweet. But I'm shocked because I'm not THAT much of a sweet tooth. It's the bitter after-taste that really bothers me with this product. I really couldn't take it.
So just fair warning to those who might think this is going to be a great combo of chocolate and almond. Think again! This is really just cocoa and almond, and, for me, that left a very bad taste.
What a great idea with the cocoa and they would be great except for the sucrolose "diet" taste.  Don't think I'll buy again.

These nuts are a decent snack on their own and I've made cookies with them as well. They are slightly sweet and I don't think the Splenda taste is overwhelming or unpleasant, but that is obviously a personal preference. Bought them on sale at Target for $3 a package, or about half the current listed price here.

I'm a person that really loves nuts, especially flavored nuts. When I go the local farmer's market, I always look for the nut stand so I can buy some kind of cinnamon, honey, jalapeño, or whatever-flavor strikes me.

When I was offered a chance to try the cocoa almonds, I was pretty thrilled.

These nuts just "okay". They're not spectacular. As another reviewer noted, they aren't very chocolately. If you have a chocolate craving, this will just make it worse. They're also very dry (as are most almonds) and you'll need something to wash down every handful.

The almonds are high-quality, and it's a good cocoa taste, but don't expect to be blown away by this. It just won't happen.

The container is probably what impressed me the most. It's sturdy, resuable, handy to hold, and the screw-top keeps the product fresh.

If you're looking for almonds with a subtle cocoa (not milk chocolate) hint then this is for you. But have a drink handy.

Can I just tell you right off the bat, this product is utterly amazing! Ever since I lost 180 pounds on the Atkins low-carb diet in 2004 eating healthy low-carb foods like almonds, I've been looking for ways to enhance my menus with something a little new while still keeping my carbs reduced. These nuts from Emerald certainly do the trick with a unique twist: DARK CHOCOLATE!

When I first saw these, I thought they were coffee beans. But upon closer examination, you realize these are almonds that have been dusted with dark chocolate cocoa and Splenda. That's right, NO SUGAR has been put in these bad boys. It's the best of both worlds--healthy AND tastes good! I'm adding these to my regular "must buy" list when I go shopping because you never want to be without these when you need a great-tasting snack. ENJOY!

I started eating almonds regularly after going on the South Beach Diet. I find them quite delicious . . . so delicious that I have to remind myself that I'm only supposed to eat 15 or so a day. Oh, well.

I could easily eat a handful . . . and still wouldn't feel like I had gotten enough flavor.

I had no idea what a cocoa roast almond would taste like, but I was pleasantly surprised that the taste was superb. It reminded me a little of eating a high quality fudge with lots of nuts in it.

But the nice surprise was that the cocoa taste lingered in my mouth so that I continued to enjoy the flavor long after the almonds were eaten. Even though the cocoa roasting adds some calories and some fat, I would be satisfied after eating far fewer of these almonds. I plan to buy and eat these on a regular basis.

Try them. I think you'll like them!

If you like chocolate that isn't too sweet, you'll be delighted by this lightly dusted cocoa almond snack. This is the type of snack you can't eat just one of, and would be perfect to serve at a dinner party too, as it is quite elegant.

I wasn't entirely sure what I would be getting when I ordered these, but I'm glad I did. There's just the right balance of salty and sweet -- the chocolate flavoring is perfect.  Plus, the container is great for stowing in a desk drawer or even in the car for an on-the-go treat.

The front of the label for these almonds from Emerald mentions two things that I am fond of: almonds and dark chocolate. I went in with hopes that combining two good things together would result in something better than the two separately. In this case the result is pretty good. While this is only mentioned on the product page (and not the actual container itself), the lid doubles as a measuring cup for a single serving. After having these over the last few days, here are my impressions.

While I like the taste (a lot!), it wasn't exactly what I was expecting. When I think of dark chocolate, I'm expecting a taste similar to a piece of Dove Dark Chocolate miniatures. It is a taste that is rich with a very mild sweetness. The coating on these almonds is a little bit sweeter than that. It's nowhere near milk chocolate, but like I said it wasn't exactly what I expected. That said these are still really good. The almonds themselves are great with only a minute amount of salt. With the chocolate and the natural flavor of almonds this is a sweet treat.

Who It's For: Disciplined people looking for a sweet, but healthy snack.

Suggested Use: A single serving makes a great between meals snack. If your stomach starts to rumble around 10 a.m., this will bridge the gap to lunch. I have the canister in a desk drawer at work. Regardless of when/where/how you use them as snack, discipline and moderation are key.

Potential Improvements: The one thing that bugs me on these is that the 11 oz package does not divide evenly into 1.5 oz servings. It would seem like a 12 oz canister would have been easy enough.

Overall: This is a great tasting, healthy snack to enjoy in moderation.

This is an innovative concept.  Dust and roast the almonds in chocolate powder so you get the light taste of chocolate, without a heavy candy-coating of chocolate full of calories and sugar.  These almonds are crunchy, non-salted, and not too sweet with a hint of dark chocolate taste.  Only 1 gram of sugar per serving, with 3 g of dietary fiber.  So it meets the South Beach diet criteria.  6% Calcium, 8% Iron and 35% Vitamin E.  My family loved them and these disappeared too quickly.

For those people who enjoy eating chocolate w/ nuts, this is a great product that gives you a little bit of that taste w/ a lot less guilt. I enjoyed the product as did my Toddler. The nuts are dry w/ a dusting of chocolate that isn't too sweet to the taste.

It's good that it gives only hint of the chocolate. I wouldn't say it is addictive as some of the other flavors like the standard smoked seasoned ones, but it is enjoyable. The coating is pretty dry and doesn't come off on your fingers either, so eating it w/ your fingers is pretty mess free.

I am torn: 4 stars or 5 stars? I decided on 5 stars:

- The taste is great! If you are Coke or Pepsi drinker, then they may not be sweet enough for you. I am not, hence I and my entire family enjoyed their subtle chocolaty flavor.

- The nutritional content is not bad at all, except artificial flavoring, which I would never notice on my taste buds if it was not written.

All-in-all -- absolutely delicious and filling snack!

The almonds are crispy and delicious, and cocoa powder gives a nice chocolate flavor without being all thick and gummy like the nuts with an actual chocolate coating.

So the taste is good, the crunchiness is nice, and apparently they're just about as good for you as normal almonds.

I'd get them again.

If you are looking for a nutty snack that is not too sweet, this might be for you. My husband and I both tried them. He thinks this is more of a 5 star item. He liked the fresh nuts with just a bit of a cocoa taste, and though I liked them, I would say they are maybe in the three star category, because I was hoping for something slightly sweeter. We both liked that the coating was not a "come off in your hand" kind of variety that makes you look for something to wipe your hands on.

We both enjoyed them though I don't know that I would purchase them for myself again. Nothing wrong with them, just not sweet enough for me. I would however purchase for my husband.

As with any nut product, they are high in fiber and the good kind of fat, but you don't want to dip into too many if you are dieting as they run 150 calories for 1/4 cup, so portion accordingly.

I like almonds, and I loooove chocolate! Even dark chocolate. The problem is that putting the two together doesn't create an especially healthy or low-calorie snack. But these almonds aren't dipped in melted chocolate, they are dusted with a dark chocolate cocoa powder. In theory, that sounds like the best of both worlds...

... but to me, it tasted kinda like they were covered in dirt. Well, maybe not dirt, but not exactly sweetness either. And that may not quite satisfy those of us with a BIG sweet tooth. But after subsequent servings I grew to like them much more. I passed some around the office and the reception was much more positive than my initial taste test (of course, it might have just been because it was free food...). And once I decided to share them with the kids all I had left was an empty container.

So, as I sniff the pleasant aroma of roasted almonds and dark chocolate from an empty container, I must admit it makes a good snack for the office, although 4 stars is a bit generous. Even a small serving is mostly satisfying and low-calorie enough that I don't have to feel guilty. My biggest complaint, however, is with the lid. It just won't screw on tight. Every time I tighten it, the threads slip and it's loose again. Maybe the next container will be better...

I really thought I would love these. I like all kinds of nuts, roasted and otherwise. I like all kinds of chocolate, really like dark chocolate. Heck, I even love mocha roast coffees and dark beers described as nutty. But I don't love this product. Maybe it's just me. I understand it's not cocoa in the sense of a creamy coating, but rather it's a dry dusting that is not unhealthy. I understand it's dark cocoa. But I didn't like the taste. I will end up mixing these in with other trail mixtures.

If you havn't tried them, I'd maybe find a way to get a nibble somewhere before buying a four pack. You might love em. Or like me, you might be surprised.

but I guess I don't really love them together. The chocolate is not sweet at all (they also have no other flavor to them), which means I can only eat about three before I feel like their getting bitter.  It may be that their just too dark for me and they will not be too strong for someone else.  they would probably be good in a trail mix of some kind to give your taste buds some flavor variety.

I'm not a huge almond fan but I can like them.  I am a huge dark chocolate fan so when I saw this product I thought "Great".  One serving is approximately 25-27 almonds I measured and contains little "bad fat" and lots of protein and fiber for the amount.  The cocoa appears to be baked on and not merely sprinkled or the nuts rolled in it because it clings really well to the product.  The almonds are nice and big, well roasted, and taste just like you'd expect from an almond.  There in lay my greatest complaint: the cocoa wasn't very noticeable.  Was it dark cocoa?  Maybe but because the taste was subtle it was a bit difficult for me to tell.  In a world where we need to be eating healthier I know that we might have to change how we eat chocolate but unless almonds are one of your favorite nuts, try one of the many other brands of cocoa-covered or yogurt-covered varieties all in easy to open and reseal containers.  So far, the cocoa-dusted walnuts are my favorite.

The almonds are fresh and the addition of the dark chocolate flavor makes for an addicting taste. Almonds in limited quantities as opposed to finishing the entire container can be quite healthy. The problem with these is that it is near impossible to stop eating them. Please note that these are not chocolate covered almonds but rather almonds with a covering of dark chocolate powder. They are healthy and quite delicious.

I think I made a big mistake getting a container of these Cocoa Roast Almonds, because I cannot stop eating them. Everyone I've shared them with (shared 1 or 2 almonds, I'm keeping the rest for me!) gives me a look like they are willing to wrestle me to the ground to get the rest of the container.

Very subtle chocolate flavor (I got the Dark Chocolate) that vaguely makes you think of brownies. Not overly sweet, but definitely not bitter the way one worries about [dark chocolate] cocoa powder.

I'd give six stars if Amazon had them.

The cap of the container is supposed to be used for determining a single serving, but I treated the entire 11 ounce container as a single serving.

Pros
Excellent tasting
Fresh
Nice hint of chocolate flavoring

Cons
Package slightly hard to open. Had to tear wrapping from the top then tear it completely off the top before I could open it.
Inner seal was a little hard to remove with my fingers.
Not vacuum packed as I thought it might be.

Review
A pleasent surprise on my first tasting. Cocoa flavoring is not overpowering. Nuts are firm and easy to chew. The 11 oz package is a good size plus the shape is very good. I like the large indentations on two sides which make the outer container easy to hold with one hand. Seems to be one of those "can't stop eating it" kinds of foods. It's really that good. The serving size according to the package is 11 however I expect to finish the product in 3 to 4 servings. The handy screw top is nice too and would seem to keep this item fresh between servings. This is something I would order fairly often and keep in my house to share with anyone who drops by for a visit. I also found the product information on the back easy to read against a light green background.

I found these delicious and highly addictive... you may not be able to eat just one!

According to the wrapper, the Serving Size is one ounce (about 1/4 cup) and there are 11 servings in the container. Nutritional information includes these facts:
Total Fat 13g (Saturated Fat 1g; Polyunsaturated Fat 3g; Monounsaturated Fat 8g)
Sodium 25mg
Potassium 210mg
Total Carbohydrate 6g (Dietary Fiber 3g; Sugars 1g)
Protein 6g

Ingredients: Dry Roasted Almonds, Modified Food Starch (potato), Natural & Artificial Flavors, Cocoa Powder (processed with alkali), Salt, Acesulfame Potassium, Sucralose.

Allergy information: This product is processed on equipment that also processes other tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soy, milk and sesame seeds.
Wow, I loved these!  Almonds with a rich dark chocolate taste but with minimal added carbs.  Nice touch with the cap being able to measure out a standard serving.  A great healthy snack.

I like these.  Like the packaging too.  These are not chocolate dipped, but cocoa powdered.  And the flavor is cocoa, not chocolate.  Very sweet.  Probably good because a few go along way.  Very flavorful.
