I still rate this product 5 stars because I don't think my personal tastes and preferences are what matters. I think this product is great for the market I perceive it to be aimed at.

If you're going to get a sugar cereal it ought to at least taste great, so you're getting some pleasure in exchange for the unhealthiness. But this cereal doesn't taste very good. Can't see any reason to recommend it.

This cereal is sweeter than the name might imply.  But if one reads the ingredients and sees sugar, honey and molasses as number two, five, and six one might guess as much.  The molasses gives it a different flavor than the other "honey nut" type cereals I have tasted.  While I didn't care too much for it, others might - tastes vary widely between different people.

Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey
I shared this with my kids, as they are the cereal connoisseurs of the family. The results were split: two for buying again and two for trying something else.
The pro to this cereal is that is stays crunchy in milk until you finish even if you leave it for a minute. The taste is primarily of sweetness/honey flavor. We really didn't taste much of the nutty flavor. This cereal reminded us of the sugariness waffle crisp without the syrup flavor.
For myself, I just didn't care for the flavor or texture. There really wasn't a flavor other than the sweetness and by the end of the bowl I had to force the last spoonful in. It was kind of blah.
If the kids really want to eat this I would buy it for them but I don't think it will be on the top of the shopping list.

What a delicious breakfast cereal! These aren't dry oatey O's covered in honey and nut like I had anticipated they would be, but rather they're a crunchy, dark-amber, honey-corn O, covered in little nut particles.

Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey cereal stays crispy [enough] in milk. I turned this box into two after work bowls one night, and then two breakfast bowls the next morning. So they're good enough to be considered a multi-bowl-per-sitting cereal.

As far as the name goes, "Crunchy Nut" sounds more like a variety of something than a proper cereal name, so maybe they'll change that down the line, but I like them, I'm sure kids will like them and if you're in the mood for a crisp, tasty, moderately sweet cold cereal then I think you will like them too.

Like many other reviewers, I'd have to agree that the cereal is very good. It tastes like Cheerios with a sweet, nutty taste. However, it has 10g of sugar per serving...that's quite a bit for cereal. I actually munch on it as a dessert rather than eating it for breakfast. Just like most things that taste good, it's definitely not good for you, but it's a good little treat in moderation.

This cereal reminds me of Corn Bran.  I don't know if that stuff is still around.  This cereal was okay.  I liked that it wasn't super sweet.  If you like more of the honey taste, then this isn't the cereal.  I would buy this cereal if it was on a good special, but it wasn't my favorite.  The texture was a lot like cheerios, but it didn't taste as sweet as honey nut cheerios.  I compared the ingredients to that of our other cereals.  It wasn't too bad.  Still had the carbs etc.  A lot like the standard box of cereal.

This might be one of my new favorite cereals.  I was amazed at how crunchy the cereal stayed, even after being in milk for several minutes.  It was a great sweet taste to it.  I'm guessing by how great it tastes, it can't be extremely healthy, but I like it anyway!

Loved it. The flavor was great, nice nuttiness, just all around really great. My wife has taken to eating it dry as a snack instead of popcorn! Sugar content is a bit high, but we don't plan to eat this every day.

This isn't anything really exciting and it's a little sweet for me, but the kids like it.
It's relatively healthy and it stays crunchy. I'll continue to buy this for the kids.

Lots of reviewers have mentioned how this cereal is similar to Honey Nut Cheerios, and I agree, EXCEPT, I think this is much crunchier.

I like crunch, and I also like a sweet breakfast cereal, so I was happy with the taste and consistency.

Now, if you don't like sweet in the morning, these may be a little much for you. In addition to sugar, they also have honey and molasses. The sugar CONTENT however is only 10g. I say "only" because there are some cereals out there, which claim fiber and other health benefits, which have more sugar than these. (Example, frosted Mini-Wheats--12g of sugar. And a certain bran with raisin cereal, 23g of sugar!)

Much as I liked these, I wouldn't eat them every single day, because I think the sweet factor might be too much (even for me :>) over time. But they're a nice every-few-days choice.

One caution: Peanuts. If you're allergic, be aware that these contain peanuts.

Is this the rich man's Peanut Butter Cap'n Crunch? Or the poor man's Honey Nut Cheerios? It tastes like the former, but looks like the latter. My wife and I dug into this one evening and, 24 hours later, have demolished it. It's not very "peanut-y," except for the artificial peanut flavor (despite, strangely, the flecks of peanut glued onto each "o"). If you're looking for sugar and aren't discriminatory in your brand names, it should satisfy your craving. Om nom nom!

I love cereal and eat it for breakfast almost every day. I've tried just about everything in the breakfast aisle, but I've never found anything to rival my two stand-by favorites, plain yellow-box Cheerios and Honey Bunches of Oats. I figured these Kellogg's Crunchy Nut O's were worth a shot, however, as they had both honey and peanuts going for them.

Boy, was I disappointed. I thought this cereal was much, much too sweet, and felt that it left a bad corn aftertaste in my mouth. My husband, a huge fan of Honey Nut Cheerios, didn't like this either. After a few bowls, the box sat untouched in my cupboard for months until I finally threw it out. Definitely not for us!

Honestly, it wasn't that good. I didn't finish the box before I moved on. The coating separated in liquid. It didn't taste too bad but also did not taste particularly nutritious. I prefer cereals made of whole grains

I like the texture of this cereal, and I'm a big fan of peanuts, but this just seems a little bland to me.  It's not a bad taste, just not really very strong to me, so it's kinda like eating semi-sweet slightly flavored little crunchy pieces of cardboard or something.  If it had a stronger flavor or maybe another flavor in addition to what it has I think I would enjoy it more.

I found this cereal so uninteresting that I almost forgot to review it, because I'd almost forgotten that I'd eaten it. It is not a bad cereal, just not memorable at all. With so many great cereals on the market, I don't see why this one is being offered. Just ignore this cereal and it will likely go away eventually.

This cereal is good, if unoriginal. My four factor review is below:

Crunch: 4/5
Flavour: 4/5
Nutrition: 4/5
Value: 4/5

I am not typically fond of very sweet cereals, so that opinion affects this review.  This cereal has a taste somewhat like peanut butter.  It is shaped liked Cheerios, but tastes a bit like Captain Crunch.  However, the cereal is overly sweet on its own and I didn't care for it.  After the initial try, I mixed it half and half with plain Cheerios and liked it quite well.

This is not a cereal I would personally buy, as it's overly sugary for my taste. Also, it's probably not as versatile as some others - added fresh fruit might not go well with this cereal. More importantly, for health, this is certainly not one of the more impressive (look at the ingredient list).

When I first saw this product all I could think of was another of the Honey Nut cereals that we all love.  I was hoping beyond hope that this wouldn't be a dud as some copies are.  Well this is the best Honey Nut Crunch cereal I have had the delight to enjoy.  It's not as sweet as I thought it would be but is just perfect.  It has a nice crunch that stays well with the milk until you are finished.  Yay, no soggy cereal here.  All in all, this is a fantastic cereal with great flavor and healthy to boot that comes at a price that is very affordable especially with the way the economy is making us pay more for less it seems lately.  You won't be disappointed here.

If you like a sweet, slightly nutty flavored cereal, then you'll like this new Kellogg's Crunchy Nut cereal.

Nutrition Facts:
Serving Size: 3/4 cup
Servings Per Box: 11

Total Fat: 1g (cereal only)
Cholesterol, 0mg
Sodium: 125mg
Potassium: 25mg
Carbohydrate: 23g
Dietary Fiber: 2g
Sugars: 10g
Other Carbohydrates: 11g
Protein: 2g

Ingredients: Yellow Corn Meal, Sugar, Corn Bran, Peanuts, Honey, Molasses, Salt, Whole Oat Flour, Caramel Color, Baking Soda, Annatto Extract Color, Ascorbic Acid (Vitamin C), Niacinamide, Redced Iron, Zinc Oxide, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride (Vitamin B6), Riboflavin (Vitamin B2), Thiamin Hydrochloride (Vitamin B1), Vitamin A Palmitate, BHT (preservative), Foic Acid, Vitamin D, Wheat Starch, Vitamin B12.

This cereal holds up well in milk and also is tasty right out of the box. Also would be good in trail mix and a quick cookie bar recipe.

This cereal would be better, in my humble opinion, if it were less sweet.  When I was a kid I liked really sweet cereal but as an adult, I've grown out of it.  Although I enjoyed the crunchiness of it.  And the nutty taste was not bad at all, simply too sweet.  Now, that's just my personal opinion.  If you like sweet cereal, this may suit you fine.

If you want a cereal that has lots of fiber and protein, and will keep you full for hours.... this is not that cereal.

If you want a cereal that is just plain delicious, to be eaten for the pure joy of eating it.... this is not that cereal.

If you want a cereal that tastes like stale kix rolled in the crumbs of some honey roasted peanuts, and is satisfying in neither taste nor quality.... then this is the breakfast cereal for you.

I think i've made myself clear.

Not a regular cereal eater but I found this to be a tasty treat. Sweet, nutty, and a little bit salty which is a great combination.

The 11 oz box of cereal did not last long at all.
Tastes a lot like honey nut cheerioes but not quite as good. stay fairly crunchy after adding milk. Kids liked them too.

I wasn't a huge fan of the taste of Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey cereal. The taste is redolent of corn puffs, with a hint of Multi-grain Cheerios. Too much honey on the front end, with corn notes that are slightly overpowering in the finish. The bouquet has distinct peanut notes which is unsurprising as peanuts (which actually aren't a nut) are the main nut in the cereal. Somehow this combines however, into a cereal that is at once both, overly sweet and mealy.

I would also add that the price, $30 + $8 shipping comes out to about .88 an ounce. Compare that to major grocery chains and other cereals, such as Crunchy Nut Roasted O's at .38/oz, or Honey nut cheerios at .28/oz, and its clear that these are horribly overpriced.

Also, when it says nuts (and I realize I'm being a stickler), I really expect it to contain treenuts, like almonds, cashews, etc. Peanuts are a legume, a groundnut, and technically a bean. Not a nut.

As advertised, Crunchy Nut smells and tastes like peanuts -- something I don't find very appetizing when mixed with milk and ingested in the morning. I eat peanuts with beer at bars, not at breakfast. I'm guessing that the honey is supposed to cut the flavor of the peanuts, but it is hardly detectable.

People will of course disagree with my thoughts on peanuts in the morning, but let's take a look at the side of the box.

To keep the calories per serving at 100 (without milk), Kellogg's has shrunk the serving size to 3/4 of a cup. That means with milk, a bowl of Crunchy Nut is going to be 300 calories or slightly more. So if you go back for a second bowl, that's a pretty high caloric breakfast. Further, the base ingredient is yellow corn meal, which doesn't have much nutritional value.

While there are certainly much more unhealthy cereals out there, in this day and age I'd like to see a more healthy, lower caloric cereal.

I liked the crunch and held up well in milk but there was no nutty flavor and felt it was too sweet.
To me, this is more of a snack type than a cereal. Even my husband who eats a cereal daily said there's just 'too much in it." I will just finish the box as a snack but probably would pass it in the cereal aisle.

Honey Nut Cheerios (HNC) is a good cold cereal if you're concerned about high Cholesterol and want more fiber. Kellogg's Crunchy Nut (CN) tries to imitate HNC and doesn't quite get there. But it's not too far off.

They're both tasty. CN is a bit too sweet for my taste (of course, you might prefer it sweeter) but it only has a little more sugar than HNC. Must be the way the honey is glazed on CN.

HNC is made with Oats, CN with Corn and some Oats. Oats are supposed to be better for Cholesterol lowering, so HNC gets the edge.

HNC and CN both have 2 grams of fiber. More than most cold cereals so that's good. (for comparison, Oatmeal has 4 grams).

HNC has almonds, CN has peanuts. I think Almonds are supposed to be a bit healthier but peanuts aren't bad. Small edge to HNC.

Summing up, when i eat cold cereal I prefer HNC to CN but CN is acceptable.

Think of this cereal as a puffed (like Rice Krispies) version of Honey Nut Cheerios, with small pieces of peanut in each O for added crispy-ness and nutty flavor.

I say these Os are "crispy" as they're puffed, airy kernels (like Rice Krispies), not "crunchy" like corn flakes or the like.

I make the distinction between crispy and crunchy because being the puffed and airy kernels that these are, they have the characteristics of soaking up the milk over time and becoming more dense and taking on a more chewy consistency, but still also holding on to a level of their crispiness. Whereas crunchy cereals tend to get soft and or mushy the longer they're in milk.

As to the flavor, these certainly hold-up to the Nut and Honey claim. The sweetness of the nut and honey flavor holds all the way through to staying with you awhile in after-taste (in a good way). I enjoy these Os.

Parents concerned about healthy content and sugar might want to be more mindful about this cereal, but otherwise it's a tasty treat.

Upon first taste, I thought that I was really going to like this cereal. I thought that it was another version of Quaker's Honey Graham O's Cereal, 12-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 12). As such, I was pretty excited. I mean, I like Oh!s. It's one of my favorite cereals.

Then the aftertaste caught me. And made me start looking at the ingredient list. I am guessing that it is the corn bran that they put in here, but the aftertaste is somewhere between burned popcorn and Honey Smacks (you know...the one with Dig 'Em Frog). Not so much ideal.

If you don't mind the aftertaste, it's pretty reasonable cereal. There are only around 100 calories per 3/4 cup serving, so it's not terribly bad for you like many oversweetened cereal. I think that this is probably the vanguard of an effort by Kellog's to sweeten their cereals with honey, but they haven't quite gotten it figured out just yet. Unlike the other reviewers, I didn't think that it was super sweet, but it certainly was sweeter than my normal cereal.

ALLERGY WARNING: THIS PRODUCT CONTAINS PEANUTS.

Harkius

This stuff tasted like (insert favorite negative adjective that Amazon won't print). I like most cereals but I couldn't put this stuff down, tasted like cardboard something with a half stale texture. Hate to throw 3/4 box of cereal away, we'll see if the birds will eat it - I have my doubts.

Kellog's Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey cereal is (at least it seems to be that it is) designed to be a competitor of Post's Honey Bunches of Oats and Honey Nut Cheerios. This is a good cereal with a slightly stronger taste than the Post cereal, but it is close enough to be of interest to fans of both. To me it tasted like a combination of the two - a very interesting combination.

Just as the description implies, these are very much like Frosted Flakes with specks of peanuts and glazed honey. That said, there isn't much difference since the days of Tony the Tiger, but if you really like them, this is easily a five-star product. Of course, this cereal can't be good for a diabetic or one allergic to peanuts (I am neither, or I wouldn't be writing a review). As a matter of fact, having just eaten a bowl prompted me to type this up! (This is my third review on a food product, by the way.)

Eat this in moderation. A new product but probably based on a highly successful product with bits of nut added to the mix. Enough said.
This cereal is very tasty and was liked by children and adults who tried it which is not an easy accomplishment.  It stays crunchy in milk for a while and is a nice twist on an old cereal.

This product is a mix between honey o's with flavor bits stuck to them. I'd rather go for plain o's or something with a bit more flavor. They did have a good crunch and lasted a good while in milk, but I do not feel they bring anything new to the cereal market.

Initially, it tastes pretty good, but if you wait a minute, it has a sort of ash tray aftertaste. That said, it does stay crispy, but if the flavor isn't great, I'm not sure how much that will matter to you.

23 carbs per serving - not Atkins friendly

Whether breakfast on a Saturday morning or even as a late night snack, what hits the spot better than a big bowl of cereal? With dozens of varieties lining the wall of any given grocery aisle, the real question here is whether Kellog's Crunchy Nut is better than the competition and worth the price.

Combining the shape and texture of Cheerios with the flavor of a much sweeter treat, the Roasted Nut and Honey cereal is a winner for anyone who likes an intense honey taste and a strong crunch. Soggy cereal - the bane of any breakfast - isn't an issue here, as it stays firm and crunchy for more than enough time to finish off a full bowl. The edges of each piece are a little sharp, but they don't shred the mouth like Peanut Butter Crunch or similar breakfast cereals.

For the cereal lover with a sweet tooth who doesn't want their breakfast to get soggy, Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey is a great choice and well worth trying out.

Honey nut Cheerios are very similar to this product except these are darker and sweeter. Kellogs is just trying to put out a better product but I think there was nothing wrong with Honey Nut Cheerios & I prefer them to the Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey cereal from Kellogs.

I'm always looking for a good breakfast cereal and there are so many on the market now that are both delicious and nutritious that it's hard to choose.  This one I had trouble keeping away from my 14 and 11 year old daughters so that I could review it.  It's not *too* high in sugar and calories and contains a pretty good amount of fiber- two of the key things I look for in addition to taste.  My only knock against the cereal is the same as all of these cereals with "bits" of nuts attached to the cereal, the nuts are too small to really have any texture left and there's not enough of them to really taste. If the box hadn't said there were nuts in there, I would have never known.  I prefer cereals with whole nuts or at least slivers of nuts.

It's hard to say that I "like" Crunchy Nut cereal. It basically tastes like Cheerios, with some nutty sugar sprinkled on top. It's not a super healthy cereal, it's not particularly original, but the taste and crunch are fine.

I wound up sprinkling my Crunchy Nut cereal onto desserts to make crunchy treats, rather than eating it as a cereal. My go-to cereal is plain old raisin bran, and I don't see that changing anytime soon.

So as a dessert item, Crunchy Nut cereal is very good. As a breakfast item, I think I'm fine with throwing my own sugar on my Cheerios when the mood strikes me. I don't really need that to come prepacked for me.

At first I didn't like this cereal much, but because it reminded me a lot of Waffle Crisp cereal, I started to enjoy it more. Then, when I went through my first box, I realized how much I liked Crunchy Nut!
It's a great breakfast item with a hint of honey and lots of nutty taste, and has a delicious aftertaste that, like I mentioned already, reminded me of Waffle Crisp.

Great new cereal!

Very tasty. I like Honey-Nut Cheerios, and these are very similar, but a little less sweet and more nutty. Of course those with peanut allergies/sensitivities will need to avoid. I shared them with my wife, who generally doesn't like cereal except Corn Flakes, and she liked it a lot.

Our whole family loved this cereal, even the 3-yr old asked for seconds. You could taste the nuts but there are no nut pieces. Nuts were completely blended in.
Would buy again.

These are obviously closely related to Honey Nut Cheerios, but get less soggy and have a somewhat nuttier flavor. I haven't tried them side by side, but I think they're also a bit sweeter. I like the Cheerios, but I think I'd choose these for the consistency and texture if I were picking on taste alone. That said, if you LOVE Honey Nut Cheerios, I'd just stick with those.

This cereal reminded me a lot of Quaker's Oh's. It's a lot lighter and less substantial than Oh's, however, and has a weird aftertaste (a bad aftertaste). The cereal is made with rice and corn instead of wheat, so it doesn't really make you feel full. The roasted nut and honey taste is somehow adulterated so that it simply does not taste good in your mouth. Calorically speaking, the folks at Kellogg's did a good job, and the cereal makes a better study snack than breakfast cereal, if not for the horrible aftertaste.

Steer clear of this product. Check out Quaker's Oh's instead.

Even if you're on a diet, there is no need to torture yourself with unfilling food that tastes bad.

One star.

Is it me? or does this cereal have the lingering taste of corn pops? They even turn soggy like corn pops. I do like corn pops, however a cereal that looks like a 'cheerio' and tastes kinda like a corn pop with a not so pleasant aftertase didnt do it for me.

Sweet without being overpoweringly so, Kellogg's Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey is a cereal that both kids and adults will like.  It has a nice flavor, and it provides the energy boost I need to get up and going in the morning.  I would highly recommend this cereal to anyone who likes a breakfast that leaves one full and satisfied without making them feel bloated.

This is a decent enough corn-based breakfast cereal, but frankly I found it rather bland. It's sweet enough, and it's a relatively low-calorie food, but compared to other oat-based or multi-grained cereals that I like, it doesn't have a very distinctive flavor.  I could taste the honey, but the nuts are a bit too subtle.  I kept comparing this cereal unfavorably to Quaker Oh's, which are crunchier, sweeter, and have a more satisfying flavor.

I like this cereal, but then again I like almost any kind of cereal. The product definitely lives up to its name and stays crunchy in milk; it is great as a dry snack, too. Flavor-wise, it reminded my of a cross between Honey Nut Cheerios and Ohs; there was a nice balance between the roasted nut and honey flavors. I'll buy this if I ever see it on sale; otherwise, I'll stick with the generic (but just as flavorful) cereals that cost much less.

My kids really enjoyed this cereal, but it wasn't quite what I expected. I assumed from the cereal's shape and packaging design that this product would be like Honey-Nut Cheerios. It's not like that at all. It's not an oat cereal. The cereal tastes more like Pops, but shaped like Cheerios. It's a pretty tasty cereal, and health-wise it seems pretty typical for the breakfast cereal market.

I liked the crunch but it was a bit too sweet for me. I like my cereals low on sugar and the calories that this had from sugars was more than I cared for. The taste was ok. I wouldn't buy it again. Glad I got to try it for free.

I like the version of this cereal that is made by the competitor of this cereal and eat it periodically. I tried this hoping to find a very similar product that I could buy on sale if the other wasn't. The other option was a cereal that was so different that it would become a new option for me.

The taste was adequate. The nuts were almost nonexistent....at least to the naked eye. They may have been rolled in dust, but there were definitely no pieces on the side of the cereal.

The color of the cereal was awful, reminding me of the color of what babies leave in a used diaper. It was not at all appealing. In addition, there is a lot of sugar in this cereal.

For the above reasons, I wouldn't bother to buy this in the future.

First of all, i was really happy to see that this new Kellog's cereal was all natural. I try to stay away from cereals that are more chemical compounds than foodstuffs I can actually recognize. So i was happy to give this cereal a try.

I didn't hate it, but I didn't like it either. It had a burned popcorn aftertaste that I really didn't care for, but the actual cereal itself wasn't too bad. It was something to take a bite of here or there as a dry snack. It didn't seem to work too well with milk.

That being said, my rabbits were willing to kill for a bite of Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey as if they were crack addicts looking for a fix. At one point, one of them snuck into the kitchen, jumped up on the counter, pushed the box off, jumped down onto the box and then began dragging it to her cage. Something about the smell of the cereal just drove them into voracious eating. Maybe Kellog would do better selling this as a pet food treat rather than a human one.

I admit that I don't like most breakfast cereals, they are usually too sweet, too much one flavor (like Cinnamon) or too "healthy" (i.e. no flavor). But this one, I do like!

It has a great combination of flavors, the roasted nut and honey are just right. They stay crunchy in milk, but are not too hard to eat. They taste good as a dry snack as well. I didn't feel they needed any added sugar or anything other than milk.

The one bad thing is that the box is smaller compared to other cereals, so the value vs. price isn't as good. But overall, I do like this cereal and have already bought another box.

We eat a lot of cold cereal for afternoon snacks, instead of for breakfast, and this cereal fits in with its not-too-sweet not-too-peanut flavor and crunch.  But it's also not-too-interesting and not-too-memorable.  I would never crave it and don't plan on purchasing it if I see it on the grocery store shelf.  Ho hum.

The flavor of the cereal is pleasantly toasty. It's a strong flavor but not overpowering. They stay crunchy in milk for some time and the flavor of the left over milk at the bottom of the bowl, an important part of any breakfast, is nicely sweet.

Two down sides. For me, the cereal sat heavily in my stomach for the better part of the morning. A friend who used the same amount of cereal and milk didn't experience that, so it's probably different for everybody.

Secondly, several times as I was eating, I found a clump of compressed peanut bits and dust. It was a very unpleasant contrast of texture and flavor with the sweetened milk and the rest of the cereal.
This cereal didn't last long in our house. Within a couple days it was gone - good, crunchy and tasty!

I got these expecting them to pretty much be Honey Nut Cheerios, but was pleasantly surprised.  They had a much more distinct nut flavor and actually tasted more like Cap'n Crunch Peanut Butter but without the kind of waxy coating that cereal has.  Overall, the flavor was good (could have been a bit stronger), the texture was great, and it was very fresh and crunchy.  The reason I didn't give it five stars was simply due to value.  The box is quite small and the price is not.  I'm not sure how many servings the box claims, but I'd say you can expect three cereal bowls full and that is about it out of a single box.

Pretty good for a sweetened cereal, tastes a bit like a sweeter version of Honey Nut Cheerios, but not too sweet.

I went to have a second bowl the third day we had them, but they were gone. That's a pretty good vote of approval from a variety of ages (two parents, 9 year old, 17 and 19.)

The remained crunchy, held up to milk, and had a nice bit of substance, a bit more than Cheerios.

This is tasty cereal.  It's kind of like Honey Nut Cheerios but a heck of a lot better! I'm a bit stanege since I don't really eat cereal the traditional way. I eat it "dry", sometimes strait from the box! I like this so much I went and bought three more boxes to put in my pantry!. I usually have some as a snack, as it's much better than chips and candy. The other day I ate some while watching a movie, instead of popcorn. This is very tasy stuff indeed and I hope Kelloggs keeps producing it. Hopefully enough people will like and buy it so it won't get discontunued.

This Kellogg's Crunchy Nut is very nutty. The cereal is good, slightly sweet and has lots of flavor. But perhaps too much peanutty flavor for a cereal. We like it best in a dry mix with other cereals, nuts, pretzels and things like that.

I agree with some of the other reviewers that this cereal is definitely on the sweet side. If you are looking more for flavor than health benefits, or just a sweet treat for your kids, then by all means there is nothing wrong with that. Just please don't think that these are anything close to Cheerios, because they are not. These are much, much sweeter and more tasty, in my opinion. The packaging and amount of product was typical for cereal - nothing out of the ordinary.
Liked the taste and they held up well in milk. I also tried the other variety, Crunchy Nut Golden Honey Nut, 14.1-Ounce (Pack of 4). Preferred this one by an edge.

Crunchy Nut cereal is definitely tasty. For me, it's just a little too nondescript. If I want a healthy cereal, I go towards a GoLean and add some raisins to jazz it up. If I want to splurge with a little sugar I'll hit the Cinnamon Toast Crunch. I thought this Crunchy Nut might fall in between and allow for a healthy, compromised, third option. For very little Fiber and Protein (2g each), I needed to be more excited to dig in. But it's just - meh.

I couldn't go as low as three-stars because it is tasty and nutty, I just don't think it's found a spot in my regular cereal rotation. If you don't focus on getting some protein or fiber out of your cereal, than this might be an option for you.

We had been eyeballing this on the shelf for a couple weeks at the local grocery store and were thrilled to get it to review. My favorite cereals are Honey Nut Cheerios, Honey Bunches of Oats, or Crispix. If it is my birthday or a camping trip and I am going to indulge in a sweet cereal I prefer Frosted Flakes. Cereal tends to be a sweet breakfast treat, and not a staple in our home, so I can overlook the nutrition facts.

Probably the best way I could describe Kellogg's Crunchy Nut is "greasy Kix." It left a funky aftertaste and slime on my tongue. The flavor, even before the aftertaste, wasn't good, though it was not the most horrible cereal in the world. It was edible so I gave it an one star more than something... inedible. My son thought it was ok, though not a favorite, but this seems to be packaged as an "adult" cereal so his vote doesn't count. I was done after my first bowl and let him finish the rest over the course of two weeks. This is unusual in my house as we usually go to blows on who gets the last bowl of cereal. Even my son did not ask to repurchase!

Unfortunately this failed for me. Sorry Kellogg's!

I was really pleasantly surprised by this cereal. I eat cereal almost every day so I'm a big fan and very picky about what I eat. I prefer cereals that are actually good for me (like the Kashi stuff), but I never compromise on taste. A lot of cereals nowadays either taste like cardboard or are too sweet. Surprisingly enough, this cereal is delicious, keeps me energized for average or above average compared to my other cereals, and is not too sweet at all.

If you've ever had Oreo O's it reminds me of that flavor EXACTLY but more nutty instead of chocolatey, and not quite as sweet. I know that sounds crazy, but if you eat one after the other I think you'll agree with me.

Anyway, if you're a fan of peanut butter and cereals that are a bit sweet and crunchy, you'll really enjoy this one.

This is a really tasty cereal that has a nice nutty taste and that stays crunchy and doesn't get soggy in milk.  That being said, they are void of any nutritional value.  I usually try to buy cereals that have less sugar and a lot more fiber, and these don't fit the bill in either way. If you don't mind that and want a tasty cereal that is even good enough to snack on on its own (without milk), then I'd recommend giving them a try.

This cereal is a great compromise for everyone in the family - sweet and very much like cheerios for those of us that like kids cereals, and healthy for my boyfriend that loves bran and granola. Great buy!

It takes real innovation to start with corn and sugar to put together scrumptious miniature glazed doughnuts (mmmm ... doughnuts). The doughnuts of this cereal are about the size of Cheerios, and surprisingly have the same calorie content despite being made of twenty-five percent sugar. It is real sugar, not the fake high-fructose stuff. To me, they taste a lot like Belgium waffles smothered in syrup.

As an experiment, I sprinkled some under my bird feeder. The regular birds ignored them. However, a flock of crows was attracted, probably by the orange color. The crows hung around for a while but lost interest without sampling the cereal. Squirrels then appeared to consume the cereal.

If they give a Nobel Prize in Food, I think that the designers of Crunchy Nut Roasted Nut and Honey deserve the trip to Sweden. I am still trying to decide whether this is a good snack or whether the rest of it should go under the bird feeder.

I really thought these would be a home run but found them bland and disappointing.  I would prefer to eat Quaker Ohs! And they are always cheapier.  So many good cereal choices out there to waste time on something boring.  Skip them.

My 4 year old likes this cereal, and I like giving it to him because it isn't garbage like frosted flakes, etc.

This cereal has a sweet taste without being too sweet. I don't think it has a noticeable "nut" taste to it like you might think. Definitely stays crisp in milk as others have indicated.

Serving size is .75 cups, 100 calories (less than Special K), 1g fat, 23g carbs (10g sugars), 2g dietary fiber, 2g protein.

No partially hydro oils, No high fructose corn syrup!

This seems to be Kellogg's answer to GM's Honey Nut Cheerios. The o's themselves resemble their cheerios counterparts except for the fact that they are studded with nuts so gives a more bumpy appearance. I think this is the most detailed observation I ever made on a cereal. It tastes great...better than cheerios..possibly due to its crunchy taste or the rugged structure tickling my taste buds in a different way. Whatever it is, it tastes great and I like it.

This cereal is real good. It is very crunchy and has tiny pieces of nuts and a hint of honey. They taste somewhat like honey nut cheerios but these will not get soggy as fast as the cheerios. They are probably as crunchy or more like apple jacks. I eat slow and by the time I finish the last bite is still crunchy. My favorite part of the cereal is the actual nut pieces on the cereal. It gives it that real nut flavor and bite. The nut flavor is not overwhelming either. Nor is the honey. It is a great balance between the two. If you like honey nut cheerios and the crunchiness of apple jacks then you will really like this cereal.

Sweet, Crunchy, holds up to milk, good for you, lowers cholesterol, flavor filled...what more could you want in a cereal? This is tastier than cheerios, with all the fiber and benefits! It doesn't get soggy in the milk and stays crunchy to the last bite! EVERYONE in my family loves this cereal! The kids, my husband and me! It is good for breakfast, lunch, dinner and a midnight snack!

How much can be said about a cereal?  Crunchy Nut lives up to it's name.  The O's are crunchy and covered with nuts.  Together they create a sweet taste with a little bit of saltiness.  It's a little on the sugary side, but still tasty for adults.  I swear this combination and taste had been done before in a long lost cereal of whose name I can't remember.

Far from a "perfect mix" of flavors, Cruchy Nut cereal is basically your average sugary cereal. Sadly, the sugar is about all you taste, there is no distinct honey or nut flavor, just sugar and crunch.

I can't imagine this is any healthier than Captain Crunch or Lucky Charms, and with those cereals, you actually have distinctive flavors. As an attempt to invade the Honey Nut Cheerios market, this is entirely a failure.

I have been able to germinate the seeds and ALL of them have popped. I live in Florida so putting them outside is not recommended. It's too hot. I have killed all that have popped by putting them outside. Even though it says they can take the heat, Florida sun is still too hot.

It's a good quality dog food, I recommend it. I have been giving it to my Yorkies since 2003. They used to have 2 options: chicken and pork, now they have turkey and pork. The ingredients are good, no by-products or grains and they are small bites, perfect for a little Yorkie's little mouth.

I have a Basset Hound and a medium mixed breed. They love these little chicken treats. I say "chicken" and they run to where the bag is kept. It's the one treat I can always get them to do their tricks for! I used to get them at a dog shop in a town over an hour away. Now, I get them on Amazon for a fraction of the price and they're delivered to my door every month (free shipping).
I have three little furballs and they LOVE these... They turn up their noses at a lot of treats, but not this one.  I just ordered the sweet potato and chicken treats,  I hope they like those too!!

My dog likes these, but isn't able to know any better.

The FDA warnings about dogs getting sick from Chinese-made chicken jerky are exactly this product. Maybe its safe, who knows. But I'm sure not going to find out. I'm never buying these again so long as they are made in China, period. I even threw 2 full bags in the trash because of this.

I thought I was doing my dogs good - paying what, $8 or $9 for one bag at the pet store. Then it was brought to my attention in a review here on amazon that this product is "made in China." Probably takes the slave labor there a month to earn that much. Will never buy this product again. Buy Healthy Happy Pet, Snook's instead.

Read the small print you will see the words 'MADE IN CHINA' - Ask yourself the question, would you eat a chicken product from China yourself? Be careful what you give your best friend, he trusts you. Now I am not one to want to hurt a companies products by bad mouthing them but I am not happy that I gave my dog chicken products from China, maybe by accident, I didn't see the small print (and it is VERY small print), as yourself the question too, if they made the words 'Made in China' bigger and on the front, would anyone buy this? If I am proven to be wrong I will be fair and remove this review but my Vitality chicken strips have the words 'MADE IN CHINA' in tiny print on the back.

Read the fine print.  Looks like its coming from your local farm, "cage free" organic, but the back states in very fine print - "Made in China".  What's wrong with that you might ask? Well you read the reports about chicken jerk breast and dogs dropping dead from it, specifically from treats made in china.  Never again.

My dog loved them but I was very disappointed when I saw the small print noting that the product was made in China.  I will not purchase this product again.  China has a dismal record regarding food safety and I am shocked that this company would produce this product in China.  At least let people know in your product description.

My 18-month Lab/Hound Mix is sometimes so stubborn and even detached, she often refuses to come when she's called. But when I take a chicken piece out from the package, she suddenly changes personality to be the most obedient, loving dog on earth. The best bribery item EVER!

I first came across these while buying a variety of treats and toys for my new Australian Shepherd puppy. The lack of fillers and bad stuff, and very simple (essentials only) ingredients list was impressive.

My dog loves these, and they have been very helpful for training purposes. As soon as he hears me open the bag, he comes and sits and waits in anticipation.

They are slightly dry, which may account for some slight constipation, but like anything, treats should be given in small quantities and in moderation.

My only real disappointment with these treats (and this apparently applies to all treats made by this company) is that they are made in China. While this isn't necessarily everything, if it were not for the great bullet point list of qualities these treats have, I would be looking for a US-manufactured product.

It is my understanding (based on statements by Dogswell) that their China-based facilities are highly inspected, etc. Hopefully, this is true, but there's no real way to know without flying to China to take a look.

Either way, if Dogswell were to move its
Manufacturing to the US, and keep or even improve its standards, I would give these treats a 5+ rating, as the concept is really great, and my puppy loves them.

Hopefully, the company will consider doing this soon.

My dog loves the heck out of these things.  She will eat them up like mad.  They are great from a natural and ingredients perspective.  I bought the large case and give her about two or three a night.  I found they by accident in a St. Augustine, Florida pet store.  I ordered on Amazon when I got home to Kansas City because she loved the first bag from florida so darn much.  Recommended.  Great for small dogs.  Not sure that a larger dog wouldn't wind up eating the thing whole.

At first, I was very hesitant to buy this treat for our dogs. I was expecting these to be hard, because they look very similar to the one I usually buy from PetSmart. The "hard" treat I'm used to break up in to tiny sharp pieces, and sometime choked our dogs making them cough up.

However, I took a leap of faith based on the great reviews on Amazon and bought the Chicken Breast flavor.

To my surprise, they were soft, and easy to bend and tear apart. The dogs seems to love them, and I was able to cut up 1 strip in to smaller bit-size to use them as a training incentive.

They will do anything for this treat, so it's a great product to our dogs motivated to do tricks for treats.

Highly Recommended!
This is my pets' favorite treat. Three dogs and two cats love this product, and it is a healthy one for my animals. One of my cats will not eat cat treats but loves this one.
These are crunchy rather than chewy.  I have to be careful not to give these too often as they seem to cause diarrhea (too much vitamin A?).  A great treat with excellent ingredients.
My dog has a Vitality habit!!  He cannot get enough of these!!  I don't know what they put in it, but it's healthy and he loves it!!

These treats are an absolute MUST for my dogs. They would probably stop eating dog food if I gave them more of these, but one nice aspect of these treats is it tells you on the back how many they can have (by dog's weight) daily. My two toy poodles will do just about anything, including chewing the bag open for me, to get these. Except, maybe, eating their dog food dinner first. Dogswell has these treats for vitality, but it  also has these treats for arthritis and other problems too. And besides chicken, they also have duck breast, which my dogs are crazy about. It's so convenient to get them thru Amazon, too.

I bought Dogswell Vitality for Dogs Chicken Breast for my finicky Boston Terrier after visiting my mom's and she gave him a dried chicken meat treat which he devoured. But I didn't like how brittle and hard the jerky treat was and made me concerned about him choking on it, even after breaking them into bite size pieces. I found Dogswell Vitality for Dogs at Target and gave it try after feeling through the bag that it wasn't as hard as the other dried meat treats with a slight bendable feel to it plus the disclaimer that the flaxseed and vitamins included helped dog's healthy eyes, skin and coat. The reason the disclaimer appealed to me is my dog has dry, flaky skin and occasionally gets dry patches.

I have tried all types of shampoos, both prescribed by the vet and store bought, even RX fish oil pills from my vet, which I disliked giving my dog because I don't like putting pill in mouth daily since I couldn't trick him by putting it on his food. I can say none of them worked near as well as Dogswell Vitality for Dogs Chicken Breast for his skin problems.

I've been given my dog, who weighs approx. 18 lbs., two to three strips a day broken into bite size pieces for nearly two months now. After about two weeks, I noticed the flaky dry skin scales weren't as noticeable and now it's barely noticeable at all. When I noticed the difference at two weeks I started ordering Dogswell Vitality for Dogs Chicken Breast through Amazon's Subscribe and Save program because I knew this treat was going to be a regular part of my dog's daily meal plan going forward and the program helps cut the cost of these expensive dog treats.

I do recommend in an additional to this treats zip bag, putting the treats in a second ziploc type bag to help keep the jerky strips from drying out further and loosing it small bit of moisture. I have found this keeps the jerky strips as moist as when you first open the bag. And even though these jerky treats aren't as brittle and hard as it's competitors, they are still brittle enough that I feel I need to break them into bite size pieces for my dog.

These are loved by my big (65 lb) dogs, but they do not chew them because they are small. The jerky type treats are very hard and give them stomach aches. The strips by this company are a better choice for big dogs.

I'm very disappointed when the company promised our offices they were a USA company, then I find out that they are actually manufacture in CHINA, and only distributed in the USA. I no longer will buy any Dogswell products. With so many dogs dying from dog products made in CHINA, it is essential to only buy from USA companies who have a GREAT track record. I no longer will buy dog products that are made in CHINA.

Write to the President and Founder of Dogswell, Marco Giannini

My dogs love these too and I never thought to check where they were made.  They look all healthy cage free chicken, omega 3s, blah blah blah.. Someone at the store brought this to my attention as she was looking for treats not made in china.  To my horror just about all dog treats are NOT even made in USA.  So sad and disappointing. ZERO stars!
My dog loves these, she can't wait to get one in the morning. I would definately buy these treat if I had a fussy dog who didn't like dog treats.

My dog got hooked on these pretty young, and now they're the only "treat" he'll eat. My mom had been giving them to her dog, and when he stayed over there he got a taste of them and went crazy. They seem to be relatively healthy, and we can make them last a long time. My dog is a wanderer, and the best way we've found to keep him close, is to give him a piece of one of these when we whistle and he comes home. Since we've gotten him trained, he always comes back to a whistle. He's a small dog so we usually only give him about 1/3 of one of these, and one bag will last us a month. If you do the subscription plan with Amazon, the price ends up being very reasonable.
My dog loves these and to buy them locally is too expensive.  These are shipped quickly and a lot cheaper too!!

We have purchased Dogswell for dogs
for many years, they keep our 12 year Old Peek-a-poo health and strong
it works wonders for us, and that all good

[...]

My boys just love them....they will dance for them soon as they hear the krinkle of the bag. I purchased them because my tiny toy poodle had a hip problem and didn't want to jump up on the sofa, after a week he was jumping with no problems!!!
Great product.  My dog thinks she is getting a treat and it is realy good for her.

Just what I had been looking for in a reward for my cocker, no fat & she just loves them, they are just dehydrated chicken breast, about the size of a quarter, crisp & we snapped them in half to use as rewards. Great stuff, with no stomach upset like you see after feeding some of those doggie cookies, biscuits, or processed items.
My dogs love these.  They'd eat them all day long if they could!  I feel good about feeding them because I know they're a healthy treat.

I used Weed B Gone last year on my Massachusetts lawn and I was impressed. I don't know about seeing results in 24 hours, but it killed all the clover, dandelions and other unidentified weeds in my lawn. After a couple of weeks they were just gone.

Ortho sells a number of Weed B Gon products, and it took me some searching to find exactly the one I wanted. I wanted one of the versions containing the chemical triclopyr, which is what my state agricultural university extension service recommends for killing wild violets, which for several years had been stubbornly resisting all my organic methods to keep them from taking over my lawn. Since I only had a fairly small area to spray and didn't want to invest in major league spraying equipment if I didn't have to, this version was just what I needed. It's very easy to use. You just attach it to the end of your garden hose, turn on the water (not full blast, just enough to make a nice controllable spray) and spray it on your broadleaf weeds. They absorb the triclopyr through their leaves, it messes them up bad and they die.

There was enough in the bottle for me to spray the wild violets that hadn't died after the first application (as the directions and my extension service mentioned, you usually can't get them all the first try.) Actually, I spent twice as much money on the respirator I bought to wear when I was doing my spraying. I strongly recommend you read the directions carefully and follow the safety instructions. You don't want to inhale this stuff or get it in your eyeballs or mouth or on your skin. Triclopyr is SUPPOSED to break down fairly quickly and not leave residual traces--we'll see about that.

Basmati rice is a very well kept secret in America. Most Americans seem to think all rice is the same (often boring is mentioned). Basmati rice is an adventure from the moment you read the label on the package. As the rice is cooked, a savory fragrance fills the air not too unlike freshly popped pop corn. Having tried various brands of Basmati rice, none have come close to Tilda. The superior quality of product and packageing has made me a loyal fan.

I realize I am just adding my voice to the chorus of approval about Tilda Basmati Rice, but I feel strongly enough to write a review anyway!

IN A NUTSHELL:
If you enjoy rice that is drier in texture and has separate grains, Tilda Basmati is GREAT. The flavor of Basmati rice is distinctive, but Tilda Basmati is yummier and nuttier than all the other Indian and Pakistani brands I have tried. I didn't expect that I would be able to taste a difference, but I can.

The packaging for this rice is very nice. It's in plastic, rather than a woven bag, and it has a re-closeable zipper, which is useful if you keep your rice in the bag, rather than in a storage container.

MORE DETAIL:
Basmati is about the longest of the long-grain rices. It has a distinctive, nutty aroma and flavor, and cooks up into fluffier, drier, separated grains, which is at least partially due to the aging process used. In our house, we like this rice texture best for general eating. It is wonderful all by itself, and it goes very nicely with any spicy dish you can imagine. I use it with Indian meals, Thai dishes (except when sticky rice is called for), Chinese food, Mexican, Latin American, and Spanish dishes. I even use it in combination with medium-grain rice to make conjee (jook).

This said, some people prefer a shorter-grain rice that sticks together more as their general rice - this rice is not going to work for them.

I use short or medium grain rice, such as CalRose, for sushi and other Japanese dishes, and sticky, or "sweet" rice for Thai sticky rice. Sushi rice and sticky rice require specific types of rice to turn out correctly.

CONCLUSION:
For those who prefer a Basmati rice, Tilda is a high-quality, exceptionally delicious choice.
