I am hooked onto this cereals, especially because of great test and high fiber content. This is a much better option than trying to eat green stock vegetables or worse metamucil. :)

This makes a great cereal - so I have thought. With almond milk, fruit, and a protein this makes a well balanced meal, and is great for an on the run breakfast. Has a nice crunch and stays with you through the morning. Has good fiber and protein. With the recent Kashi controversy regarding how their soy is processed, I am not sure how long I will continue to use this. I have recently returned to my flax cereal on some days. Arrives as expected - fresh and well packed.
Being almost $5/box at most grocery stores, this is a good deal. At approximately $3.39/box, it's definitely better buying in bulk.

As I said in my title-I depend on this cereal for:
Weight control
sugar factors
morning energy - my work place environment (protein)
Not only is this healthy and delicious, I now have enough to survive a zombie apocalypse. Seriously, really simple and yummy cereal.

We now subscribe to this cereal and get it shipped to us every month, but my husband first discovered it in basic training for the Army, and every morning passed up eggs and pancakes for this healthier alternative, without sacrificing on taste! He loves this protein-packed breakfast and it's a quick and easy meal for him as he is running out the door for duty every morning.
Highly recommended!

I'm working to boost the fiber in my diet and I've tried every "high fiber" cereal on the market. Most of it is barely edible -- and some simply isn't.

Kashi's GoLean (and GoLean Crunch) are my favorites. It's sweet, but not overly so. It's got serious crunch and holds up well to milk. It's a satisfying breakfast (and I take the crunch version in a zip lock baggie to have easy to access high-fiber munchies on the road.) And, ten grams of fiber per serving (8 on the crunch version) is not bad, not bad at all!

Even my highly-resistant-to-health-food-of-any-kind boyfriend likes the crunch version!

This is my favorite cereal in the morning. I even have a subscription to it because the price is so good with the subscription.

All the major nutrients you want in the morning, protein and fiber. I've had the crunch version in he past, it's just too hard on the teeth and sticky. The berry one is okay, but not filling enough.

This is my favorite cereal.I have converted from an absolute cereal hater to lover thanks to Go lean.(mind you, I don't like the crunch version)
It is a very satisfying breakfast and really prevents me from snacking before lunch.
I have it with low fat milk and the taste is very good.
I can see myself continuing with this for a long time.
Amazon offers a good price and the convenience of buying in bulk.
This is at least a dollar cheaper than in the stores, and it's pretty good/healthy! I like how 6 come in a shipment... I don't have to worry about running out of cereal anytime soon!

This cereal tastes great and is so good for you. I've yet to find another cereal that has the same amount of fiber and protein per serving. The price on amazon is much cheaper than the grocery store. The package arrived quickly and in good condition.
Being a diabetic it is important to start the day off right and this cereal helps me do that. best balanced meal of the day.
This is low in calories and very filling. Plus the macro breakdown is very good for a cereal. The only downside is that the protein comes from soy, which is less than ideal.

I have some health issues and need lots of protein in my food plan.  I use this cereal as a "snack" and get great protein and fiber. Amazon orders come 2nd day so I can count on quick delivery and cost is is less than in the stores.

We have automatic shipping set up monthly and we love it! it's the cheapest anywhere and it is on time. If you like kashi then this is the only way to buy. Oh, and yes my husband and I do go through all six bags by the end of the month.

I eat high fiber cereals because they are good for me. But, can't say that I really enjoy how they taste. No, they are not horrible, but I'd much rather have a bowl of a sugary "kids" cereal rather than something such as Raisin Bran (or anything else that has the word "bran" in the name).

Heard a lot of mostly positive things about Kashi, so took advantage of the recent sale on Amazon to give it a shot. Really pleased with this cereal! It actually tastes good!

I eat it mainly as a snack rather than as a breakfast cereal. Great dessert replacement when mixed with some dried or fresh fruits. Very crunchy and tasty, with just a hint of sweetness. A cups worth really fills you up, and provides far better nutrition than a typical snack food (although, I have to confess that once in a while I skip the fruits and mix in M&M's. Not so good for nutrition, but tasty!!)

The crunchiness is appreciated when I eat it as a snack, but not all that great when eaten as cereal - just a bit too loud for that early in the morning.

Highly recommend!

Tastes good, especially if you are not craving for super sweet food.
And consider the nutrition facts, can not be better.

this cereal has it all.

very high protein and fiber. low in calories.

can't go wrong

I have to say I am glad I decided to purchase this cereal. Great for those who are really trying to watch what they eat and want a cereal that is nutritious and not loaded with sugar and all kinds of other junk. If you like those sweet empty calorie cereals then you will have to adjust your taste buds. This cereal tastes GREAT, and what really matters is that it is great for you. Way to go Kashi! Keep it up

I have been eating nothing but Kashi Golean for breakfast for the past 4 or 5 years (OK, with the occasional splurge at IHOP or similar). Its nutritional values are perfect: high fiber, high protein, will keep you going for a long time. I add some Splenda and cinnamon for sweetness, skim milk, and some dried fruit (cranberries, etc). I love the taste, and I love the calorie count. For people who love cereals, but can't afford the ridiculous amount of added sugar in most commercial cereals, Kashi is the best.

I avoided this cereal for what seemed like years. It looked like bird food and I imagined the taste would be the same. When I started losing weight 2 years ago I finally caved and was pleasantly surprised. It has a great mix of crunchy textures and is lightly sweet.

Best of all it is low in calories while keeping me full and satisifed. A cup is only 140 calories and yet gives you 10 grams of fiber and 13 grams of protein. Being an abid label reader I've come to appreciate how rare that is and although I've tried many other healthy cereals it's hard to find a nuritional profile that matches this one. If I eat something else in place of this I can tell the difference because the fiber and protein of this cereal keep me fuller longer than anything I have tried.

I think the one criticism of this cereal could be that the flavor is mild so I often combat this by paring it with lite flavored soy milk, berries, or other toppings. Or, if I am feeling in the mood for a more flavorful or sugary cereal like Nature's Path Organic Optimum Banana Almond 11-Ounce Boxes (Pack of 6) I will usually mix my bowl of 1/2 and 1/2 to get the best of both worlds.

Overall though this is a fantastic cereal. It is filling, crunch, and much more flavorful and sweet than one might think.
GoLean is tasty and healthy and buying it in a 6-box case is convenient and a good value
This Kashi cereal is excellent.  Many flavors and textures that don't compete.  Trusty banana really makes this cereal stand out.  Seems to have helped us lose some weight as well.

This is how I eat my kashi - in order to incorporate more coconut oil and more cinammon in my diet for my blood sugar and weight loss, etc. I melt 8 TBSPs of coconut oil in a big metal mixing bowl (1T per serving) and dump in the kashi and stir and stir till it seems to have absorbed the oil. Then I add cinammon to taste (at least 1-2 tsps) stir some more and then pour it in a pan and toast it at 350 for 10 minutes - the resulting cereal is absolutely fabulous and I like to mix it with my sugar free activia as well as milk.

It's super! and for weight loss use it as a meal replacement and you'll drop weight like a stone.

However, do not order this cereal from Amazon, as I post this they want over $4 per box. It's regularly $2.78 at my local Wal-mart.

If you are like me and don't eat a lot of meat (I rarely eat red meat) then this is a great source of protein! Eating a lot of fiber is also a great way to stay healthy. I love this cereal and the price on Amazon is unbeatable (it sells for $3.29 at Trader Joe's) especially when it goes on sale.

I bought the Kashi GOLEAN cereal from Amazon because I couldn't find it at my local grocery store the last time I went...

I really like the cereal, it was the packaging for shipping that is getting the bad review:

The boxes were all taped together with packing tape, and the tape ran accross the top of all of the boxes, rendering the resealable closing tab on the top of the box useless, as it basically had to be ripped off to get the tape off of the top of the boxes. The same thing happened along the sides, now I have 6 boxes of Kashi with half of the box ripped and destroyed, including the nutrition facts on the side.

Cereal is good for you and tastes good but too hard on the teeth. I am 51 years old and in great shape but this cereal has me worried about my caps on every bite. Only recommended if your teeth can chew jawbreakers.

This cereal reminds me a bit of Sugar Smacks from my childhood (which I loved, but this is a tamer, drier version). It is OK, but Go Lean Crunch is much tastier, satisfying, and keeps me full longer. Trader Joe's has a similar version that costs a lot less. I don't think it's worth the price.

Go Lean cereal is hard and milk does not soften it much but it does taste great. One morning I poured a bowl, bit down and felt a shock of pain.  I ignored it and my jaw swelled.  The dentist said I cracked a back tooth and had to pull it.  At the time, I was a 25 year active duty military member who up until that point no dental problems outside a few cavities during any of my annual exams.  The dentist explained that teeth are like people with different shapes and sizes and that some back teeth are flatter than others and these are more susceptible to breaking especially as the teeth age.  Go Lean, while delicious, is hard and I gave it up to avoid any more dental issues.

I have no complains about the nutritional benefits of Kashi Go Lean cereal. It's got the lowest fat content of any brand cereal on the market. It only has 130 calories per 45g serving.

However, it is the worst tasting cereal that I've ever had (and I've had quite few in my lifetime). Combine this with Skim Milk and it's akin to eating cardboard pieces soaked in water. It is absolutely revolting, with a weird chemical after-taste that refuses to go away. The least Kashi could have done is throw in some raisins or dried strawberry pieces in there. Sure, the fat content goes up a gram or two but at least, you won't feel like throwing up each time you take a mouthful.

I tried it for three weeks (one serving every day) to see if it was an acquired taste but I will tell you, it was as revolting on Day 21 as it was on Day 1. I've since then switched to Special K Protien Plus. It's got 2 extra grams of fat (that's 30 calories per 45g for the calorie counters out there), but hey, you can eat it and not feel like throwing up. That, I guess is reason enough for me to switch. I can walk the extra 20 calories off by parking the car at the far end of the lot.

Taste Horrible and bad after taste.  Like eating tree branches.  I'll have to stomach through 6 boxes.  Go with Special K Protein Plus.. I wanted to try something different, but I'm sticking with the Special K Protein Plus.

I went ahead and ordered this 24 bottle case since it's difficult at best to find a local supplier of the Mexican Cokes in my area. Costco MAY carry them here, but I don't currently have a Costco card, and all other shops here only carry it sporadically.

So, based on this my review ignores the cost. Shipping was actually free for me, but I'm also an Amazon.com Prime member.

This is the true Mexican coke, made from sugar, not High Frutose Corn Syrup. The flavor is different, and better if nothing else simply due to that, although I do somewhat wonder if the formula is slightly different also. I do remember that Canadian coke in the 90's tasted slightly different (and better) to me also when I'd travel up there, but at the time I didn't check labels to see if they were using sugar and not corn syrup.

Packaging was fine, all the bottles came in intact and undamaged, the box was about the right size for the flat box of 24 cokes and also was padded well enough with packing paper. I would have added a bit more padding, but things were done well enough too I feel.

The add this seller placed does read a bit strange, but my take is he is saying all the cokes he sells are of consistant quality, not that every coke from every nation is good or the same. Otherwise, all of HIS coke products are good and the same.

Anyway, when I see this or Pepsi Throwback (which is also sugar based, not corn syrup based) locally I'll get that instead, but when my area is out of that, I'd consider this merchant again for sure.

horrible experience. many bottles broken. coke leaked everywhere making mess. my front porch is stained from the leak.
scrubbing hasn't helped so i will have to rent a pressure washer. beyond angry

For several years my wife has looked in every candy store we walk past to find the candy of her childhood,with no luck. This year I found it and bought it through Amazon for a Christmas gift. She was delighted and said it tasted the same as when she was a kid with her Grandpa. I should take back all of the other gifts 'cause nothing compared to that old fashioned candy star.

I am not really a flavored coffee fan because it usually dilutes coffee flavor but this coffee had a rich flavor. I purchased the small pkgs to tuck in with Christmas cookies I sent and it was perfect. I am trying more Community Coffee and I have concluded it is a exceptional coffee brand.

Like the previous reviewer, I purchased these at Costco. Their in store price is about half of the Amazon seller's price. But-Costco doesn't sell these online. So if Costco is not an alternative, this may be a good option.

Package doesn't state country of origin. Distributed by a Missouri company. Seal of Veterinary approval on package. Good ingredients.

At first I thought my dog loved them. I broke them in half. She is a 11.5 lb Shih Tzu.  But after two days she started bringing them outside and burying them.  So I guess she's not that fond of them. I wont be buying these again.

I have tried a number of other dog treats that assist with keeping a dog's teeth healthy but have been very concerned about the safety.  At some point my dog would begin to choke on the treat because it would get caught in his throat.  Then I found Checkups at Costco (a company that sells great products) and thought I would give them a try.  The Checkups dental treats are awesome.  They give his teeth a workout but are not hard to the point of having sharp edges and my dog loves them.  For his size it is recommended to give him the whole treat but they are scored so they can be broken in half and he is satisfied with half.  I went on line and found Amazon sells them and am on my second bag now!  Great product!!

Do not feed these to small dogs. I would break them in half and give them to my pug, and she wound up vomiting it up on 2 different occasions. It would be nice if they made the treats for different dog sizes...

I'm probably on the 10th bag I've bought right here on amazon...however the reason for the 1 star doesn't reflect the quality of the treats but the pricing. I went to Costco the other day and they were being sold for less than $11. That being said I'll be stocking up from Costco and hope theyll always be sold there.

I am unsure why this product caused such problems for my dogs as the ingredients look okay and it says "highly digestible".  I guess I need to look for "fully digestible".  I didn't throw them out because I want to write the company and my husband decided to give a treat to one of the dogs, who has been subsequently ill for the last 3 days.  She won't eat, wants to eat grass and has bad runs.

We have a 126 lb Bernese Mountain Dog.  He is addicted to Checkups.  He will sell his soul for a "white bone."  I buy them at Costco for approximately $12 for the 24-count bag.  Your prices are a bit steep.

Alright so about 3 months ago I asked my vet how much a dog teeth cleaning would cost me.  Because the dog would have to be put under anesthesia, she said total would be about $350.  Pretty steep but I thought I should give my dog a cleaning since he was in need of one.  Last month I called in to make the dental appt. and was surprised to hear their prices have gone up to $550....c'mon people, I love my dog a lot but in today's economy $550 is a lot of money, certainly almost more than a car payment.  I stumbled on these Checkups at my local Costco and have been using them for a week.  I am AMAZED at how well these work!!!  In just a week I have noticed a real drastic reduction in plaque buildup and in the bad breath.  I highly recommend these, my dog loves em so much, it's his special treat and at the same time it's helping his teeth and the bad breath issue.  Can't beat that, and the Costco price is awesome!  Try these.

These are the best dog treats ever. The dogs seem to like them and they really, really, really work. We have two Labs (a black and a yellow). The yellow is nine years old and has about the worst breath of all time. You know like when he breathes in your general direction, it causes a physical reaction. Well after about four treats (one per day), you could see err smell a significant improvement. It was amazing. They are a good chew for my guys as well (taking about 2 minutes to get through), as opposed to some other treats which go to fast or Greenies which are way too expensive. I highly reccomend. I just wish more people carried them locally.

I have a small dog with very bad teeth and she runs from a tooth brush.  So I rely on these every day.  I break them in half and give her a half every morning.  Even with bad teeth, she has no trouble chewing them up and she loves them.

These treats really work!! My 4 year old Sheltie had a serious build up of plaque on her teeth when I got her two years ago.  The vet has been advising me to have her teeth cleaned while she is under anesthesia.  I saw "Check ups" and decided to try them.  My dog loves them, and best of all, after about two months there is hardly any plaque on her teeth.  I truly believe these treats saved me from the risk and expense of having my dog under anesthesia.  Plus, these treats are wheat gluten free so they don't aggravate my dog's allergies.

My dalmatian loves these. They seem to do a good job cleaning his teeth.  He's an avid chewer so for him they only last a minute or two but I purchased these to give him some dental cleaning not entertain him.  Also, he's prone to allergies and the meat-free formulation works great for him.
Our dogs love these treats, and we feel good that they might help their teeth.  These don't make them sick to their stomach like those horrible "greenies!"

I found these at Costco (for less) and thought I'd try them for my 28lb beagle.  He generally needs his teeth cleaned by the vet every 12-15 months due to tartar buildup, even though I brush them.  He absolutely LOVES these treats!  He gets a half of one (they are very easy to divide) after dinner and he sits by the cabinet and waits for it.  The treats are not completely hard, but slightly rubbery, so they clean the teeth as the dog chews them.  His teeth look great and his breath smells cleaner.  The treats are not scented, and are made of mostly potato flour.  I HIGHLY recommend!!

I have been using these for every day for the past 3 years with my 3 dogs, two over 60 pound pit bulls and a little Jack Russell mix.  I split the chew into 1/4's and each dog gets 1/4 after breakfast and dinner.  My dogs' teeth and breath are perfect, the 7 year old is often mistaken by his teeth as being many years younger.  I buy these at Costco for 1/2 the Amazon price....and my dogs also get rawhide Chews and big knuckle bones to complete the teeth cleaning process.  Never had ANY problem with allergies or choking, but these are pretty big bones to give a dog, even a gobbler dog.  Try cutting them smaller even you give the entire bone at a sitting.  These are GREAT!!

I was skeptical about whether these would work or not, but I figured I would give them a try on our GSD. My GSD had massive tartar buildup, even though we only feed her dry dog food. I have been giving her two Checkups a day for the last 5 days and I am amazed at how good these dental bones work. These bones have completely removed the tartar on most of her teeth, and continues to remove the remaining tartar with each bone eaten. I tried brushing her teeth for a month and could not get remove the buildup of tartar!

In addition to removing tartar buildup, her bad breath that used to drive our family crazy has also cleared up! We were also very happy with the fact that these did not upset our dogs stomach. Our dog has a very sensitive stomach and most food and treats will cause her to vomit and develop diarrhea, but these treats caused no problems at all. If your dog has tartar build up or bad breath, give these treats a shot.

I've become hesitant about giving my American Bulldog dental chews because she tends to gulp them in two bites. My vet recommended the C.E.T Oral Hygiene Chews, but my dog doesn't chew them properly and ends up gagging and regurgitating them. Based on the good reviews here, I decided to try the Checkups and so far they are working great! My dog is eager to get the treat, but she chews it more slowly. I haven't used that many yet, but I can tell her breath is better and it looks like her teeth are improving, and it doesn't upset her sensitive stomach.

A truly outstanding product! My dog loves his Checkups and his daily enjoyment has resulted in several hundred dollars savings when my vet says, "His teeth look great, his gums looks great: no cleaning necessary!" My dog loves them so much, he never lets me forget a day.  He stands and stares at the cupboard where they are kept each afternoon letting me know he's not yet had his Dental Treat. :-)  Absolutely love this product!

These are great, our dog has never had to have her teeth cleaned in the nearly 6 years she's been with us. Every monthly trip to Costco, I pick up two packages, and she wants them every time I head towards the garage (where we keep them).

Unfortunately, they weren't there on our last trip to Costco. Apparently the only Costco that will still carry them is in Anchorage.

Please please please if you're a Costco member, and your dog likes Checkups, add it to their suggestion box -- at the store, and online (memberservices at costco dot com).

My dogs love these dental chews, and they actually take up to a minute to eat one, which is much better than most affordable dental chews.  I'm poking around the net for another place to buy Checkups because my Costco is an unreliable source.  But about that affordability.  I have been paying about $14 per bag at Costco.  A 50% higher price at amazon makes them that much less competitive.

I have been using this product for more than a year now. It keeps my 22 month old Golden retriever's teeth very white and clean. I see no tartar buildup and bad breath what so ever. Another plus is that it is wheat free. I occasionally invite the neighbors dog over for play dates. One day I took a look at their dog's teeth who is 8 months younger than my dog and he already has tartar buildup on most of his teeth. I give her one bone a day every morning after she delivers the morning paper to me. To bad she doesn't know how to make me breakfast.

My only disappointment is the price. They were once available at Costco's for $11.99 the markup here is unbelievable. Now you have to pay almost double for them here. It is my understanding that Costco is no longer going to carry this product anymore. I emailed the company but Amazon and Costco were the only companies getting them at the time. I think they have a great product but need to make it more widely available and maybe that would bring down the price.

They also make Bright Bites (which are the same with flavor added to it) but I find the checkups a better value for your money. The checkups are much bigger than the large size Bright Bites and cost less when you compare the weight. If you have a small dog it is not that hard to break up the checkup bone. With all that said I will keep buying them here until I can find someone else who sells them cheaper.

I have a 6 1/2 month old, 47lb, pit bull mix. He has absolutely no allergies, and no sensitivities. He basically eats everything without an issue, however, we found the one thing that does not agree with him, "CHECKUPS." I just bought the product from Costco last night, and gave him one bone while I was home so that I could see how he reacted to it and how long it lasted. At first I was happy to see that he spent some time chewing on it. We all went to bed, and all was fine, until 4:00 am, when we were awoken by Rocco throwing up his dinner. An hour later, he proceeded to throw up blood, a large amount of blood. Soon after, he threw up blood again. We rushed him to the vet, and the vet said that this product was way too hard for a puppy that young. We were surprised to hear this because the package stated that the product was designed for puppies 6 months or older, and Rocco was double the suggested weight limit. He said this product should not be given to dogs until they are more than a year old. The product, when chewed, became sharp shards, that tore up his digestive tract. I feel terrible for putting Rocco through this. It is not worth the risk.

My rescued 4 year old pit bull absolutely loved Checkups and downed them as if they were his favorite treat. My 6 year old lab mutt, however, would take these in her mouth and then set them down and ignore them. While I'm glad my pit bull loves these dental treats, the treats did not do a thing for his breath. It took a good ol' toothbrush and Petrodex dog toothpaste to get his breath under control.

I have two dogs ... a little 15 pound pug a poo and a 90 pound native american indian dog.  Both dogs go absolutely crazy for Check Ups.  Don't know what it is but makes me happy cause it keeps their teeth clean and their breath fresh!  And yes, get them at Costco for around $12 for 24ct.

My black lab Jade is 6 1/2 years old. She's been having tartar lately, probably because her mouth was sore after having a molar extracted when it got cracked, and rawhide chews no longer interested her. I bought Checkups at Costco for a good price, less than $12. By the way, after not finding them recently, I was told they have been terminated. None are left at any Costco in the Las Vegas area, so by all means place it in the suggestions box.

Anyway, when I first brought one out of the bag, it didn't look like anything special. The bag smelled like vitamins, and pretty strongly at that. Jade followed me upstairs to our bedroom, knowing I had SOMETHING interesting I was hiding from her. I tried to toss it to my wife, who was sitting on the bed. Jade went nucking futz! She jumped uninvited onto the bed, which she NEVER does, sniffed out the Checkup quickly, and ate it. Since, she's repeated this behavior. She absolutely loves them! She's never acted like this over anything.

After a few weeks of Checkups, Jade's teeth are white again. Her breath is clean. But now I'm out of Checkups and can't get them from Costco. Amazon's price is much higher, and it has to be shipped. I've requested the company send me dealer locations, so maybe all is not lost.

I don't know what it is about these - they are white, no color, no real smell, no interesting meaty ingredients... but whenever I show my Goldens these, their eyes get as big as saucers and they start drooling.  An added bonus is it helps their teeth.

After trying many different dental chews that ended up being thrown away because my dogs hated them...I found Check-Ups at Costco and my dogs love them and beg for them!!
Then Costco discontinued carrying them! I'm so glad I can get them at Amazon !

My 35 lbs. terrier has been devoted to Checkups Dental Dog Treats for several years but he is nuts for the combination of 1/2 a Checkup stuffed into a medium-sized Kong ribbed Stuff-a-Ball. After about two years, he is on his fourth Kong, having worn and weakened the others after many hours of torturing it. Pushing it all the way into the new Kong might take hand strength and determination on your part. Getting it out requires crushing doggie jaw pressure, a series of well-thought out strategies like slamming down the Kong while perched on a footstool, or carrying it up a flight of steps and bouncing it down to the lower level, then checking each step for crumbles that may have dislodged on the trip down. All the time he is working on extracting the dental bone, he is cleaning his teeth on the Kong - I don't think the vet will ever have to have to anesthetize him and clean them again. My boy brings me the Kong right after he finishes his supper each night and cries like a girl until I stuff it with a Checkup and the fun can begin.
My dogs love these treats and they have become very hard to find.  The shipper sent the order on time and the products were received in excellent condition.  My dogs are happy once again!

Read the ingredients.  These are good prospects for a treat that the dog loves and it appears that even at small amounts, make a difference on teeth. Seriously.  Most of all, large border collie, ten years old, loves them.  We keep amounts low, most evenings give her a half of one bone.  They leave no mess behind, to not choke like rawhide.  Originally purchased at costco, now bummed that they have to be ordered online.  They are worth it.
tried them once at Costco and then couldn't find them anymore...finally found here on Amazon...She LOVES them and they help her breath/teeth!

These were recommended by my vet.  They break apart pretty easily for my small dogs while the big dogs get a whole bone.  It's the enzymes that help the teeth.  Wish they were less expensive however..

I don't know what is in these things, all I know is that our dog can't stop eating them. If her teeth didn't look so good since she I started giving her them (and if they weren't so easily digestible), I'd feel bad that I enabled a Checkups addiction in our dog. She's a forty-pound mutt, and I give her one-half of a Checkup after breakfast and dinner... if I wait too long to give her the treat, she starts whining and moaning until I pull one out of the container on the kitchen counter. Then she runs to her bed and waits not-so-patiently for it... yeah, she's a weird one. :-)

Like many other reviewers, I used to buy these at Costco for about half the price, but had been unable to find them at either of our local stores. I contacted both Diamond Pet Foods and Costco about it. Diamond said that Costco rotates the availability of many of is products, discontinuing items for a couple of months then bringing them back. They suggested I let Costco know that we liked product and wanted to see it on a permanent basis, but in the mean time that I could buy them from Amazon. Costco said the item had been discontinued, making no mention of it being a rotating product, but that they would pass my message on to their buyers. If you want to see these back on the shelves in Costco, send them an e-mail or drop in a note in the suggestion box at your local store about it. The more customers they hear from, the better the chance they will bring them back.

Diamond also suggested another one of their products, Bright Bites, which are similar to Checkups. They come in three flavors -- peppermint, wintergreen, and cinnamon -- and are available in retail stores (you can find a list on their web site) and Amazon. I don't know if our dog would dig the flavors, or if switching to them would be any less expensive than continuing to buy Checkups from Amazon, but maybe I'll try them out some time.

Our dog has one a day and never needs his teeth cleaned.

Mallomars are a soft, vanilla wafer that has a marshmallow layer on top, which is then covered over with scrumptious chocolate! Much to my surprise, these cookies are actually quite low in calories (60 calories each, with no trans fats), which is one thing I was a bit worried about originally, before I got my first taste! ;-)

The cookies were fresh, which is one thing that I appreciated. I know that some earlier reviewers mentioned that they had experienced some issues with this, but mine were great! One suggestion is to freeze the cookies, as it makes the outer chocolate layer crunchy and the marshmallows delightfully chewy, if that is something that you enjoy.

One word summary -- BUY!

This is an excellent seasonal cookie that has been around for almost 100 years. It consists of a small cookie topped with marshmallow and then covered with chocolate. I enjoyed the cookies and agree with the other positive reviews here.

There are a couple of concerns having to do with how these cookies are handled and stored.

Fragility - the cookie part of the Mallomar is quite fragile. The sample I received was shipped in a bubble-wrap package. At some point, something heavy was on top of it or dropped on it. That's how almost half of the cookies were crumbled. Regular shipments would be packed in cartons, but this is definitely something you want put in at the top of your grocery bag.

Chocolate Bloom - When stored in warm conditions, real chocolate will "bloom." Some of the cocoa butter will separate and migrate to the surface. This results in what appears to be a very thin light-colored coating on some or all of the surface. It is generally held that this is a cosmetic issue which has no effect on the taste of the chocolate. The sample I received had chocolate bloom and a few of the cookies were sticking together, definite signs that they had spent time in a warm environment after leaving the factory (it was unseasonably cool here the day they were delivered). This may be one reason that this is a seasonal, cool-weather product.

Neither of these issues have to do with the manufacturing of the cookies, so I don't think they merit any stars off. They are something to bear in mind whether you're buying them online or at a retail store.

They are one of those foods that speak to you and do not shut up until they are all gone.

If you've never had one, it's a fairly nondescript relative of a vanilla wafer topped with marshmallow, the whole thing thinly coated in a nice dark chololate. Sweet and gooey and not too heavy; what's not to like?

The particular sample that was sent to me seemed a bit old, or as if it had been stored at too high a temperature; and this is a cookie that needs to be fresh to be at its best. Thus, I received these at the end of October, with an expiration date in February. I would look for something with the date a bit further along if I were buying them in a store.
