Since I had liked the Emerald Marcona Almonds, 11.5oz Canister (Pack of 4) better than I thought I would and since I like cashews anyway, I was sure that I would like Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashew, 10oz Canister (Pack of 4). What I didn't anticipate was how much I would LOVE them!

Salt & Pepper makes an entertaining movie crime fighting duo, and in hair color it sounds a little better than "going gray", but as a flavor it did not appeal to me...

until now. I had planned to ration them out by the lid full per day, but the whole ten ounces was gone in a couple of hours. I guess I should consider myself lucky that Amazon only sent me one canister to sample! Some might consider the flavor a bit strong, especially if they enjoy the bare cashew taste, which is all but obliterated here.

(sigh)

Yet another temptation I must learn to resist!

Note: I'm simply going to have to take their word for it that the "Twist-on lid locks in freshness" because mine didn't last long enough to test the claim.

Oh yum yum yum. Double plus tasty. A pow! of pepper followed by a strong left hook of salty nutty knockout. These nuts be good.

So the subtle taste of cashews is lost. So there is also some sugar and maltodextrin in the mix. But if you like the taste of black pepper and are looking for a bold (i.e. super strong, maybe even a burning aftertaste) experience from just a few nuts then this is it. Good for just having a small handfull, or will be good sprinkled on an otherwise bland bed of lettice. The light canister is egonomic, but won't be accepted by recycling programs as the plastic is index 7.

I love cashews and was looking forward to trying these. Unfortunately to my palate they have way too much salt and pepper. The bitterness of the salt overdose gives way to the bitterness and bite of the black pepper. The cashew flavor was completely overwhelmed as well as the pleasant subtle flavors of the onion and garlic. :P

Sea salt, pepper, cashews---are any three words, together, more capable of evoking images of love and desire? Emerald knows just how to combine them. These cashews are so delicious I can, while eating them, close my eyes and feel I'm lounging on a divan in a pasha's fragrant tent, fanned by eunuchs as a breathtakingly beautiful member of the royal family whispers seductive parables in my ear!

Open a canister, close your eyes, and see where you're transported!

Yes these are sea salt and pepper cashews, however they are SO salty that neither me or my husband could handle eating them. The sea salt did have a nice flavor to it (not regular old plain salt taste). However it just was really hard to eat and then we were both thirsty for long after eating a couple of handfuls.

We are both black pepper lovers and we loved the black pepper taste.

If only these had perhaps 1/3 the amount of sea salt with this same amount (or more) of black pepper then they would rank a 5 star rating.

The nuts themselves are excellent.

I have tried other nut products from this company and loved them.

I like the Emerald brand nuts. The canister is very convenient and easy to take along. I was a bit leery about the salt and pepper flavor. It wasn't as bad as I thought. I was mainly concerned that the pepper would be too strong. I actually found the salt to be a bit overwhelming. As I got closer to the bottom of the canister, the salt taste became stronger and the nuts at the bottom were very salty-almost inedible. If you love cashews this is a nice change from just salted as the pepper gives the nut a little "kick."

These were really good cashews.  The flavor is great, though it was important to pay a bit of attention when eating as occasionaly one nut will have a insane amount of pepper, but over all a really great taste. The nuts were fresh and not too salty, which is a problem with a lot of nuts.  The container was also very nice and convenient to use.

I love cashews, and I love black pepper flavored potato chips, so when I saw these, I knew I had to try them.  At first taste, I wasn't sure what to make of them.  The pepper taste was strong, almost overpowering the cashew flavor.  But I soon found myself enjoying the flavor, even craving them.  This is certainly not a flavor for everyone, but if you prefer savory flavors to some of the sweeter nut varieties out there, give these a try.  And I have to once again comment that I love the canister these come in.  They fit well in a car cup-holder, and I can just pop the canister in my messenger for a between-class snack, without worrying that the container will pop open, scattering nuts everywhere.

I love cashews but wasn't so sure how I was going to like them with pepper added.  At first, I thought they were just okay.  I ate a few and then put them away.  A short while later, I found myself wanting a few more and this seemed to just keep happening.  The pepper makes for an interesting flavor, and when combined with the sea salt - well, they became strangely addictive.  I recommend anyone who likes cashews to give them a try!  The only reason I gave them 4 stars, though, was that some of the cashews were overwhelmed with salt.

I have to admit I wouldn't normally throw pepper on my cashews but I liked the combination. There are other flavors as well (a hint of garlic, I think) so the label be slightly misleading. This product is definitely worth trying. My teen loved it too and it disappeared quickly in our house.

If you like unique flavor combinations and are willing to kick things up a notch, give this product a try. Odds are, you won't regret it, if the preferences of several teens, 2 adults and one bird (who flew down and ate a couple of dropped pieces - we were outside) gives you something to go on.

Some other details that might be of interest: not too salty, large sized cashews, nicely roasted. There. That should do it :) Enjoy!

These reminded me of seasoned nuts I've purchased at the Indian grocery in the past, but ten times better. The cashews themselves are fresh and large with a good rich cashew taste. The pepper and salt add a wonderful flavor and the result is a very pleasant snack with a great aftertaste that kept me going back for more and more. Yes, they were a tad salty (especially the last 1/4 of the canister) but to me that was the only drawback. I can see how, if someone did NOT like spicy or peppery foods, they might be "too bold" as others have said, but come on, they are salt and PEPPER flavor...what do you expect?

I plan to get some more in the near future...my canister is empty!

When I got these nuts I expected what the description said,sea salt and a 'hint' of pepper.Instead I got a salty,hot assault on my taste buds.There is no taste of cashew left.All you get is an overpowering hot,peppery mess.I would never buy these and do not recommend that you buy them either,unless all you want is heat.Then I recommend you stick your tongue in your car's cigarette lighter.The resulting taste is about the same.

After enjoying the Emerald Marcona Alomonds, I was really looking forward to the cashews. I love cashews and thought the Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper would be great. However, it was evident with my first handful that there was way too much salt and pepper for my taste. Maybe that was a good thing because it slowed down the momentum of how I usually eat cashews. Each time I had more, I had to wet a paper towel to soak up the excess seasoning.

I quite imagine that for recipes that call for cashews, the pre-seasoning would probably be a welcomed addition.

I've been partial to Emerald's products so my favorable reaction to this one comes as no surprise to me.  However, I would warn that this may not be to everyone's taste - at least at first.  The sea salt definitely has more kick than the usual salted nuts and the pepper gives it a decided bite.  For those whose taste in nuts tend more towards sweeter concoctions, this may be a bit much.  But for those who like dark beer, strong coffee, and snacks with attitude, this is a welcome treat.

I was not expecting to like these, but was surprised to discover I had absent-mindedly eaten almost half the container while working at my desk for a couple of hours after first opening the package. I took the container to the kitchen where it managed to last a few more days.

These are an interesting variation on the traditional salted cashews. I would not buy them instead of traditional cashews, but would be happy to have them as an occasional change of pace. One star off because the onion leaves a mild aftertaste.

As a health nut, there's nothing like picking up fresh food that's tasty and nutritious. During breaks or on the run, Emerald's Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews are a zesty change from drab, empty-calorie snacks.

Nutrition wise: It adds a healthy dose of protein, iron, zinc, and good lipids (fats) to the nut mix. For kids, it's a low-sugar alternative to everyday peanut butter.

The designer canister fits snugly in your car beverage container, and the nifty lid is perfect for portion control. With four canisters and 10 oz. in each, you get about a month's worth of rewards--if you can control yourself.

I think these would have been better without the pepper -- or maybe just a little less pepper. It creates a very overpowering taste. I can only eat 2 or 3 at a time.

The cashews themselves are soft and delicious. The packaging is nice -- resealable and recyclable.

So if you like salty nuts, you may like this. I prefer my nuts lightly salted and with just a little pepper.

Ok, when you start screwing with the original delicious flavor of cashews, then you are experimenting randomly. These do not taste good! Plain and simple. Pepper belongs on eggs only and NOT on cashews. There is a tangy citrisy flavor that doesn't make it either.

I honestly say, I tried a handful, husband tried a handful and we said, NO WAY! The claim is SEA Salt, whatever that is; I know I wouldn't drink sea water, so why would I like SEA Salt. The cashews are hot and spicy and overall, the heavy seasonings take away the original flavor, and without original flavor you have something completely different.

Cashews generally are a good source of snacks and these have no transfat which is good. It's a good thing I have a few enemies in my lifetime, because they will deserve these!....Rizzo

I like nuts.
I eat pistachios and cashews and walnuts and pecans and macadamia nuts all of the time.
After all this time, I know what I like and what I don't.

At first, these cashews didn't grab me.
Sure, they are a good quality nut and are crunchy and "fresh."
But the spicing was not something I was used to. I usually like my nuts plain or lightly salted. The seasoning here seemed a bit extreme.

However, by the time I reached the "bottom of the barrel," these nuts had grown on me and I have to say they are pretty darn good. The spicing really suits the cashews. If you like salty, peppery nuts with a very strong onion aftertaste, then you will really enjoy this offering from Emerald. They also make some Cocoa Roasted Almonds that I just have to try. But if you like your nuts fairly plain, I would steer clear of the strong flavor these nuts offer and instead get something like Emerald Nuts Whole Cashews, 4.5-Ounce Canisters (Pack of 12).

Overall recommended if you are a little adventurous with your nuts. :')

Your friends and family may envy you...when you show them these incredible cashews spiced up slightly (do not worry--your mouth is not set on fire!) by the sea salt and the pepper. My only advice is, unless you don't want to have any left by the end of an hour or so, DON'T share. I know that is not nice of me to say, but these cashews are so phenomenally delicious, you will end up with an empty green pencil holder (one idea I had for what to do with the can after my can of nuts was empty because of my family eating all of the nuts) and just a fleeting memory of your incredible delicious Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews by Emerald. Yes! It can hurt to love something this much! I should have hid these!!! Wow! Five stars for these cashews!

I'm a big fan of Emerald nuts, just check out my other reviews. However, I was slightly disappointed in these cashews. While they're very fresh, there was much too much seasoning, especially going overboard (haha, get it?) with the sea salt. Furthermore, I question whether real sea salt was used, which typically has larger grain sizes than table salt. It looks just like regular table salt.

However, there is a saving grace for these nuts, and it prevented me from dishing out just 3 stars. What to do with overly salty, peppery cashews? Stir fry some chopped chicken breasts, and make Chinese chicken & cashews with bell peppers. Don't bother adding salt to the chicken- just add in these cashews, and you're good to go!

I am writing this review fully acknowledging that tastes are matters of personal preference, whether in music or in food. That being said, I have to come out and say I just don't like these cashews, which are practically encrusted with salt and pepper.

In our family we don't salt and pepper our food liberally, so maybe my wife and I were particularly sensitive to the salt-and-pepper blast of these cashews. Again, it's a matter of taste: if you love salt and pepper, you might like these.

To write a fair review, I decided to wash the seasonings off the cashews under tap water to taste the bare nut underneath. I was surprised to find that the salt and pepper didn't just rinse off. Something was making it adhere to the cashews. So I soaked and rinsed and rubbed with my fingers a little more and finally got all the seasoning off the 5 or 6 cashews I had in my hand.

Once I got all the seasoning off (or so I thought), I noticed something else that surprised me: the cashews were still greasy. This wasn't intended to be a whole-day affair, so I just popped two in my mouth. The first thing I noticed was that the cashew retained a slightly crisp, roasted character even after the drenching. That was the good news. Then I dropped the remaining cashews in my mouth, and a few seconds later came the bad news: I started tasting that pesky little prickly pepper picked for palate pop, poking its way through an otherwise tasty though plain roasted cashew.

If you'd like a simpler review, my wife, a no-nonsense woman, ate just a couple and said, "I hate these. Do they have those Emerald almonds with the cocoa back in stock yet?"

I love cashews, was VERY hungry when I opened the container, and was ready to scarf down a handful of these!

Unfortunately, they are nothing like "sea salt and pepper" flavor. This is one of those weird combos of ingredients that end up tasting very artificial. In fact, the coating of sugar, granulated onion, and salt even has a strange texture that feels sort of plastic-y on the tongue and does not seem to dissolve. The ingredient list is ridiculously long for a product marketed to appear simple and natural. Why was all the artificial and processed junk added, when the basics of cashews, salt, and pepper could have been so tasty?

If these had truly been as advertised I'm sure I would have eaten half the container. :) Instead, I was only able to eat 3-4 nuts, then closed up the container. When I find time I'll try rinsing them off with hot water in a colander so that they don't have to go to waste.

On a positive note, the packaging is nice-- reseals easily and is convenient.

These cashews are awful...no, wait, awful isn't strong enough word.  Disgusting, yep, that's it.  They're disgusting.  Eating these cashews is like going to your cupboard, grabbing a container of onion salt, and eating a spoonful of it.  If that is appealing to you, then buy these cashews.  Remember to give your significant other a sloppy wet onion kiss when you're done.
They took a great nut-and ruined it by putting too much salt & pepper on it.  Usually one nut leads to another -- for those on a diet, try this nut, it will curb your desire for seconds.

I'm a big fan of Emerald nut products, especially their almonds, but I have to say I'm not nuts about Emerald Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews.  Cashews are generally tasty enough so all they need is a little roasting with a sprinkling of sea salt to heighten their flavor.  In this case, the poor cashews don't stand much of a chance against all the salt and, especially pepper--not to mention the granulated onion.  Where cashews are concerned, less would definitely be more!

I like salted cashews to begin with...and I just discovered that a good sprinkling of pepper makes them even better.  The taste is great. All that fruity sweetness in a cashew is brought out by the pepper. These nuts have plenty of salt and enough paper to leave the tiniest burn on the tongue.  The peppery flavor enhances the taste of the cashew and heat is just the right intensity. If you have an ultra-sensitve or immature palette and cannot abide anything spicy, you may want to give these a miss. But if like a little bite in your bite, you'll gobble these goodies down. Serve them with beer, alongside a sandwich plate, or tossed on top of any salad. They'll add a little crunch and terrific flavor.  I liked the Cocoa-poweder dusted almonds that Emerald recently introduced. They are subtle, unusual and delicate. These cashews, on the other hand, are bold...all that salt and pepper pack a lot of flavor into every nut.  The taste is so intense that one handful is very satisfying...good news for us who like to watch our calories.

Honestly I love cashews however these are a bit too strong for my liking. As others have said, too much salt and way too much pepper! Still the nuts are crunchy and fresh although I can taste some suger on them.

The pepper leaves a hot aftertaste in my mouth that lasts for several minutes. I ate a 4th of the can then had to get something to drink

If you like pepper then these are for you. If not then maybe you should get something else instead...

Like Marlon Brando in "On the Waterfront," these lovely cashews could have been a solid winner, if they had at least half the salt. Instead they remind me of the time I put a cup of salt into the cookie batch instead of sugar. There's quite a bit of pepper too, and it's nice if you like things peppery now and then, and most of us do.

The best one can do is try to shake or paper towel some of the salt off (unfortunately this takes the pepper off as well) and sprinkle the nuts on a simple salad with just oil and vinegar for dressing, or perhaps nibble them along with some very plain veggies, like celery sticks. Serving size is listed as 1 oz. (1/4 cup) which gives you 160 calories, 4 grams of protein, and 270 mg of the dreaded sodium.

Like other Emerald nuts that I have really liked, Sea Salt & Pepper Cashews would have been delicious and a 5 star item with much less salt, so they are a disappointment. Perhaps Emerald can change their recipe a little to give us "menos sal y mas pimienta." The sturdy container has many "post nut" uses, with a label that comes off easily, a lid that screws on tightly with ease, and a shape that fits the palm of your hand, as well as the cup holder in your car.

I love cashews, so I was intrigued by this product. However I found it very disappointing: there is way too much salt on the nuts, which covers the flavor instead of highlighting the natural sweetness of the cashews.

Also, they could have chosen a more environment friendly packaging, like recyclable see-through plastic, which is also less likely to leach into the foods contained within.

I love Cashew nuts and spicy foods, so I thought this would be a good combination.  Unfortunately, the nuts were too salty for my taste.  I have tried other snacks with Sea Salt that I found enjoyable, but I cannot recommend this product.  I will wash the seasonings off of these Cashews and  add them to a spicy soup.

This is the second type of nuts that I have tried from Emerald with the other being the Cocoa Roast Almonds. While the almonds were a sweet and salty snack, these are salty and spicy. As with the Almonds, the lid measures a 1/4 cup serving of nuts. After eating these for a few days, here are my impressions.

As you can tell from the headline, these didn't turn out to be quite what I was expecting. Granulated onion is listed on the ingredients along with "spices", but the onion flavor comes through rather strongly with the salt and the pepper. While the taste grew on my pretty quickly, I found that these made me very thirsty. Compared to the 25 mg of sodium in the Cocoa Roast Almonds, these cashews clock in at 270 mg. The almonds also win with 210 mg of potassium versus only 140 mg in the cashews.

In the end, though, the taste is what is going to make or break this product for most people. What you need to know is that the flavor of these cashews is very strong, and it doesn't come from the cashews themselves. If a strong salt, pepper, and onion flavor is what you are looking for in a snack, this will be right up your alley. For me personally, they are something that I wouldn't turn down if someone offered them to me. However, I probably won't go out of my way to buy more of them. Finally as with all nuts you have to be disciplined because the serving size is small for the calories you get.
Holy cow... way too much salt and pepper... There is nothing good about this seasoning.  It completely wipes out the taste of the nut.

These are really great nuts.
One thing though, they have too much salt and pepper.
Just use a strainer and shake them for a few minutes.

Wow!  Someone likes Salt and Pepper way too much over at Emerald.  I got a coupon for it so I thought I would try it.  Didn't like them - I will go back to buying Planters Salt-n-Pepper.  The Planters has just the right mix of seasonings.

Nobody likes salt more than me.  And I love cashews.  So it really means something when I tell you these are too salty.  Sorry.  I was ready to love them but it just didn't happen that way.  Seriously, I'm someone who finished a bag of pretzels and then pours the remaining salt and crumbs right down my throat.  I like salty.  But I could only eat a few of these cashews before feeling like I was baking in a kiln.

I tried to like these, but they were just COVERED with salt and mostly pepper, way, way, too much.  I ended up using them in stir-fry and didn't have to add any salt and pepper to the dish!!  I don't recommend them at all unless you REALLY like lots of seasoning (and I THOUGHT I liked salt!).

I enjoy cashews and thought these would be a tasty variation. I eagerly bit into my first one and was replused by the oily taste. Since I always make my kids take 3 bites of everything, I kept chewing. It didn't get any better. Soon a salty taste mixed in with the oil, followed by the flavor of stale dimestore pepper - the kind grandmas keep in a tin in their cupboard for years because no one uses it. After completing the first tortureous bite, I ate 2 more nuts just to be sure they were not some acquired taste or novelty I may be missing out on. They were not. Took a good brushing and rinsing with Listerine to burn the flavor out of my mouth.

I gave them 2 stars because I eat a lot of fresh foods and an above average amount of raw foods. Some one more used to a processed food flavor might find them more desirable than I did.

As a nut the Cashew is one of my favorites. The pepper flavor was interesting and added a unique flavor to this already great nut. The salt was a bit much. Salt tastes good but i would cut the salt by 75% here. It was very overpowering and required water almost immediately.

These are very strongly seasoned, with not only salt and pepper, but also sugar, granulated onion, citric acid, and mystery "spice." (I've uploaded a photo of the label above).

I find them unpleasant for two reasons -- 1) they're just FAR too strongly seasoned and 2) I do not enjoy the pepper/onion/mystery-spice combination. I can definitely taste the onion and citric acid (provides a bit of tartness), and cannot quite put my finger on the mystery spice.

The nuts themselves are reasonably sized, most are whole or halves, with some broken pieces. I've uploaded a photo above so you can see them.

But ugh. The taste is just not for me, and there is too much of it. I think the rare person who really likes the salt/pepper/onion/mystery-spice flavor might enjoy these, as at least one reviewer has, but I'll pass in the future -- and I *LOVE* cashews in general. The might be good to cook with, adding to a dish with no prior seasoning to add cashew and spice flavor!

I've noticed in the last few years the tendency of companies to try to dress up normal every day products by adding something new: Lime Coke, Vanilla Coke, vitamin coke, Lemon Coke, you get the idea. Sometimes it just gets ridiculous.

Anyway, I like cashews, though I don't eat them too often compared to almonds and peanuts. I usually avoid salty snacks, but find the sea salt and pepper a good combination and the container is a nice size and design. I could see these being especially good with/ after a couple of beers.

I love cashews, and the idea of these yummy nuts with a dash of sea salt and pepper sounded inspired. However, the result is way too salty. If there was one-tenth the amount of salt, I might have tasted the pepper and -- even better -- the nuts.

Another problem is the twist-on lid. It doesn't stay secure, which means the nuts are going to get stale, and maybe spill.

I love salted cashew nuts spiced up with cayenne pepper, but this product is way too salty and hot. Cayenne pepper powder and salt lumps were found at the bottom of the canister. The product description says, it has "a hint of pepper," but this is an understatement. I have to say this is not one of the best Emerald products.

1. Cashew Party Bag - 5 lbs.
2. Whole Cashews, Rstd/Salted 8 oz.
3. Snacking Sensations-Almond Brothers Gourmet Nut Tray
4. Pecan Paradise-Almond Brothers Gourmet Pecan Tray
5. Everybody's Pistachios-SALT + Pepper

I found these cashews too salty and peppery for my taste. There is also a hint of onion flavor with some citric acid to give them a slightly sour taste. Some cashews were almost completely encrusted with coarse salt making them almost bitter in taste. I found it hard to have more than 2-3 cashews at one time. Combining a handful of these cashews with a cocktail is a sure way to get heartburn!

The price is also on the higher side. I prefer the store branded lightly salted and far less oily tinned cashews you can get at any grocery store to these.

I was quite excited to try these nuts and equally disappointed upon putting them in my mouth. They're greasy, not crispy and dry as I'd expected. This is a bummer both from a mouth-feel perspective (the nuts just don't feel right!) and from a sticky-smelly-mess-in-your-hands perspective as well.

I've had some wonderful sweet nuts and also savory nuts that are baked just right. These nuts, however, taste soggy, oily. And given how much I love both cashews and pepper... what a shame! :-(

Emerald Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews were quite a disappointment. The cashews are rather small and a bit broken up (which could have been from the shipping) although they seem to be of good quality. The problem with this product, however, is that it goes way overboard on the salt and pepper spices. They nuts are too salty and too peppery and just not very enjoyable. And they get even more salty and more peppery, thus less pleasant, the further down the container you go.

I love cashews, but these are ruined by the spices.

I love cashews, but Emerald Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews have too much pepper on them for me. They look dirty, taste peppery, and leave a burning sensation in my mouth. The pepper takes over completely and there is very little actual cashew-taste.

Emerald has some good products, like the Emerald Marcona Almonds, but this time I think they are trying too hard to be different. I am definitely disappointed and would not buy this product.

PS. I rinsed them off and they tasted fine. (Hardly an endorsement.)

I have the feeling that people are either going to love this or hate it. For me, I hated it. The salt and pepper combo is extremely aggressive. The chunks of salt are so large that sometimes they make a {crunch} when you bite down on a particularly large one. The pepper is also large flakes and there is a lot of it.

After just a few of these I felt a bit sick to my stomach and now even the thought of them makes me a little queasy. I have loved the Emerald product line up until this one. I do give them respect for taking chances but I think they went too aggressive on this one.

I enjoy a variety of nuts for snacks and cooking. This is definitely more the snack-variety.  I liked that the nuts tasted very fresh and had a pleasant aroma when I opened the canister. The canister itself is very convenient and wide enough to reach into for the snack without scraping your knuckles on a rough plastic rim.  The pepper flavor is significant, but not overpowering. A good balance.  However, I like salty snacks, but found this to be a little too salty, even at the risk of drowning out the flavor of the cashew.  If you like VERY salty, these are good, but if you like mildly salty, steer clear.  I can't even imagine how the ones on the bottom of the canister would taste.

Wow... VERY peppery! I love cashews, and I love salted cashews, so "Salt and Pepper" Cashews sounded intriguing... unfortunately, this product has too much pepper for me. The pepper overpowered the taste of the cashews. I would never buy these. I'll stick with good old salted cashews.

First off, let's start with the product description for these cashews that appears on the product page: "Lightly roasted with natural sea salt and a hint of pepper - Value added seasoning for the consumer who is tired of plain old cashews." From reading that description, one would assume that these cashews have "a hint of pepper." That is not the case. These cashews are LOADED with pepper. When I first opened the container and saw these nuts, it looked like someone had wet them and dredged them in black pepper. And believe me...You can taste the pepper; and it stays with you. Very, very spicy. Too much so for me. I also agree with other reviewers who have said the nuts are too salty. WAY too salty, with 270mg of sodium in a single 1 oz. serving. Now, back to the "value added seasoning" description...Nowhere in the product description does it mention that these nuts have SUGAR added to them. Sugar? With salt and pepper? Add that to the "granulated onion" that also appears on the list of ingredients and maybe you can understand what I mean when I say that there's just a bit too much going on here flavorwise. You can't even taste the nuts!! I love cashews. And I love seasoned cashews. But these just don't make the grade. I think my biggest complaint is definitely the amount of pepper that are on these. It's WAY more than a "hint." Stay away from these nuts unless you want to make your taste buds very, very angry and give yourself some major heartburn.

If you didn't like the taste of cashews, you probably wouldn't eat them. But this product seems designed for people who don't like the flavor of the nuts.

Your mouth is hit with lots of saltiness first, quickly followed by warmth from the pepper. You can get the same experience by sprinkling some salt and pepper on your hand and licking the spices.

No one could eat very many of these without a beer or other beverage that complements the saltiness and pepper.

The package shows lots of perfect cashews, but my package contained more broken pieces and halves than complete cashews. The package needed to be filled more completely to avoid breakage in shipment. These don't look good enough to serve to guests.

Stick to regular cashews!

My hubby loves salt and pepper anything and I had purchased other brands of Salt & Pepper Cashews in the past. He said that the Emerald were better at first: crunchier and had a more pronounced freshly-ground pepper taste. He said that they were much less salty than other brands he had tried.
Update:

Unfortunately, after eating them a few times, he told me that the pepper taste was becoming overwhelming and he adores freshly ground pepper, he must eat about 5 times the amount I do on food. Maybe it was just that he was eating too much at once?

I did notice that he went back to the Archer Farms brand that I had in the pantry, so I don't know if he'll be finishing the Emerald brand or not.

If anything changes, I'll update my review again.

I like the fact that the lid fits securely and they seem to stay fresh for a long time.

Firm, Crisp, Perfectly Salted with hint of Pepper...A little on the stronger side for people who dont like spicy....But I am the Spice Queen and these are absolutely Purrrrrfect for me. Infact they go really well with Drinks...thanks to the pepper in them.
If ur about flavor and taste..this one is for u.
It has become a regular feature for when friends come over...besides these are quite economical.
I have a thing for nuts anyways and who doesnt love cashews....Get them u wont regret it.

I think it's important to note that the "pepper" here is ground black pepper - not a spicy pepper like jalapeños - something I didn't realize when I ordered these cashews. But, no problem, I actually like black pepper. And I think the combination works very well here, except that there's a bit too much pepper being used - the amount could probably be cut almost in half. And the pepper is pretty strong, like freshly ground pepper, so it gives a good strong taste, but not so much that you don't taste the cashew. I thought it kind of overwhelmed the flavor of the sea salt but as I shared some around the office others thought the product was a bit too salty (I'm something of a salt-aholic). Nonetheless, everyone agreed that they're good enough to be slightly addicting.

As with the other Emerald nuts, the cap makes a great measuring cup for a serving - if you can limit yourself to a single serving. It's maybe not my first choice among the many excellent Emerald products, but a good snack for anyone who likes pepper.

Emerald's Sea Salt and Pepper Cashews are top quality roasted nuts seasoned with a generous amount of black pepper and sea salt. What that means is the flavor here is very strong and spicy, and for those, like myself, who like strong flavored snacks, these are very good. However, you won't be able to eat more than a few at a time. The flavor is that strong. Of course, maybe that's better than a snack you continuously pop into your mouth until you've devoured the entire container. Some may say that the salt and pepper overpower the nut flavor here. I disagree, though the heat from the pepper definitely lingers. I'm going to give a thumbs up on this tasty product, but with a strong warning that if you don't like things hot and spicy, you won't like these. There probably is a smidge more salt and pepper than necessary, the only reason I'm not giving it the full 5 stars, so perhaps Emerald could take note of that and lighten the amount just a bit.

As for the nutritional information:

Calories - 160 per serving (120 from Fat), Total Fat 13g (saturated fat 2.5g, trans fat 0, polyunsaturated fat 2.5g, monounsaturated fat 8g), Cholesterol 0mg, Sodium 270mg, Potassium 140mg, Total Carbohydrate 8g, Dietary Fiber 2g, Sugars 2g, Protein 4g, Calcium 2%, Iron 25%.

Ingredients: Roasted Cashews (cashews, peanut and/or cottonseed oil), Sea Salt, Peanut Oil, Black Pepper, Maltodextrin, Sugar, Granulated Onion, Citric Acid, Spice, Natural Flavor.

Allergy Info: This product is processed on equipment that also processes other tree nuts or peanuts. May contain tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, milk, soy, or sesame seeds.

First of all, I'm a cashew lover, so I figured I'd like these nuts. What I didn't expect was how much I'd like the sea-salt pepper combo. There's a slight 'twang' after eating a handful of these, and they are great with a cold beer or soda. Each nut is big and bold, no little pieces in this jar. The packaging is great; good for taking along on trips. The twist lid is easy on and off. If you enjoy spice, go for these, the pepper does give a little extra kick.

HOLY GUACAMOLE!!! Never thought I'd say this, but MAN I LOVE HAVIN' THESE NUTS IN MY MOUTH!!! As if cashews weren't already perfect enough, the Emerald guys decided that "nope; they need to be better"! They've gone and packed a whole bunch more flavor into an affordable can of already scrumpcious cashews. I'll admit every now & again you'll get a cashew so salty that your face'll contort into one of those stupid salt overload kinda faces, but those are few & far between. The pepper adds a great flavor & a little heat at the tip of your tongue, it's literally unlike anything I've tasted on a cashew before, AWESOME!!! Seriously, it was like god touched my mouth while eating these suckers. Oh well, he giveth & he taketh away. In the time it's taken me to write this review half of my stash is gone :(. If you're looking for something semi-healthy this is for you. Pimp My Cashew Baby!!!

Now if only we could get some Wasabi flavored cashews (Hint! Hint! Emerald)
I love Cashews, but this product SUCKED! It had too much Pepper. I washed them off and put them in the toaster oven to freshen them up. Now they are semi descent.

I love cashews but wanted to get several different opinions so I brought this in to be enjoyed by all of my coworkers.

It didn't last three minutes.

Personally, I loved them. The picture shows some cashews lightly covered in pepper but when you open this up there is no light covoring. These things are three times as smothered in salt and pepper than the picture depicts. The taste was fantastic! It added a lot of flavor to cashews and brought them to an entire new level. They do have an after-taste, but it is a good aftertaste so you can enjoy them longer than they last in your mouth.

Now this is all opinion, but I hope you can trust this lover of cashews. How quickly they disappeared amongst coworkers should be further testament to their tastiness. One of them even hunted me down asking for more.

If you love cashews, at least give these a shot. I haven't found anybody yet who didn't enjoy them.

The product description currently states that these nuts have "a hint of pepper."  Don't you believe it.  There's at least as much pepper on these as there is salt, and there's too much of both.  I can't taste anything but the pepper when I eat them, and they're so salty that I'm thirsty afterwards.  This is a terrible product, and the company needs to seriously scale back their seasonings.

Do you like cashews? You've never had them like this! I have never met a nut I didn't like, so of course I volunteered to try this new product. I looked at the container and thought, hey yeah, cashew snacks -- gotta be good, right?  Well not only are these GOOD, they are completely and utterly sublime. The blend of sea salt and pepper adds just the right spice to the cashew. I could eat this snack all night! It will add a little zip to an otherwise ho hum dish of nuts at a reception or party! I am currently trying to figure out how I could use them in another recipe -- say for instance, a chinese rice and cashew chicken entree????  YUM! Get some today!
Sooo much pepper and heavy salt - reminds me of "Adams" trick food gags (garlic candy, hot pepper chewing gum, etc. ). Can't eat as is - seriously , these are fresh nuts - just over seasoned.

I picked these up at the grocery store the other day just to try them out, and boy, are they super-salty!  I can only have a couple before I have to chug a glass of water.  The pepper taste is fine but they really need to cut down on the amount of salt used.  :(

Too much, not enough, needs this and that.  This was the surprise I wasn't expecting, and I almost put them back on the shelf.  The reason I am here is to look for other nuts with the salt and pepper (and onion).  I was hoping you had peanuts with the same additions.  You have a winner here, try it with other nuts.
Not terrible. The seasoning is a bit  overpowering, a little too much onion. Cashew is a mild flavor to begin with so the seasoning was a little too much.

I ordered the cashews and the first order I received was great...could have used more pepper, but that's just my taste. I thought they were fantastic, so I decided to autoship them. My very first autoship order was HORRIBLE!  Way, WAY overseasoned.  I didn't mind the extra pepper, but they were so salty they were inedible.  Unfortunately, I was hoping the problem was limited to only one container, so I opened them all, and they were all inedible.  I was very disappointed, so I cancelled my autoship. I see no reason to keep paying for something and you're rolling the dice on the quality.

This product contains genetically modified cottonseed oil. There is no excuse for a premium nut company to be using GMO oils in its products. I'm finding it more and more difficult to find nuts that don't have GMO oils. And now Emerald has sold out too!
My new favorite snack.  While visiting my son in Richmond, had the opportunity to try these.  They are delicious.  Love them.

I love cashews and I love pepper. The first time I bought these I thought they were great. Then a friend gave a canister to me as a gift and they had tried Sea Salt& Pepper cashews and they were not sure they liked them. I was surprised by their comment and then tried some of the cashews from their canister and immediately noted that they were much saltier than the cashews I had tried previously. I later tried the cashews they had given me as a gift and those too were much too salty! I thought at that time maybe it was just a "bad batch". I had almost decided to not buy any more but then gave them one more try and once again found them delicious and not too salty! I have bought more since then and some are too salty and others are not! I plan on letting Emerald (Diamond Foods) know about the inconsistency because when they are not too salty they are REALLY good!!!
Update: 7/12/2012. Diamond Foods responded promptly to my complaint that the product is inconsistent by sending me a coupon for $5.99. But unfortunately the product continues to be very inconsistent. The last few packages I have bought have been way too salty--so sadly I will not purchase any more! Once again--if you are lucky enough to get a good package they are great!
Great concept but just way too much pepper. The combination would be perfect and this product would rate 5 stars if they just held back on the pepper by 50%.

I received a package of these in a birthday gift basket. I love cashews. I love salt. And I love pepper. So I expected them to be good, and I wasn't disappointed. The pepper gives the cashews a nice kick without being overpowering or too spicy. (Note that I like spicy food, so my palate may not match yours!) Definitely a nice change of pace from normal cashews seasoned only with salt.

I have purchased this particular item several times (10-12 canisters)and have been somewhat disappointed in at least half of these purchases.  I don't know how the process is done when adding the salt and pepper, but on most of the containers I have purchased, the salt and pepper did not stick to the cashew - hence, just another cashew!  I have waited for months in between purchases to see if the next canister is better - sometimes yes, normally no.  I don't know if I will continue to take a chance on purchasing these really good cashews (when S&P adhere to cashew)as they are rather expensive and I am tired of not getting what I pay for.
This are large great tasting lightly salted. I really enjoy them and they arent over powering.

This product was very good! i am not sure what people were referring to when they claim "the heat was turned up in this"....maybe these folks are super sensitive to spice. I found the flavors to meld wonderfully together, a fresh tast combination! i am desi and have aquired a taste for heat, so to me, these were not in the least bit spicy...they were, in fact, tasty...salt with a bit of a pepper flavor. i loved them and couldnt keep my hands out of them! i also got rave reviews for them when they were presented as part of the appetizers for a party i had. dont be shy about trying them...they are realllyyyy good!

I was surprised to see all the people complaining about the taste.  I thought these nuts were really good.  I enjoy mixing them with raisins.  The combo of textures and tastes when mixed with raisins is really good.  Yes, these nuts will make you thirst so have some water handy.

I have looked long and hard for a great affordable everyday tea. Between us my wife and I drink about 2 1/2 to 3 liters of tea daily. This tea can be found for 4-5 cents per tea bag and holds more than other teas such as Lipton. For me a good tea should be able to sustain a long brew time to get the most flavor without an excessive tannin taste. I can brew the amount above for 5 1/2 minutes with only 3 teabags. 4 bags would suit others. We put the tea in an airpot and it tastes good all day. Just try that with Lipton "tea dust". It has been stocked in our local grocery stores over the last couple of years and I buy several boxes at a time. I bought 12 boxes from Amazon though because it was cheaper and tea keeps for months if not a year or more. I hope this tea catches on. Only 4 stars as there are other better tasting teas, such as Empress from Fairmont Hotels or a good pure Assam, but as noted this is a great economical everyday tea.
They right amount of tea in the bag for a true cuppa tea, british style. Wait for it on sale. I decided might as well spend the money and get a good tea you enjoy.

I found this recently at Walmart and have practically bought them out!  It is the only worthwhile tea to drink in this country.  I am convinced that the only reason the US prefers coffee is due to the poor quality of tea available here.  Anyway, if you're used to the strong, milky cuppa that is popular in the UK, this is all you need.
I love this tea.  It's just like what I used to get when I lived in Canada. It has great flavor.  I'll continue to purchase this from Amazon.  Thanks Amazon for the fast shipping.

I drink a lot of tea, usually 2-3 liters a day. Of all the teas I have tried, Tetley British Blend and Twinings English Breakfast are my two favorites. If I had to pick one tea, it would definitely be Tetley British Blend.

If you like a strong but smooth tasting tea without bitterness or a twang, Tetley BB is a tea to try. The little round tea bags are great with no bleed through. It is good for hot/iced tea, sweet or unsweetened. To me, Tetley tea BB is the perfect tasting tea. It is what tea should taste like. In my opinion, you will not find a better quality everyday tea for the price.

Also, one case of Twinings Breakfast Blend, 120 tea bags, is about the same price as one case of Tetley, which is 480 tea bags. So Tetley is by far the better deal.

Tetley Tea's British Blend is our family's favorite; so much so that we have it on a subscription service through Amazon.com.  So many other teas are weak tasting, but this product tastes robust and delicious even when you add ice to the drink.  It really is a great tea.

I take this tea with me everywhere I go in zip lock plastic bags, just in case I cannot purchase it on trips. It is the ONLY tea I will use now. I used to buy Stash and Yogi other nice lines of tea (pricier too!) but I am so in love with this, I will never buy another brand. I pray they don't stop making it. All other brands of tea now give me terrible heartburn. This one soothes my tummy and makes me a very happy woman :-) I typically purchase by the multiple boxes, such as at least 4-6 boxes at a time. I live in a very rural area and it's difficult to get out to "the store", meaning the ONE WalMart within 45 miles! LOL. Otherwise, I do all of my shopping for items like this online, which is much easier. Thanks, Tetley and thanks Amazon, for being there for me in a crunch when I was almost out of tea!

I was thrilled when I saw Amazon sells this product. It is very hard to find in my area so I purchased five boxes. I live near the Canadian border and was raised in Canada so became used to British tea. I normally drink Red Rose (Canadian) and have since I was a child. Now it is so difficult going across the border to get the tea so I tried and finally found one that satisfied my taste in this Tetley product. If you are a tea drinker I think this one is so full of flavor and so close to the Canadian Red Rose you will enjoy it as I do.

I noticed Amazon also sells the Canadian Red Rose but they are out of it, when it returns I will order a full supply for myself. Or may even try crossing the border again to go shopping in Canada.

When I lived in England, I used to buy this type of Tetley tea. Of all the English teas, this was my favorite. English tea is strong and mellow, whereas American tea is weak and bitter. British Tetley was the best English tea. It is nothing like American Tetley tea. Completely different. Buying this British Tetley from Amazon is no more expensive than buying regular American tea at the grocery store, postage notwithstanding. I order case after case; never get tired of it. Serve it, after steeping it in fully boiled (not just heated or warmed) water, with milk and sugar, the English way!

It smells like tea, that's the first thing. As soon as you open the box, it permeates your breathing passages. A really nice touch is the serrated lid so that you can tear off the lid and the side top flaps to get a nice container that fits perfectly in the kitchen drawer under the counter where my kettle is. Generally, I'm a coffee drinker, but my family likes tea occasionally. My daughter is very fond of British teas. This one brews up very bold with just a ton of flavor. Most teas I won't add anything to them. This one I need to add a bit of milk or sugar to because the flavor is so strong.
It's excellent iced, and one of the more affordable teas we drink.

I agreed with all these rave reviews. BUT, maybe 6-8 months ago they changed this tea and ruined it. It is pathetic as lipton or any regular tea. I like a bold flavor with cream "british style" I, even, tried 2 tea bags and  it still did not taste the same. I have used this tea for years and am exremely picky about my tea. Having tea, is a big part of our family day. I have change to british PG TIPS tea or Irish Breakfast tea. It is not the same- but, they are pretty good.
I love good, old-fashioned black english breakfast tea.  Tetley fills the bill.  Good hot or cold for ice tea.

I would only recommend this "meal" to people who enjoy junk food and fast food and who are going to eat it anyway. The good things about this mac and cheese cup are that it tastes pretty good, it is convenient and easy to fix, and there are no dishes. If you want a little taste of fast food (220 calories), but don't want to leave the house, have money to spend and care nothing about nutrition, you've found a terrific product.

The negative things:
(1) It is super-high in carbohydrates at 40g per 220 calorie serving. Definitely to be avoided if you are diabetic or are pre-diabetic or don't want to be.
(2) It is high in sodium at 670mg for just those 220 calories--yikes!
(3) The ingredients list is long and reads like a chemical formula. If this is what you eat anyway, you might not care. But if you're used to real food, it does have a kind of synthetic odd off taste to it. I liked it initially, but it lingered with me for a while afterwards and I had to keep drinking water to wash the aftertaste away.
(4) It is mostly white rice flour, corn syrup solids (sugar), and fake cheese. Please don't feed this to your children. Whatever you do.
(5) As mentioned above, terrible for nutritive value--no nutrition whatsoever besides calcium (6% of your daily requirement) and iron (8% of your daily requirement). No other vitamins or minerals.

Only recommended if you're already used to fast food and junk food and if you also don't care one bit about nutrition. I gave it two stars because if you're that type of person anyway, it's not a bad choice as at least you're not getting the gluten. You're not getting anything else either except empty calories, but if you can handle the chemically aftertaste, you might upgrade your diet by avoiding the gluten.

Being an avid BBQ fan I wanted to branch out into sausage making but I didn't want to break the bank on equipment. This weekend I put the 38237 through its paces making about three pounds each of snack sticks, Polish sausage, and summer sausage.

Pros: Very precise control of the speed and quantity of sausage exiting the gun. Casings were easy to fill and the three tube selections gave me the appropriate size for each product. The tool is sturdy, heavy gage metal and plastic, which by the way is the slightly flexible kind (think the heavy, old school Tupperware bowls) so it feels strong and durable, unlike the cheaper clear plastic models that look like they would crack from use or shatter if dropped. The pump trigger could be operated one handed, leaving the other hand free to control the casings. Unlike a grinder-powered stuffer, simply pressing and releasing the trigger allows you to adjust the speed and stop the flow of product with precision. The gun was easy to disassemble and clean. I always clean kitchen apparatus by hand, so I can't speak to it being dishwasher safe. Also, I don't make extruded jerky, but the performance with snack sticks makes me feel it would be fine for that as well.

Cons: Instructions extremely sparse, practically non-existent. Difficult to load product without getting air pockets in the cylinder. I found a video online for a competitor's product that recommended pre-rolling the sausage into a tube shape slightly narrower than the gun's cylinder which helped quite a bit.

Conclusions: I'm happy with the performance of the product and the price I paid. Eastman Outdoors includes accessories with this unit that others charge extra for, making it quite versatile. Although I would recommend a mechanical stuffer for very large batches, this unit is ideal for stuffing a few pounds at a time.

Also, I needed to replace one of the nozzles (damaged in the dishwasher) and the part at the end of the plunger that pushes the meat out. Unfortunately, replacement parts are not available for this item.

When I opened my Eastman 38237 Jerky and Sausage Gun kit, I noticed that the piston seal made of a nylon like material was damaged with a tear very evident. Perhaps it was damaged when the cylinder was placed over it(inserted) because the cylinder entrance on both sides is not chamfered at all and presents a sharp edge to the flexible lip seal. In any case it seemed like the damage wouldn't prevent me from trying to stuff my first batch of sausage. I only tried to stuff about 3.5 lbs of meat with this device and I would say, that is about the most I would try unaided. The control was excellent in terms of moving the meat mixture into the casing even if slow. My biggest disappointment was the tediousness of filling the narrow tube with fresh meat. It seems like the narrow tube holds a bit under 1 pound per loading. The small diameter of the tube made it difficult to refill with the sticky meat mixture without creating massive air pockets. I have to admit that the manufacturer responded to my damage complaint and sent me a new kit free of charge.
It is a completely different model (38239) which I haven't found too much information yet. The tube, piston and mechanism are completely different and the tube is now chamfered. Instead of screwing on and off the tube to refill, the tube slips out of the cage type holder. In addition, the new one's mechanism for advancing the piston is now completely open instead of closed which should allow for the ability to thoroughly clean it. I haven't tried it yet but I think it may be a better choice for small batches than the original one. However its tube diameter (1-7/8") is even smaller than the original (2")so it will hold even less meat and be more difficult to refill. These small, caulking gun types of stuffers are ideal for the small home sausage maker, but when I decide to stuff more than about 3-4 pounds at a time, I will have to invest in something more appropriate.
I would say that the value was very good for the price, but it's probably a better jerky maker than a sausage stuffer due to its size.
