This Keebler Cookie & Cracker variety pack has 36 small pouches inside. 9 mini Fudge Shoppe Fudge Strips cookies, 9 Cheez-It, 6 Animal Crackers, 6 Scooby-Doo cinnamon Graham Cracker Sticks, and 6 mini Chips Deluxe Rainbow cookies. I like all of them and think they all taste great. Each pouch has just the right amount to give a little snack - not too much. Just one note about the name is this item. It's called a Cookie & Cracker Assortment on the box. But because of the sugar content of both the animal crackers and the graham crackers those are more cookies than crackers making the box mostly cookies - with the Cheez-It the only true cracker.

These snacks maybe most suitable for young children ages 5-12, but they're also perfect for a busy and hungry college student. Why? It's convenient, and it's tasty, perhaps slightly better than your typical vending machine/fast food because of the controlled serving portions (each pouch is about one ounce in weight).

As of the time of writing, at $10/box, it's not cheap, but if you compare it against retail/school dining choices, it's kind of a bargain, because each pouch comes out to be about 25 cents per pouch. This is one-fourth of the cost of your average vending machine snack. To make it more worthwhile, for college students, Amazon throws in the free shipping with Amazon Prime, which means that it gets delivered straight to your door, which is a HUGE time saver, because you don't need to drive out to the store and buy snacks. Plus, PORTION CONTROL! (of course, this requires resisting the temptation for second serving of snacks, which admittedly is hard to do so)

My least favorite snack in the assortment is the animal crackers. They're just really dry and tasteless, almost like a cardboard substance. But I think they're are only six of them in the box, so it's not too bad.

My absolute favorite snack has to be the fudge cookies. They are AMAZINGLY good. The fudge/chocolate melts in your mouth and the cookie is kind of buttery and melts along with the fudge/chocolate. It's really good. My only problem with the cookie is that they market it as a shortbread cookie, which it really isn't ... it's just a fudge cookie. Everyone knows that the Scots/Brits are the best at making shortbread cookie. Nonetheless, digression aside, the fudge cookies are awesome in their own right.

Anyways, try one! The assortment isn't perfect, but if you're short on time, you won't regret it.

I bought these when they were a lighting deal for an amazing price because I thought they would be nice to keep in the car or stroller so snacks are easy and available. It was great intentions, but my 2yr old had one pack of scooby snacks and decided they were his new favorite treat so we've also given them to him inside and he likes being able to carry a snack around in his own little bag.
The only thing I wish was that they had a more equal # of each snack.
Nice and convenient and if you find them for a good price, worth the buy

The freshness wasn't a problem with this order...however there was a problem.  The chocolate on the Fudge Stripes was all melted off of the cookies and was stuck to the inside of the package.  Another no go for repeat sales.

If you need to portion control your snacks or have something tasty to throw into a lunchbox, this Keebler Cookie & Cracker assortment can't be beat for value! There are several types of Keebler snacks, but more cookies than crackers. The animal crackers are my favorite and since I live in a humid area of the country, buying them in small packages means I won't open a large bag and have it spoil before they are eaten.

With prime shipping, this is an unbeatable bargain!

As a busy Mom I'm always looking for quick and easy ways to feed my son. He has a very healthy appetite but often times he has his preferences, this is the ultimate snack pack with a variety of each snack. My first thought was that they were really small packages but on the inside they hold more that I thought possible.Totally worth the price.

You can not go wrong with this box of snacks. It is the perfect amount for that snack just before a meal when the kids can't seem to wait. I hate it when they grab a box of cookies or crackers and end up munching the whole box down before a meal. This solves that. Just limit them to one package and the problem is solved.

They are also the perfect size for lunchboxes and diaper bags. Take some with you for a Dr visit or other engagement to keep the kids happy. But best use is for parties and family gatherings so you will not have a big bowl or platter of waste left over. Any uneaten bags are easily restored unlike a plate of stale crackers or cookies the guests just pushed around. Besides having their very own little bag of snacks helps kids feel more comfortable. And will help keep the piggies from eating too much.

Well im in a college dorm so i need all the snacks I can get. The fudge ripples are definitely the best. The animal crackers are a weird knockoff and the cookies are extremely dry and grainy. Overall though i would recommend it as an alternative to late night vending machine runs.

Ordered this right at the end of November and was surprised to see that the expiry date was the first week of March. I ended up giving them away at a party in January because I don't think my two young children would be able to finish the many packets before March. Also, many packets had biscuits in them that were badly broken up. I guess this is not a good item to be ordered online and delivered. Will stick to buying these biscuits from the supermarket.

On a positive note, I did enjoy the variety that this box of biscuits/cookies provided. However, I don't think I will be ordering them online again.
The recipient enjoys having the snacks available in fresh packets. He mostly liked the Cheez-Its. This assortment might be better for a family with children.

When they first came in the mail I opened it up and gave one to my dog, who is a small 10 year Shitzu/Pekinese/something else mix, we call LueLue. She is getting more discriminate in her old age but she was eager to tear into this treat. For about an hour she went off and chewed it. Since then she hasn't touched them. I find them laying around the house. She just snubs her nose at them.

I wish my 3 dogs would have liked these more, but none of them really likes peanut butter, so these were just okay. I wanted them to like them because they're good for them, but, although they ate them, they didn't treat them like anything special. Usually if they get a treat they really like they run off with them, each to a separate area. These, they took, and eventually ate, but they didn't hide them, or run off with them. These are probably great for dogs that love peanut butter, but not one of my dogs does.

If your dog likes peanut butter treats, I'd definitely give these a try, but I won't be buying these for my picky dogs.
My dog really loves the FunBites MiniCongo Digestive support bones. She goes wild for the inside and will chew the outside after. Overall, I highly recommend as a safe dog snack.

These treats might be fine for larger dogs, but they were not good for my 13-pound miniature poodle.

At first he wasn't really sure what to do with it, but he finally started chewing on it. The outer rawhide separated and the dark center came out. My dog abandoned the rawhide at that point and concentrated on the flavored "filling." The package says one per day for a dog of his size, but I should not have let him finish it. Although he didn't throw up the treat, he seemed to be a little "off" after eating it, as if he wasn't feeling very well.

These are probably OK for a large dog, but I will not give another to my miniature poodle. And I would not feed even a large dog more than one a day, despite the package recommendation.
It took our dogs a little while to warm up to these, but they sure enjoy them now!  I haven't noticed any digestive difference, though.  They are a good size for our small dogs.

Generally when she eats grass she up chucks it, she hasn't since a few days after starting with these. Her breathe is also noticeably better. She is 10 years old and you can see that some of the crap off her teeth has come off since chewing these. I give her one a day.

I gave the bigger version of these to my dog Murphy, and he seemed to love them. These arrive from Amazon pretty fast as usual, and I soon unleashed a few on the big guy. Chomp Chomp Chomp... he was chewing away... I read some other reviews where their dogs had issues with these bones. I checked on my dog a few hours later, and he was fine. Its hit or miss with these. I own a english lab btw.

If our dog could talk he would tell you how much he appreciate these leathery treats that taste of peanut butter and contain papain to assist in digesting the hide.  Whenever I give him one he takes possession of it eagerly and goes to work on it.  Usually he takes a break in the middle but then he'll go back and work on it some more.  On one occasion, he had a bone that he really shouldn't be chewing but he willingly surrendered the chop bone for one of these treats.

The pets seemed to enjoy these about as much as the FunBites Calcibone. A product that they enjoy,
while providing them with healthy digestive support?

A good product for our pets (and yours, too)!

May I suggest that you (and your pets) try them?

I rate FunBites MiniCongo Digestive Support...4 stars!

I rarely give 1 star reviews, but how do you rate it higher if it does...nothing?

First of all, I was a little surprised by how large these "mini-Congos" are. We have an 8-pound Pomeranian and the only reason I chose these is because of the word, "mini".

The "mini-Congo" is a full inch in roundness and about 3.5" long. When you go to the pet store and buy "mini" treats, they are about the size of a matchbook or so. This seriously looks like something for a medium-large sized dog. I can only imagine a regular "congo" is enormous, heh.

But all dogs love bones and they all love to chew on something, right? Well our Pomeranian is not impressed. He looked at it, licked it for a little bit and left it alone.

We also give him these "dental sticks" and he hates them (well he doesn't devour them like he does a real treat). He will lick them and put them away for awhile and if we don't give him any treats for a couple days, he'll go ahead and eat the dental stick.

Well it's been over a week now and he won't go near the "mini-Congo" treat at all, in fact he'd rather go eat the "dental stick" he doesn't like.

So it is confirmed, our dog simply does not like these, plus he can't even put his bite around it to begin with. Caution - these are not so "mini" for your "mini" dog like our Pomeranian.

Two paws down says Chocco.

I have really finiky eaters but so far they have loved all these fun bites products. Usually they would just turn their nose up at dog treats but they chew and chew on these and it's good for their breath and teeth. They last quite a while too.

I can't really speak to the digestive support benefits of this product. I'll assume it works, but only if you can force your dog to eat these. My experience:

I gave one each to my obese Jack Russell (Gizmo)and blind diabetic quasi-chihuahua (Bruiser). These guys are true chow hounds and general treat fanatics. Gizmo had to work hard to finally get his softened up and eaten. (He has big, strong jaws). Bruiser couldn't even scratch the surface on his. He finally discarded it, and Gizmo (a treat thief) wasn't even intterested in it. I put the treat back in the package unscathed.

Plan B - I introduced these to my daughter's two large and very hungry ex-racer greyhouds, Mosche and Canova. Mosche (the bigger stronger of the two) examined his and abandoned it. Canova struggled through his with little enthusiasm.

After reading some of the other reviews describing digestive problems brought on by these, I'm not going to even take a chance. The dogs don't like 'em anyway so into the trash with what's left. Thumbs down on this one.

Who doesn't love Peanut Butter? My pup sure does. She chewed and chewed on these "mini" congos. She is generally pretty picky but definitely gives these 2 paws up.

My only complaint would be the recommendations on the packaging. They say they are for small dogs, once a day and there isn't much mini about them. I took it away from her after awhile because I felt a whole one of these is just too much for a small to medium dog. They are probably a good size for larger breeds. You might want to pace your little one on these. Unlike several comments on here, she did not experience any digestive problems but that might be because I didn't give her the whole thing at once.

Overall, she liked them and I would recommend them. Just use with caution. Remember you are the best advocate for your pet.

The pups loved these--well they're peanut butter so who wouldn't love them?  They went through the package of 7 bones in about 3 days--fighting and growling over them as if they were protecting a fresh killed antelope on the Serengeti.

I have 3 dogs - a Grey Hound, a Boston Terrier, and a Chihuahua/Rat Terrier mix.  They all love various kinds of treats, and will also chew on generic rawhide when I purchase them sometimes.  Due to the size of the FunBites MiniCongo Digestive Support chew, it is only appropriate for my medium and large dogs.  (They are too hard to break in half for the small dog, which is what I've done sometimes with other kinds of treats.)  As to my 2 larger dogs liking the FunBites, I'm not too sure. Therefore, I cannot recommend FunBites MiniCongo Digestive Support, since my dogs will not chew on them.

My dogs sniffed these chews and then left them ignored on the floor for the next week.

Finally, I picked them up and since they had not been chewed , I figured I'd pass the bag to a friend, rather than waste them.

Since my dogs would not chew them, I cannot recommend them.(My dogs are not very fussy with chews)

I'm unsure why they lack appeal for my dogs, but having them lay on the floor so long, there's definitely a lack of flavor or scent. They are not inexpensive either.

I'm sorry that my dogs could not give them a second chance.

I miss-read the label and thought they would be good treats for my 4-pound Yorkie and 5-pound Maltese. Problem was, the treats were nearly the same size as the dogs. They might have liked them but there was no way they could have eaten them.

So I gave them to the neighbor who has a German Shepherd. The 90-pound dog ate them down as if they were M&Ms. I think the dog would have given me a thumbs up if, of course, he had thumbs.

The dogs love, really love these things.  We have two Yorkies and they were climbing all over each other to get the treats.  Normally this would be a good thing, however we have two concerns.  The first is a concern over eating so much rawhide and what it might do to their digestive tracts.  Taking it away from them in the middle of consuming it is a bit traumatic for both of us.  The second is there is a rawhide shell filled with something.,  It seems like a lot for little dogs.  For the time being, I've been cutting them smaller on the band-saw, however you can only go so small before you fear they will swallow it whole.  I'd like to see these in a thinner form at this same length.  That would provide less for the dog to consume.  On the other hand, if you have dogs over 10 pounds or so, they should love these.

The first time I gave one of these to my dog, she didn't get up until she finished it.  We like to give our dog rawhide as a treat instead of softer treats such as Beggin' Strips and she really seemed to enjoy this.  The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is because it leaves a mess.  We've decided to only give it to her outside because little niblets get all in the carpet.

My elderly 13+ year dog has experienced gastrointestinal issues for the last two years and I have to be very selective in my choice of treats. I was hopeful this digestive support treat would work out. I gave him one a week for 4 weeks and every time, within 12 hours, an incident followed. Though I can't directly connect the two (treat=incident), 4 timing coincidences was enough for me to stop short of giving him the last 2 treats.

He LOVED them ... which is why I gave them two, and not one, stars. But for a treat advertised as providing digestive support, at least for my dog, this is a 2 star product.

OK, so he's actually a Rottweiler Shar-Pei mix. He's 100 pounds of happy dog.

This package came with 7 sticks. He loves them and I gave him one a day.

He normally has a digestion problem, stopping to eat grass almost each time I walk him. I can honestly say that while he still stops to chew grass when I walk him, it's only a nibble here and there whereas previously, he'd "graze" like a cow.

I'm ordering more.

My dog is excited about the treat but hasn't finished one. That is not the norm for her. She loves her treats and will spend hours working on them. This one she goes to but never makes much of a dent into it.  So I can say it last a long time. I can't say she loves them.  I like feeding her a treat that is good for her. Just not sure she feels the same way.

I gave one to each of my dogs.  The little one, under 10 lbs, took a sniff and dropped it.  The thing was almost as big as her so it isnt for small dogs.  My medium dog couldnt get his mouth around it either and he is about 20 lbs.  On the flip side, my 50 lb dog tore the thing apart like there was no tomorrow.  He thought it was the coolest thing ever and chewed it to pieces.  In his opinion it was the coolest thing since sliced alpo.  Now, we must remember that these things would probably not be good for dogs under about 30 lbs.  I have a junkyard dog so I dont worry about his digestion because it is made of iron.  He did manage to plow through the treat in about 20 minutes.  As to the smaller dogs, they are out of luck I guess.  Anyway, it is a good item from the dogs sense.  They did all like the smell, and they did try to chew it up.  The little ones just were to lazy to try to get to the middle.  I will see if they eat more later.

I've got a Shih Tzu and a Jack Russell mix. I had no idea how large these FunBites were. After receiving the package, I realized it was too large for the Shih Tzu. He and the Jack Russell mix are the same size, but the mix is younger and has a larger mouth. I didn't even try to give it to the elderly Shih Tzu.

The other guy liked it very much. He carried it off and alternately chewed on it and hid it. He quickly got the coating off and essentially made it into two treats--a rawhide and a munchy. He sometimes has a sensitive stomach but had no problems with this one. It took him about 24 hours to devour the whole thing. I'll probably give him one a week.

(And really, keeping a dachshund occupied for long enough to be useful is a bit of a challenge, so they win on that account alone). She was a little hesitant about the first one but with every subsequent FunBite, she's eaten them more and more quickly -- I think this speaks well of their quality, because she can be a little picky!

These also don't leak anything all over the floor like some other chewies, which is great.

For once I have nothing to do with this product opinion. I left it all up to my dogs. I have two small dogs, a Chihuahua and a Min Pin. Both completely ignored the FunBites MiniCongo treats when I first gave them one. But after a day the Min Pin started going to work on it. She seems to like them but probably wouldn't bite me if I tried to take it away. The Chihuahua could care less and shows no interest at all. There seems to no health concerns yet but I'm keeping an eye on them.

Nice package, looks good,looks tasty but dog wouldn't eat it.  Our dog is not generally picky on what she eats but for whatever reason she didn't like chewing on these or want anything to do with them.  Not much else to say.

I read some of the negative reviews due to digestive issues with concern, but decided to try these on my dogs since my dogs are extra large with cast iron stomachs. My dogs are Irish Wolfhounds and even with their size, rawhide is not recommended in large amounts. These had a small amount of rawhide with filler. One dog is a food-aholic and the other is picky. The picky dog liked them, the food-aholic thought they were so-so--how could I tell--he didn't need me to say "gentle" to save my fingers from a chomp.

If your dog can digest these, it is a nice treat for them. Although they didn't provide the Wolfhounds with much of a rawhide chewing challenge as they had them ingested within a minute or less, they did like the filler. Didn't notice any change in their digestive systems, breath or with the male his, ummm, flatulance issues, but the dogs were happy and that made me happy.

I thought maybe these FunBites MiniCongo treats would be small enough for my lab mix. He certainly liked the idea of them. He carried them over to the rug where he eats his treats, and then put it down. I could tell that he was interested, but this is a very hard treat, and even the "Mini" is too large for him.

I picked it up and started to put it somewhere for another of our family dogs, one who needs this kind of treat to keep her from chewing on her leg, and my lab let me know he wanted the MiniCongo right where he had put it.

So, it's still there. I'm not sure why, but that's where he wants it. He can't do anything with it, so I'm going to grab it when he isn't looking and get it to the dog who will be able to do something with it.

I gave 4 stars, because although it doesn't work for our lab mix, this is probably a very good choice for other dogs. It's more of a problem with him than with the treat.

EDITED to say that my son's dog, a shepherd, loves these! He gave her one of the larger ones, not the "Mini", and she just carried it to the area where she takes treats and sniffed at it, trying to figure out exactly what she was going to do with it. When he came back a few minutes later, it was gone. These "MiniCongos" are built exactly the same, but they are cut in half, still too big for my lab mix, but either size will be perfect for the Shepherd.

I'm not the one who ate the product, but I am the one who had to clean up the vomit after the product was eaten.

I offered these new chews to my dog and at first he couldn't have cared less about them. For the record he loves chews, they are his drug of choice. I thought maybe he was just reluctant to try something new so I left the chew out for him. A little while later he ate it and seemed to enjoy himself but afterward threw up twice.

I'm not sure what the problem with these chews is but I won't be buying any for my dog and I certainly won't be recommending them to anyone else for theirs. I thought about giving the remaining chews to the SPCA for their dogs but then decided against it, what if it makes their poochies sick to? Sadly I had to throw the rest away.

I read other reviews and how these have caused some health concerns for their dogs, but I have not had that same experience.  Our active large sized Yorkie loves these and has ever since I have opened the bag.  She took the first one and walked around the house with it for about 5 minutes.  She has shown no hesitation when being given one of these treats and I have not found one left on the floor yet.  I am not able to comment on their claimed digestive abilities, other than than to say that I have not had any visible issues with it.  The bones in this bag are approximately 1"x3" in size and are rated for Medium and up dogs.  Our Yorkie seems to enjoy them and I would get them again in the future.

Gave these treats to our 2 greyhounds.  They chewed and ate a bit of the beefhide outer wrapping, but learned quickly to just mash it and make the filling come out. Once that trick was learned, they left the wrapping for me to clean up.  Our female has had an upset tummy, very gassy, so I am not sure if the treat contributed to this or not.  However it was the "new" thing added to the diet, so it is suspect.

These are a strange shape, and my dog couldn't quite figure out how to eat them.  We keep her lean, not feeding her much, and she always scarfs up any little molecule that happens to fall.  Not so with this.  She carried it around for a while, and then finally crunched it down.  Not the best treat.

My Golden Retriever loves these treats that I received through the Amazon Vine Program.  So does my Bichon, although  they are  a little big for him (10 pounds).  But he carried it around  & chewed on it daring anyone to come near.  I'm not sure if he is going to be able to eat it because of its  size , but he is protective of it.  DJ, the retriever ate his immediately & came back for more.  So far, their stomachs haven't been upset, so hopefully they will be good for their digestive system & not just another treat.  I  would  buy these again.

I can't say how much these actually help my dogs' digestive system, but before I opened the bag my two dogs were sniffing and nosing at it. I gave one to each and they gnawed on them with relish. The bag claims to have enzymes to help clean the teeth, which would be a definite plus. I have read the other reviews and I can say neither dog had an upset stomach. However, both dogs are one hundred pounds plus and have have fairly strong stomachs.

Well, the dogs (basset, golden and retriever) loved these! It took them about 30 minutes to completely finish these. I liked the quiet in the house. The bad part, these are not super nutritious and these contain grains, which can cause problems for dogs. Now, if this is for digestion, I wonder why all three dogs had the worst gas ever. The only thing different in their diet for the day was these FunBites. They are not normally gassy. This leads me to believe it was caused by this treat. Beware.

EDIT: After reading other reviews, it seems hit and miss about the quality of these rolls. Be sure to read the one-star reviews. I don't know if the reactions are breed specific. My old dog is a Rottweiler and the young one is a Cocker Spaniel who gets the runs from who knows what she has gotten into. She did not have a bad reaction to this product. However after reading about other dog reactions, and since I got these free through vine so no financial investment, I am going to throw away the rest of the bag.

I presented my two dogs each with a roll, which they both accepted, mainly because they are dogs not cats.
The roll is white rawhide wrapped around that crumbly mix used frequently to stuff these products.
One roll did not have a complete wrapper. My old dog quickly removed the wrapper and ate the center. The younger dog, a cocker, took the wrapper. I don't think that she ate it all, but it is out of sight at this point, probably hidden with other treasures.
The cocker chewed one end of her roll. When I found it later, the insides had moved a distance out one end equal to the distance on the other end that the dog had chewed. The whole thing has since disappeared. See previous paragraph.

Evaluation: For my dogs, one old and one under 25 pounds, the rolls are a pleasant challenge over several days. If your dog has strong young jaws, it can probably eat one roll in just a few minutes. I don't know about the digestive support. Neither dog threw up or had GI distress. At the rate they are consuming these (very slowly for intact rolls), I don't see how the rolls can have an effect on digestion. But if your dog is a quick eater and there's actually digestive support in the rolls, then these rolls could be helpful.

My dogs quietly and contentedly chewing away on treats... I have a mid sized senior dog and two young small Chihuahua's. Everyone is happy with their FunBites. My older dog is usually a major chowhound but this time she isn't able to make it disappear too quickly as she usually does. It's nice to see her getting to enjoy her treat. She in particular needs the digestive support the treat offers also, as well as the teeth cleaning. It's a win-win offer for my whole pack. I'm liking this product a lot.

From the first second I opened the package, my pit bull puppy has loved these treats.  It takes her a few days to get through them, so dogs with less strong jaws than a pit will take a while.  It smells fine (but I assume smells great to the dogs).  Also, it says it's nutritious.  Great product.

She ate this but not very quickly. Then she proceeded to stink up whatever room she was in for about the next 8 hours.

Looks like others are having digestive issues. Nothing life threatening here, just flatulence. She didn't care...we did.

I gave each of my 2 labs one of these treats. Both happily took the treat and went into their respective corners to eat it. My dogs are avid chewers and it took each dog about 5 minutes to eat the treat. The treat did leave crumbs but both dogs cleaned up every morsel.

A bag contains 7 treats. Each treat is about 3 1/2 inches long, and 1 1/4 inch in diameter. Each treat is filled with what looks to be ground rawhide which has an artificial peanut butter flavoring (I didn't notice any peanut butter smell). That is surrounded by a coating of rawhide. It seems to be easier to eat than normal rawhide (which takes my dogs much more time to eat). If you want a treat that takes a longer time to eat, (and your dogs are avid chewers), this isn't the treat for you. However, I liked the fact that this rawhide coating was easier to eat and I was less worried about a choking factor.

The treat is advertised as high protein and low fats. According to the packaging, it contains a minimum of 61% crude protein, a minimum of 0.5% crude fat; 3.5% maximum crude fat; and a maximum of 5% crude fiber.

Overall, I liked these treats. They seems a bit pricey, but my dogs seemed to really enjoy the treats. If it matters to you, these treats are made in Mexico.

I admit I have one of those spoiled dogs. I am not sure she knows she is a dog. She doesn't eat regular food, I make sure it is natural and doesn't have the wrong kind of additives. Her treats don't come from a box; I pick them out special, just for her. So when Amazon Vine gave us a chance to try these new dog treats we were excited.

They are called FunBites, but unless your dog is big, these are not bites. They are about two and a half inches around and three inches long. (I measured) The outside is hard rawhide and the inside is filled with a peanut butter looking substance. I don't normally give my dog rawhide because it can cause some health issues, but this says it has papain enzymes to facilitate protein digestion. It also says that they help clean teeth while chewing.

My dog loved it. She is a high-energy dog and treats that might take another dog hours to devour; she can take care of in minutes. This one did take her about fifteen or twenty minutes. I got the package out to look it over before I typed the review and she was all around to see if she could talk me out of another one.

I do spend more money on food and treats, but there were only seven "bites" in this package and you are getting four packages, so they are not an inexpensive treat. I haven't had them long enough to see how they affect her digestive system, but I will let you know. Part of what I look for in a dog food is the amount of protein, the front of the package calls this a daily treat, but they have 61% protein and I am just not sure that my dog needs that much extra protein every day. I think this is more likely a weekly treat.

These are better than the regular rawhide bones because it is a treat with a smaller amount of rawhide, and better than the crunchy bones because it did not fall apart and leave little pieces everywhere. So they seem to be a favorite.

So they must be good! They are a nice substantial weight, I was thinking they would be thin but they are quite wide. I have a boxer and he gobbled it right up when I gave him one. It seems like a pretty good value for the price, there are similar treats out there that are a bit more expensive (for only a couple in a package) so I would probably buy these over the other kind!

I have 4 cocker spaniels, 3 male, and 1 female weighing over 30 pounds each.  I gave them each a Funbites peanut butter flavored minicongo.  First of all, I don't give my dog's whole treats of this size.  Normally, one of these would be cut in half and I would make two treats out of them.  However, I couldn't cut through the white rawhide with gardening shears so each dog received their own minicongo.  My picky male promptly took his off and I didn't see him for 2 hours.  He busily and happily chewed all that time.  My female spent all her time growling at the boys and would never chew hers so I ultimately had to take hers away.  She wasn't upset; she just lay down and went to sleep.  My oldest male growled and barked over his for an hour but then eventually ate all of his and foraged pieces from the youngest one.  The youngest male spent 20 minutes so excited over it, he ran from room to room and then outside hiding it then going and getting it and he finally took it to the couch and chewed on his for the next two hours.  The dog treat is said to contain papain which I looked up on Wikipedia and it is an enzyme present in papaya used to break down tough meat fibers and is sold as tenderizer.  It is also used in small amounts in toothpaste as a whitener.  It's not just good for their teeth, but will whiten their teeth, also?  Just kidding.  I haven't noticed anything with the digestive system yet. The only problem I had with them was they were messy and small pieces came off as they chewed but they eventually cleaned all the pieces up.  The price is $22.15 for a 4 pack which is by my calcualtion $5.54 a pack and I think that's a bit much for a package of dog treats. All in all, my dogs loved them and I would buy them.

My two dogs really enjoyed these treats. Fiona, a little rescue mutt who's about 14 pounds, worked at her treat for a good two hours, with a couple of breaks in between (but only when her doggie brother wasn't around, since he would have stolen it). She loved it. Lately, she hasn't been very excited about her food, merely sniffing it in the morning and not eating much until later in the day. But this morning, after eating the Congo last night, she was thrilled about morning kibble again, spinning in circles before diving in and eating the whole bowl.

Finn, another rescue mutt who's about 35 pounds, also really enjoyed his treat. He spent the first hour burying it around the house and staring at Fiona while she snacked on her treat. Then he headed outside and snarfed it down in peace before coming back in to stare at her again. This morning, he was spunky and perky on his walk and, while he didn't eat his kibble this morning (it's too hot for him & he's only been eating at night), he did go out and patrol the yard, fertilizing the bushes, and scaring the squirrels.

So, by every indication, my two pups give these treats four stars and can't wait for their next treat.

We have a 9-pound Malte-Poo with dental "issues".

We need to keep her chewing on something all the time so her teeth do not get too much plaque buildup.

As soon as I opened the package and gave her one, she grabbed it in her mouth and took it to her spot where she likes to chew.

And there it has stayed.

I read the ingredients list:
Beefhide
Rice Flour
Maltodextrins
Dextrose
Caramel Color
Papain
Artificial Peanut Butter Flavor

Nothing too unusual.

They are MADE IN MEXICO - so if you are sensitive to things made outside of the US, just a head's up.
They are 1" around, and 3 1/2" long.
There are (6) in the package.

Hope this helps! =)

UPDATE:
Our dog will NOT touch these after her first attempt.
Someone was gracious enough to comment on this post and tell me that their dog got SICK on them.
We IMMEDIATELY threw the remainder in the garbage.

I have DOWNGRADED the number of stars from 4 to 1.

PLEASE DO NOT BUY THESE TREATS!!!!

I have one dog, an older beagle/basset mix, and my brother has 2 dogs (both corgi mixes), so we let all three dogs try the FunBites. The dogs loved them. The FunBites are not, in fact, bite-sized. Toy-sized dogs or very small dogs may have a hard time with them. The FunBite has a diameter of between 1 and 2 inches.

Each FunBite has a beef rawhide exterior that the dogs can chew/gnaw on. The center is an artificial peanut butter marrow. It must taste good because the dogs had to work to get through the rawhide to get to treat inside.

As a dog-owner I do like a treat that keeps the dog occupied for a while and does not leave a mess in the house. FunBites rawhide exterior keeps the dog busy. And the treat is not coated with sauce or anything so it is clean for indoor use.

I also like to know what I am giving my dog. The main ingredients in FunBites are beef hide and rice. It is about 65% protien and about 1.5-3.5% fat according to the package. It also has an interesting ingredient called "Papain" that is supposed to be good for digestive systems.

I did a little research into Papain: Papain is an enzyme found in papayas. It has many uses and is found in a wide variety of products. Its utility is in breaking down tough meat fibres and has been used for thousands of years in its native South America. It is sold as a component of powdered meat tenderiser available in most supermarkets.

I am happy with the FunBites. The dog enjoys them. The FunBites keep him busy chewing away on the rawhide exterior and the FunBites don't leave a mess in the house. FunBites are a high-protien dog snack which is good for dog's general health. The papain enzyme may also be beneficial to his digestive health.

Overall, any dog owner would do well by their best friend to buy FunBites.

This is one of those things where you can buy a treat and feel good about giving it to the dog. What's not to like? Digestive support through papaya which is also available as a human supplement too.

'Mini' is a bit of a misnomer though. They are about the size of a quarter - that is if you put a quarter on one end that is about how big the chew is round. Length is about 4 inches. So your doggie size is a big factor on deciding if these really are mini or maybe too big. They are too big for really small breed dogs.

The first one I gave my dog (he weighs about 20 pounds but he's lanky) he chewed it up in about 10 minutes. He's part cocker spaniel so he is a capable chewer if he likes what he is gnawing on. After that first one though he was a lot less excited to get the treat. Even if it'd been a day or two since he'd had any treat. He usually does finish it sometime during the day.

That isn't such a big deal since this probably should be a once a week treat.

[edit: updated Aug 4th, 2011

Well. The doggie is totally disinterested in these treats. Now he eats it after two or three days of being on the floor. I changed my rating to 3 stars because the dog has relegated this to a non-treat "I'll eat it when I am totally bored' type item.
/edit]

I have a 27-pound Scottie and, apparently, his weight was what saved him. Interestingly, my dog wouldn't take the treat the second time I offered him one.  Thank heaven!!! Within 24 hours of giving him this product, he started throwing up (and the "treat" came up almost intact) because it hadn't digested.  I took him into the vet when he started crying and was listless. The vet said if Jamie had been a smaller dog, the treat could have killed him.  So I'm out $127 for my vet and associated medicine.  I'm stunned Amazon would even handle this product!!!

Back from vet. Vet is about 100% sure it was this chew stick that upset my dog. His digestive tract is inflammed and will have to be on meds. He is not allowed to eat anything today. My vet said that even one is a lot for my size dog (I brought this to the vet with me), but bag said small dog, one per day (dog weighs 20 pounds). He said it obviously upset his digestive tract. He was throwing up bits of it over 24 hrs after having just one. The vet said my dog is VERY HEALTHY except for this. He is a little over a year old and in great shape...until he had one of these. AND FOR THE RECORD....My dog HAS HAD RAWHIDE chew sticks before with NO ill effects. I believe it is the inside of the chew stick that made him ill, as THAT is what he threw up. It is distinctive and hard to miss!

Particularly if you have a SMALL dog, I would be wary of this chew stick. I'm not saying it would upset ALL small dogs tummies, just that it is hardly mini and if my vet said it was too big for my 20 pound dog.

I have read a lot of dogs love this and did fine with it. Unfortunately mine didn't and it seems SOME other dogs (mostly smaller ones) didn't either.

Just trying to save dog owners the worry of seeing their dog in distress and a big vet bill.

My Boston thought these were AWESOME, and stole a second one from the package after I'd already given him one a few hours before.  After getting halfway through the first one, he threw up the entire thing.  That evening, he had pretty yucky diarrhea.  For that reason, I haven't given him any more since then.  In general, he's got a touchier stomach than a lot of other dogs, so maybe it's just him.  However, if you're going to bill this as offering digestive support, it better not cause my lil man to throw up and have diarrhea.  Wouldn't buy again.

My dog is a 15 pound Maltese. He is really picky about what he will chew, so I did not think he would like these, but I figured  it was worth a try to see if he would like them. I put it on the floor and he ignored it, just as I had expected. He  only likes a couple of types of chews. The next evening, I was happy to see he was chewing away at it with glee. He was really liking it, I was glad I found something he actually likes. But the next morning, he was throwing up, and had really bad diarrhea all day. Poor doggy! The ironic thing is that these chew bones call themselves "digestive support"  "Health and Fun" NOT!!!! I threw them away and will never give them to my dog again. I would not recommend these dog chews.

Family dog loves them...what more can I say. Smells pleasant enough for we humans to handle to feed to our furred loved ones.

He can be a little bit of a stinker sometimes so something that helps his breath goes a long way. Also, he's getting a little older and I think this helps his digestion.

In the heat my dogs don't want to go outside much so I am constantly looking for ways to entertain them inside.  I tried these one afternoon and for a good half-hour both dogs were thoroughly engrossed.  Upon offering them, a quick sniff was all they needed to know they WANTED this treat.  And after snatching it up, they each disappeared to a private place where they could enjoy it in peace.  I've had issues in the past with rawhide producing stinky farts but after each dog had consumed this treat, there were no after-effects, so that made me happy.  So all in all I am very happy with this product.

After our experience with other Funbites treats, I thought our dog Snowball would really enjoy these treats, but despite giving him these on different days, under different conditions, when he was hungry and when he was full, Snowball just wouldn't do more than sniff at them.

Why? I suspect that it must be the Peanut butter flavoring. He's always eaten meat or vegetable flavored food and treats, and the peanut butter must be throwing him. I may give the treats to a neighbor to see if their dog will eat them, but since these reviews are all about our experiences, I have to give this One Star - Snowball, a dog that I would think would eat ANYTHING, just won't give these a chance.

That said, I'll have to buy another Funbites flavor for him to see if he'll like these. He just loves the FunBites FlatSticks Calcibone, 60-Count (Pack of 5), so it isn't the outer "crunchy shell" - it's got to be the nutty flavor and scent.

This was the first treat we gave the dog (a 50 lb hound mix) after she was getting over some tummy troubles. She loved it and it lasted quite a while (they're fairly good-sized). She sort of ripped it apart, ate the inside first, and then ate the wrapping last. Though Lucy did have some problems again a few days later from some other treats, she had NO issues after eating these. I recommend them if you want a 'big' treat for your dog and they have recently been sick or have chronic tummy troubles.

I have a 60lb English Bulldog/German Shepherd mix who sometimes suffers from varying degrees of indigestion so I'm always on the lookout for treats to help reduce issues. Unfortunately, many doggie specialty treats are a bit on the pricey side if you want to give a daily helping. When these Fun Bites popped up on Amazon Vine I naturally snatched them up right away. Here are my thoughts;

Pros

+ High in protein, low in fat.

+ My dog loved them.

+ Contains papain enzymes.

+ Lasted about 20 minutes.

+ Resealable bag.

Cons

- Contains filler/rawhide material.

- Can leave a sticky residue.

- Treats are too large for smaller dogs. Approximately 3.5" in length.

- A bit pricey considering you only get seven in a package.

My dog sure loved these Fun Bites (although he's not terribly picky about treats) and guards them quite aggressively (not always a good thing). Sadly, I couldn't tell if he got any digestive benefit from eating these treats. Better suited for larger dogs who are average chewers these treats were nice but I don't think I'd pay the asking price for them. The best thing about these treats were they occupied my dog long enough to properly groom him without him constantly trying to bite my hands!

Kozmeaux (Shih tzu - Bijon frise mix) is a spoiled rotten house dog. He sleeps in the bed, begs for table scraps and thinks (or perhaps realizes) that he has the run of the house. He was completely uninterested in these treats. Sniffed it, walked away, and never returned. Now, in fairness to the treat, Kozzie is a picky, picky puppy and dislikes more threats than he actually likes.

Gator (American Staffordshire terrier) was given one as a bedtime snack. He didn't eat it right away, but the next morning, he was on his blanket and the treat was gone. He liked it, but I wouldn't say it's one of his favorites.

Grizzy (Husky-Chow mix) took hers out to the yard and proceeded to disembowel the treat, tearing the outer shell off and eating all of the peanut butter from inside. Once the peanut butter had been completely removed, she finished off the outer husk. Bonus points to the treat for Grizzy not only enjoying the treat, but being entertained by it as well.

These are large "raw hide" bone-size treats.  My dog loved them - and immediately tore them apart.  Be advised they are a bit of a messy treat - there were a lot of tiny particles left over - almost dust size - that I had to vacuum off the carpet.  Hard to tell if they really provide digestive support - but she loved them.

My dog, Oscar, loves these treats. Oscar has had some nasty digestive problems in the past and, even thought he's on a pretty restricted diet, he still has problems.
I tried these FunBites about a week or so ago and within days, there was a noticeable difference in his digestive issues--his problems have just about completely cleared up, he doesn't get gassy and his breath is so much better. I definitely recommend these for anyone's dog...whether they have digestive problems or not. The enzyme that is in the FunBites really improves there digestion, freshens their breath, and whitens their teeth. Plus they seem to love them.

Since I have an assortment of dogs, I was delighted to review the dog treats. I gave them to three German Shepherds, a cocker Spaniel and a Rat-cha. I am glad to say I only had one that got loose bowels and only for one day. It was one of the German Shepherds. All the dogs seemed to enjoy the treats, for its rare that I give them rawhyde. Although the Rat-cha had some difficulty with the size of the product, the Cocker and Shepherds had no trouble at all. They appeared to have liked them with no other negative effects. Although I am sure they would appreciate another taste, I don't think that I will be purchasing the product.

I ordered FunBites MiniCongo Digestive Support, 7-Count (Pack of 4) for my dog not realizing that they would be too big for my Shih Tzu's mouth. Since they are called "minicomgo" I got the wrong impression upon the size. My dog will lick the hard bone material so I know she liked the smell and taste, but laboring over the thickness is too much for her.

However, FunBites MiniCongo Digestive Support, 7-Count (Pack of 4) would most likely be lovely for a larger pet. I am loathe to give it a bad review because of my own ignorance.

These are supposed to be peanut butter flavored, but the filling neither smells like, nor resembles peanut butter at all.  My dog loves peanut butter and raw hide, so I thought these treats would be a hit. They are not. I gave him one last week, and it's still sitting on the floor, untouched. Sometimes he pushes it around like a hockey puck, but never tries to gnaw at the outside or dig out the filling. Obviously, I can't speak to whether they really do promote clean teeth and fresh breath as advertised. They are also a little on the large side, so if you have a tiny dog, these might not be appropriate.

My lab will eat any type of food he can find but is very picky about "chews."  There are only a few types he likes, and I've tried dozens.  I tried these recently.  This is now one of his favorite chew treats.  He really enjoys them, and unlike some other chews, he doesn't finish them off in a few minutes.  They last a good 15 - 30 minutes, which for my dog is a long time.  These are supposed to be good for his digestion, but unless I ran some type of controlled scientific experiment I'm not sure I can tell if this is true.  The ingredients seem reasonably healthy, although it does contain some artificial flavorings, which is not good. Overall I'm satisfied and  the dog likes them. Although they are a little pricey, I will probably buy more.

At first my chihuahua didn't go for these but after my wife figured that they were too big for him she cut off a piece about an inch long for him. Since they were cut down to a more appropriate size for him he really likes them now. It seems to be giving him a bit of a workout as it's taking him a while to work through the piece we cut off for him.

Original review appears first. Please read the bottom for the updated edit.

I've never given my dogs any type of rawhide product, so I can't tell if they like these any more or less than other similar products.

The size is described as mini, but they don't look that small. I thought the sticks might be too large for them but they each happily managed to pick them up and run to their corners. I never heard a peep from either for the next two hours, when they only budged to trace spots. They managed to eat about 1/3 of their stick in that time, and I took them away to save the rest for another day.

I read the review by the other customer who was worried after his dog became ill. If my dogs get sick, I'll update this review and the rating accordingly. But otherwise, they just spent two hours in doggy paradise.

UPDATE UPDATE UPDATE
Unfortunately we are not as happy now. I gave the dogs the minicongo treats again the next day and they loved them just as much. This time I took them away after they had eaten about an inch. Later, both dogs vomited the mixture and both had really weird poop. I threw away the rest of the package.

I have one siberian that will eat anything, including a small horse if it can fit in the dog's mouth, and the other siberian is such a princess she just licks and licks until she's full, which is usually very quickly.  So I was happy that both dogs liked these treats.  Unfortunately, both of them had diarrhea the next day and were high tailing it out the back door pretty fast several times in the same afternoon. This was the only thing that was different in their diet unless they got hold of a neighborhood toddler I do not know about. I hate to give a treat a bad review, because I know the people work hard to make a good product and no one sat around and said, "Well, so what if it makes a few dogs barf! We're rolling in money, hahahahahaha!!" but I have to speak the truth here, and the truth is, they appear to have given the dogs some pretty awful diarrhea. Sorry. They did eat it though and did not die, so 2 stars.

It's tough to review a treat for dogs, so this may be a bit short.  Bear gets one of these after our long evening walks; he now knows to expect them ans sits patiently while I get one out of the package.  He loves them.  I can't comment on whether or not they've improved his digestion, but there aren't any problems, so . . . !  Recommended.

Fun bites are too big for my 6 & 7 lb Maltese to handle easily and my littlest got sick and had to go to vet after eating one. I AM NOT saying the illness was caused by these but after reading others who had troubles it does cause concern. I will not purchase these.

Whenever I give my dogs something to chew on I hope it keeps them busy for a while and tire them out. These Fun Bites are too big for my Chihuahua (it is suggested for dogs over six pounds), but for my medium sized mix breed, it would take her about a half an hour to finish them off. I really cannot comment on the "digestive support" that the Fun Bites advertise but she does not seem any different as to the way then before she ate these.

What is annoying about this product is the labeling as they have important data and warning on the bottom of the package making it very hard to read it without ripping or cutting it. If it is important, how about putting the warning wear someone can actually read it?

Unfortunately my dog didn't go for this product. The bone casing was pretty hard for her to get through and the stuffing wasn't enticing enough for her to even try. She is a Shitzu but has no problem with hard bones or treats. She carried this one around for a couple of hours and then never bothered with it again.

As soon as I opened the package, Buddy, my 20 lb mini-Schnauzer was all eyes and ears. He disappeared with his MiniCongo, returning empty-pawed about 15 minutes later. About 10 days later, and Buddy's had about 3 or 4 MiniCongos, I made a startling discovery.

Buddy really likes these MiniCongos. He'd stashed them all beneath the sofa cushions. Now that we'd exposed them, he took them out in the yard, and buried them. Every now and again he digs them back up, chews on them a while, then buries them again so no one else can deprive him of his enjoyment. MiniCongos have to be very special because he's never done that with any treat before--food or toy.

We still have a few MiniCongos left, and every time we give him one, we have to follow him around to make sure they don't end up in the sofa. Yeah, if Buddy has anything to say about it, we'll be buying these again.

How to review a dog treat? I opened up a pack of these and tossed one to the dog figuring that might be a good place to start. After taking a minute to sniff and inspect the treat, my dog took it and promptly devoured the thing in a few minutes. Granted, my dog is quite large, but these definitely did not last as long as regular rawhide treats of the same size.

Next, I sat my dog down to interview him about the product. When I asked him if he liked the treat, he said "yip". Sweet, so they are a hit. I then asked them what they tasted like and he told me "bark". Hmmm, this seemed a bit peculiar. I thought they were supposed to be peanut butter flavored. I then asked him about the texture and he responded "ruff". So my dog liked a rough textured treat that tasted like bark, not exactly a convincing answer, but he was the judge. I was not about to eat one to see if he was right. He liked them and that was good enough for me.

I fed my dog a couple of these a day. Being a 90 pound dog, I was not concerned about feeding him two of these a day. However, when I went outside the next day, I was greeted by piles of diarrhea. In all due fairness to the treat, my dog did start a new medication (one he has had in the past with no issues) about this time. I honestly cannot say if the treats or medicine did this. I did not think of the treat causing this until I read other reviews. I will give the product the benefit of the doubt as it could have been the medicine, but given what I saw and what other reviewers went through, I would start your dog on these treats slowly if it is their first time having them.

i have a beagle mix, a miniature beagle, and a corgi mix and they all enjoyed these bones. took an average of about 15 minutes for the dogs to eat them and they left very little mess, mostly drool. they have a rawhide-ish outside wrap and in the center a softer center that sort of breaks off in pieces. they're suppose to taste like peanut butter. overall i'd recommend them since my dogs enjoyed them without any problems. if i could i'd ask them if their tummies felt better after eaten but well i'll just have to believe what the makers say,

I have two mini Doxies, one wouldn't touch this at all (smart dog), the other who will and does eat just about anything, tore right in. Unfortunately about an hour later, it came right back out... onto the carpet...

Needless to say we have moved on to other more digestible chews... I wish I had read the reviews before hand, I could have saved myself and my puppy the trouble and the mess.

My black lab ate them up. Loved them. My mixed breed akita mix did not even bother with them. Left his sitting on the ground for days until the lab found it. Not sure what to think. Nice size treat for large dogs. Lasted about 5 mins for my lab.

Not sure if it was just my dog's reaction to these (he's a 13 yr old Beagle) but I'll just say I wish I'd worn a gas mask about an hour after he ate his first one.  Didn't agree with his stomach at all, and made a mess on the floor because they got really gooey as he was chewing them.

I hoped my dogs would like these.  They eat most chews, but I thought these might last longer, and be gentle on their stomachs, based on the description.  One of my dogs is fussy, the other will eat almost anything, and they both turned up their noses at these, and I tried on a few different occasions.  Therefore, I cannot recommend them or comment on their digestibility.

OK....did my dog like these???  Yes!  Did I feel they were a healthy option for her?  No.  Honestly, unless I was home with her I would not give these to her.  I am concerned about choking or that a hard piece from the outer treat will be a problem.  These may help digestively, I don't know but when I am choosing to feed my dog Wellness Core why would I give her treats that were not of the same quality?  Dog nutrition is the most important things for your pet.  If I could afford to feed raw I would but since I can't I do my best to find high quality dog treats that I know will benefit my dog.

kinda hard to review something, that an animal must eat, who can not provide other feed back than "wag my tail and eat it" "eat it" "wag" or "vomit"...

i mean i put em down and the dogs licked a few times but didnt want it.

in my human opinion it failed. i cant tell why the dogs didnt like or want it. maybe they just werent hungry? maybe it smelled bad, but would have tasted ok..

each dog is different.. so try it for yours. maybe your dogs will like.

mine just didnt, and arent picky eaters either.

I had thought at first that my dog did not like these. He ignored the first one that I gave him and never got back to it. I finally threw it away.

A couple of weeks later I gave him another one and he chewed on it for hours. He has been equally fond of all of the ones that we have given him since then. I am not too sure what the issue was with the first one, but he really seems to like them.

Our baby girl, despite being almost 100 pounds, has always had a sensitive tummy. Anything can make her tummy upset.

I gave her one of these a day for seven days. While she had no upsets during that time, we didn't do anything to challenge her, like giving her a pound of beef fat. But more important, she loved them, seemed to look forward to them, and they didn't cause any digestive upset. Since there is nothing wrong with these, they have to get five stars.

These seem to be very popular with the resident dog in out house.  We have three tins loaded with treats and she gets most excited when we go to the one with these in them.  I have not had any of the problems with illness or other ailments mentioned in other reviews.

My two mongrels gobble down all treats but they didn't do it this time! They had to chew and chew on these babies to get to the end.

They must taste really good to the dogs because I had my daughter's two dogs here with my own pair and all four growled and guarded their individual Funbites. I'm sure that these treats are good for maintaining the dogs' teeth and I would highly recommend them.

Our pup, Banjo, loves these treats but they crumble and make a bit of a mess on the carpet as he chews on them. He did not experience an upset stomach or belly issues like some of the other reviewers.

My dogs are big, spoiled babies but I rarely buy dog treats because while they like them, most of the stuff out there is messy and smelly. FunBites Minicongo Digestive Support treats, however, were the exact opposite and they kept my dogs busy for a good while. The fact that the outside is covered in rawhide with the yummy stuff in the middle made my canine's work for the treat and let me tell you, they were occupied trying to get to the chewy center of these FunBites.

By their enjoyment alone I would buy these treats again. Most definitely.

Natalie S.

I have 3 dogs, 2 of them ate these and got sick that night. I can't say for sure that this is what caused them to get sick (throwing up and diarrhea) but there was nothing else different that I can point to.

I picked these FunBites MiniCongo bones for my puggle.  I am pretty picky about what kind of chews I give her.  Sometimes she has a hard time of chewing them so she gives up and swollows them whole.  This usually makes her sick then.  She was able to chew these bones goodand into small edible pieces.  She would chew on them for hours.  Sometimes she would leave an unfinished chew on the floor.  If I would find it I always picked it up and would hide it from her and then tell her she had to find it.  They must smell really good because she always would.  I will be buying these again for her.

These FunBites seem to be a good idea, but, they do not seem to be that appealing to dogs. My dogs were not terribly interested in these chews and often ignored them when offered. The sticks are too large and it would be better if it were possible to break them into pieces. Not something that I will purchase in the future for my "pack".

I have a picky dog with tummy troubles who has to eat a prescription diet. She loves the Newman's treats but they are too hard for her since she is missing half her teeth. Still, occasionally I hear a crunching sound and she is munching down a Newman's. I was hoping she would knaw on these treats and thought the center would be a little easier to eat. Here's how the trial went:

Me: opening the bag "you want a treat?"
Dog: tail wagging, ears perked up and looking at me intently
Me: I pull one treat from the bag and hand it to her
Dog: She takes it carefully and sets it on the floor. "sniff, sniff". She looks back up at me. "sniff". She walks away and lays down in her bed.
Me: I pick up the treat and sniff and don't smell anything. This doesn't mean much since I'm not a dog. I pull on the outside "wrapping". It's pretty tough. I push the middle up a little. It's hard! I was expecting a softer middle. I taste the middle. It's tasteless.

I tried again to tempt her with one of these treats by giving it to her in place of our nightly "bite of cheese" ritual. Once again she just sniffed of it and then ignored it. The other treats I've tried with her (beggin strips, puperoni, blue bison apple/yogurt biscuits, milk bone) she will either attempt to eat or carry around in her mouth for several minutes looking for a safe place to hide it. These treats don't even get the honor of being buried.

Not sure what the problem was, but neither of my dogs accepted these treats if an option was available.  If this was the only thing offered, they seemed to take them with a disinterested attitude.  They were made in such a way that the dogs didn't devour them in a few seconds, so were long-lasting, and were a good size to take up some time when you want something to occupy your dog for a longer amount of time.  I may try another flavor of these, as I did like the long-lasting aspect of these treats.

These treats are definitely not meant for smaller dogs as they are way too big for my wiener dog and pug. However, I picked these up for my 35 pound dog and it's perfect for him. Just an FYI. He really seems to like the treats but not the outside. He works on squeezing out the insides and then discards the husk, which I thought was pretty funny. So the dog definitely likes them, he just doesn't love them.

I have rather mixed feelings about this. A neighbor's dog who does have a sensitive stomach has been eating these and it seems to have helped, maybe. It certainly hasn't caused additional problems. However, my dog is somewhat picky and I couldn't get her to touch these. Even broken up and put in her bowl it was of no interest to her. Tried it with four other dogs, one other wouldn't touch it, the other three ate it but certainly didn't seem to be over the moon for them.

It may well help with digestion but they don't seem to be especially attractive to eat, certainly not on the level of a Bonz or coated rawhide.

No one in our household liked these, of course it was only the 3 dogs that sampled them! Our neighbor's Boxer mix loved them, and our Maltese did snap up the bits that fell from his chomping. The wee ones had no interest in the treats when they were whole, however.

My dog (mid-sized Chow) simply wouldn't touch them, whereas she loved the other product from this company, the FunBites flat sticks. Of course, your dog's taste might be different so buy the smallest package first (like any new dog food/treats) and let them be the judge!

They lasted quite a while and my two dogs seemd to enjoy the treats.  There was no stomach upset after they finished them.  My dogs ate the treats completely - sometimes they don't finish a treat which could be a sign they don't like them.  I'd buy these again.

My English Springer Spaniel absolutely loves food. It doesn't matter what it is - if it's edible, she's game. My cockapoo is more of a picky eater, so you really have to try hard to find anything she'll try. When the package of treats arrived, I made a big show of opening them for the dogs who were very excited to see what they'd be getting. They readily took a treat each and promptly dropped them on the floor. I picked one up to try to give it to the cockapoo and she took off down the stairs and out the dog door. Turning to my springer who, as I said, never turns down anything edible (in her opinion), I tried to coax her into giving it another try. Being a sport, she took it in her mouth once again then trotted away and dropped it. She came back as if asking, "okay, so now where are the real treats." I finally gave up trying to coax either dog to bite into the treats and just left them laying on the floor for them when they wanted them. Yeah, that never happened. I can understand my cockapoo not eating the treats because she's really picky, but my springer not enjoying them shocked me. They smell like normal dog treats to me! No, I did not try them and nor will I ever be tempted to taste a dog treat. I do plan on trying them out on other dogs and will post an update if one of the pups actually eats one. It's impossible to know if they really support the digestion if you can't get a dog to digest them.

My dogs eat just about anything, but only 1 of 5 would eat these.  He was very happy with them, but the others gave them a lick or a nibble, then walked away.  Maybe on another day, the results might have been different, but that is what happened.  Perhaps if the peanut butter scent were stronger?  Who knows?

With four dogs of varying sizes, it is difficult to find a bone they can all enjoy. From the biggest to the smallest, these bones were a hit. Keep in mind, the bigger dogs "wolfed" them down, but the little dogs took their time.  These were more substantial than expected.  They have an "easy digest" center wrapped in a raw-hide shell. Though a great quality product, I would not recommend this particular SIZE for anything larger than a cocker spaniel. These served as a good time killer for the babies.

Chewy is a 70 lb doberman/sheppard mix who is what is called an "aggressive chewer." So he likes crunchy treats (and anything else he can chew up). Our previous try with a FunBites product,FunBites FlatSticks Calcibone, 60-Count (Pack of 5), did not go over well. He would hardly even try to eat it. He seems to find these treats more interesting, however. They break up pretty quickly so the treat doesn't last long, but he seems to enjoy it and it didn't upset his stomach (though he is a mutt, so unlike some purebreeds he isn't prone to a sensitive tummy). But for what they are, they are overpriced. The ingredients list isn't really anything different than what you would find in a store brand dog treat.

My dog loved these from the moment I opened the pack!  They were a little hard at first, but once she got through the rawhide exterior she was munching away.  These FunBites are perfect for medium- to large-size dogs; I would, however, avoid giving them to small dogs because of their size.

Given that our dogs don't get rawhide treats often, we thought they might like to try these. However, both our 70 lb Aussie and 10 lb. Papillon rejected them. The Aussie eventually gave in and tried to bury one in the back yard, but never bothered to cover the hole. This is pretty important, because our boys will eat nearly anything! These were a nice size for small or large dogs, but neither seemed interested, despite that fact.  That said, these two dogs of ours love dehydrated cow lungs and organic carrots for snacks, so perhaps their pallates are just too refined for cardboard filled rawhide chews.
We have four dogs, so each one received a FunBite. And each one loved it. However, due to the size, I would recommend large dogs only be given these rawhide treats.

I have a large shepherd and a beagle. Both of the spent a long time finishing this treat.  My big dog can handle anything, the little dog not so much.  But his BM's were more solid, and he didn't have his normal gas. I recommend this.

With the best of intentions, these didn't work for either of our dogs, a jack and the spaniel next door. Why? I couldn't guess, but even after a few attempts, neither of them will pick them up.

Oh well...

My dog is a chewer. She loved chewing on them but I'm pretty sure it's what upset her stomach. I am going to give her another one today and change my review if she doesn't get sick again. It could have just been a coincidence. For now, just 2 stars.

These funbites are the perfect size for my medium sized dogs. it does take them a little bit of time to chew for it and they really enjoy these. I would suggest not letting them eat this on the carpet as it can get very messy. It also does not make them too gassy like other treats I've tried.

I just wish there were more in the package than just 7. Because I have two dogs, one of them is going to be getting one extra funbite.

It's possible my pup is too young to enjoy these, but the first one, he ate up pretty fast.  He is a lab pup, and loves to chew.  He does particularly like thinner chews; we finally threw the one away he has now been ignoring for weeks.  We have one or two more in the package we will try giving to him when he is older, and if he likes it better, I will revise my review, but so far, I am not too impressed with this product.

I have 4 Chihuahuas. Although they seem to like these I find them too large for them.
I think these snacks would be better for dogs 20 pounds and up.
I worry about my smaller dogs eating so much rawhide. Unfortunately these things are so tough it's very difficult to cut
them into smaller pieces. I tried with a saw and it took about 10 minutes. Too much work for me but
if you have a larger dog I'm sure them will like them.

I have six left in the packet. My dog will not chew or even play with these.

This is my second try with this chew. The first I'd tried were the soy and I thought the peanut butter flavor would entice my dog, but no such thing.

I ended up having to put the one I'd offered him in the trash after a couple weeks of it lying on the floor.

I just cannot get my dog to like this chew at all and I've given up completely. Something must be amiss, either the flavor or the scent.

I have two dogs, a 17 month Caucasian/alsatian mix and a 6 month caucasian. They both love this treat. Whenever they see me coming downstairs in the mornings they run towards me excitedly expecting the morning treat. I have not been able to determine it's nutritional benefits, though i can say there are no negative effects so far.

I got one bag as a sample for review and tried giving one of the treats to my dog, but she wasn't willing to give it a serious try. I let her keep it for a week and every once in a while she'd toss it around the living room or pick it up and carry it around for a minute, but she never made any real effort to eat it.

I ended up giving 2 of them to my nephew's dog, and he seemed to like them all right. I took the remainder to a playdate my dog was having with 3 other dogs and out of those one chewed on one a little but didn't seem awfully interested, one took no interest at all, and one really liked them. I tossed the bag after the playdate, forgetting that I'd want it for reference, but I seem to remember not being very thrilled by the ingredient list either.

The final tally for me was 2 dogs out of 5 who seemed to like it, 1 who thought it was okay but nothing special, and 2 who didn't have any real interest.

I'm not impressed with these at all and I can't see myself recommending them to anyone. Given that my own dog wouldn't eat hers, I definitely won't consider buying them in the future.

Edit: Leaving my original review intact, but reducing from 2 stars to 1. I just heard that the dog that liked these the most was chewing on it a while after I went home and started whimpering. Her owners found that her gums were bleeding. It might just be a random thing that she bit at it wrong and no fault of the treat, but given the other problems people have reported having with these I wouldn't want to gamble on it. I'm definitely not going to be recommending these to anyone.

Despite the box color and misleading labeling Muesli, don't be fooled as I was.  This is not the same as the No Sugar version of the Original Formula with the muesli consistency that expands when soaked with milk or soymilk and which has the wonderful date pulp flavoring.  This is a new hybrid muesli-flakes version that I have never seen for sale in stores especially created for American taste which is used to lots of flakes and raisins.  Now I have to finish off six boxes before I can go back to Original Formula or No Sugar Original Formula.

This is not the original Swiss Muesli that made this company famous and I've found that in a lot of the stores in this area this is now the only Familia Swiss Meusli available.  In my opinion, what they've done is an attempt to make a less costly product ( for them that is} by adding large volume puffed type cereals to the mix. This makes for a lighter product , but with the same size box. The original box weighs 32 ounces, compared to 21 ounces for this new product. Unfortunately, this results in an inferior product, both in taste and nutrition. The real original product is still available in a red box , but I fear they might phase it out if they can get people to go for this cheap imitation.

This is definitely not the original formula that one can buy in the grocery store. One box might not have been too bad but we had to eat through the complete order of multiple boxes! We were quite disappointed.

Familia Muesli is a healthy and tasty combination of oats, corn flakes, nuts, sunflower seeds and Swiss
tradition. The tradition still lives and the picture on the box exactly depicts the company's
location in the countryside. I've been there!

I call this my "horse feed," but it is really good.  I love this stuff.  My local store hasn't been able to get it in several months.  I was happy to find it here.  It makes you feel good and I actually crave the stuff.  There is no sugar, try finding another cereal without sugar... it's not easy.  I went out of my way to find it, buy it and get more of it!!!  Ordered six boxes.  I hope Amazon keeps it in stock, not sure what I will do if I can't get my Swiss Balance fix.
I love this cereal.  Doesn't get soggy and mushy in milk.  Love the fruit and nut bits.  The perfect muesli.

Do not buy this product if you expect Familia Original recipe. The product description claims that this is the original recipe in a newly designed package, but this is not the case.

I had been buying Familia for years. Perhaps the formula is the same but the product I received was not the milled grain I expected. It was more like puffed wheat; think sugar puffs without the sugar.

It was like eating cardboard.

To their credit, Amazon gave me a refund.

The muesli is good, but dried apple pieces just spoil everything.
Would you eat apples with milk?
Familia Natural thinks that it's a great idea!

This stuff is so yummy, I'll be buying it again and again. I don't even like pomegranate and I resist the ubiquitous pomegranate juice in stores. But this stuff - is great! I used it as an addition to a sauce (an Iraqi recipe I was trying out) and it is tart and sweet at the same time. I can't resist helping myself to a teaspoonful right from the bottle now and then. Its flavor is so intense, that's all you need....

I had a recipe for a pear-pomegranate pie which required this ingredient. I also used it in a blood orange, pomegranate, fennel, shallot, beet, feta cheese and toasted almond salad. I served both of these with a crown roast of pork with Cumberland sauce for Christmas dinner. This molasses is sour and sweet simultaneously and imparts an interesting taste but could, if used too lavishly, overhwhelm a dish.

Great things about this mix: 1. only needs water added, all other ingredients are already in the mix. 2. you can make any size cake you want and save the balance of the mix for future baking endeavors. 3. it bakes up into a very light, yet moist cake.
