Got this to make Roja sauce, but it adds complexity to many mexican dishes.  I love that it is in a paste form!  So easy to use!

I loved the Taco Bell Jalapeno Sauce, 8-Ounce (Pack of 6)and was eager to try the Chipotle flavor also, and I wasn't disappointed. Actually this doesn't taste a great deal different from the Jalapeno, just a slight smoky flavor on top of the spice. Like the Jalapeno, this sauce is great for tacos and burritos, burgers, hot dogs and as a veggie dip.

This review applies both to the "Chipotle" and the "Spicy Ranchero" flavors, neither of which tastes much like anything identifiable. The base is a thin mayonnaise made from soybean oil, chemically dyed to vivid and rather odd colors. To that are added various natural and artificial flavors to create a strong, though only moderately spicy, flavor.

This isn't really a sauce and it isn't very Mexican. What it is is the sort of bright-color/strong-flavor condiment that kids like to squirt over everything. Juvenile palates are evidently what it's intended for. Since that describes the clientele Taco Bell targets, it should go over well with them.
This creamy sauce has a good amount of spice to it, which really complements the smoky, BBQ flavor. I enjoyed this unique sauce.

I have actually tried all three new Taco Bell Sauces, the Chipotle which I am reviewing now, and also the Jalapeño and the Spicy Ranchero sauces.

The Chipotle is my second favorite of the three. (I like the Spicy Ranchero the best). It definitely has a distinct smokey peppery chipotle taste to it, with of course the creamy base. This sauce goes well on taco salads and (as I used it on) beef burritos. I suppose you could use it for french fries or tacos as well. I felt that because the sauce had such a bold flavor that probably its uses would be more limited than the Spicy Ranchero flavor that was much more mild and subdued. But if you like a bold chipotle flavor I think this would really be for you.

The bottles are squeeze bottles but I found that they don't squeeze out easily once you are half way done with the bottle. You have to store upside down in the fridge or be forced to really shake the bottle to get the sauce to be forced down the the top. Sauces are thicker than traditional salad dressings.

I tried this chipotle sauce on a sandwich. It was not bad. But it was not great either. Just okay. The taste seems a bit bland, and more of a me-too, mass-produced flavor that you might see in a fast-food restaurant than something original or tasting special. Given that this is a Taco Bell product, that's not surprising.

The flavor of this creamy, ranch-like chipotle sauce is very mild, with a hint of smoky, cheesy pepper flavor.  It tastes okay, and it goes well with tacos to complement the taste.  However, it didn't knock my socks off.  For those concerned about nutrition, 2 tablespoons of the sauce come in at 110 calories.  To me, something that rings up that many calories ought to really blow you away taste-wise in order to make it worth it.  There is a long list of artificial ingredients (which may explain the bright orange color).  The sauce overall is fairly bland, not bold as the label suggests.  Those who prefer spicier, fresher flavors at a lower nutritional price tag should probably look elsewhere.

I found this sauce to be delicious and suitable for Mexican food or even a general purpose sauce that could kick up a sandwich, omelet, or stew with a seriously tasty Chipotle flavor.

The hot sauce addicts who tasted it were disappointed. It has lots of flavor, but no real kick. But, these are guys that put the super hot pepper sauce on everything they eat - I'm not sure how many taste buds they really have left.

My husband and I used the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce on some steak fajitas we made a few evenings ago. We were out of picante sauce so we decided to use the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce. It was spicy with a strange twang. I couldn't decide if I liked it or not. In a way, it was good. On the other hand, the taste was too different for my tame tastebuds.
I imagine that people who frequent Taco Bell will be excited to be able to purchase this sauce. I believe the taste will grow on me, but for now, I am sticking to picante.

This sauce really was yummy - it does have a little kick to it, though. I prefer it to the other flavors that Taco Bell also offers. My only complaint is that it was expired the day it arrived. We ate it with our fajitas that night, but I had to throw the rest of it away.

On rare occasion, we do stop off at Taco Bell. That was why I decided to give this Chipotle Sauce a try. We tried it on sliced cucumber -- not so good. We tried it on some roast beef -- not so good.

I am sure that this sauce will be loved in another home, but not mine. That "smoke" flavor was overpowering, and the taste was just heavy in an unpleasant way.

Sorry bo be so critical, but our reaction was negative. We did consider mixing it with mayo or sour cream, but realized that we were only trying to dilute something we already didn't like.

I don't eat things like this but hubby LOVES anything hot or with pepper flavor.  He tried this as soon as it came today.  He spread a little bit on the sandwich he was in the middle of eating.  He says it's good!  Not super hot but has a good pepper flavor.  He says we'd buy it again and he could see putting it on salad, on burgers, dipping fries or veggies in it.  Guess we'll be buying it again soon!

It's no secret that I like spicy food. When I reviewed Taco Bell's Home Originals Bold & Creamy Jalapeno Sauce a little while back, I noticed two little words on the label that really got me hopeful: Home Originals. Will there be more flavors in this line?
Yes! Bold and Creamy Chipotle sauce is even more flavorful. Chipotle peppers are fiery chili pepper made by smoking jalapeno peppers. The smokiness adds a depth that's just hard to beat. If you like creamy hot sauces, you will love this on all those fall meals: tail gate parties, hot dogs, fries, rice and grilled veggies. It's zippy with out being overwhelming and tasty without being tongue numbing. As always, it's great on all you Mexican food faves. I know this will be a stock item in my fridge.

Clearly, this sauce provides an alternative to traditional non-franchised sauces. It's a runny salad dressing that has some tang and a lot of calories. Whereas adults will find the taste, color, and texture largely unappealing, children may like it based on their experiences with Taco Bell. This sauce is not "hot" by any measure and not even close to any real Mexican sauces. I consider myself a fan of real Mexican food having lived in San Diego for 13 years. This sauce is garbage compared to what any small restaurant or even street vendor on the border can produce.

As with any processed food, the nutritional value is horrible and I doubt I will use it again. In 2 TBSP, which is not a lot, you will consume 110 calories, 300mg sodium, and 11g of fat. Who eats this stuff? These nutritional facts do not seem apparent on the Amazon product page.

Bottom line- if you your eating habits are garbage, this sauce fits right in. If you try and eat healthy, stay away. You will find very little return in terms of taste versus nutrition.

I was sort of looking for a product like this and luckily for me, this one became available.

The actual Taco Bell Restaurants used to have a taco salad that I liked and, unexplainably, they discontinued it -- but by incorporating the ingredients that they formerly used and by topping the salad with this dressing, it tastes much the same to me.

Over and above that, if you're tired of the same old Italian or Ranch dressing on your green salad this will bump it up a notch. It's especially good if you include sliced boiled eggs in your salads. You can also use this dressing (a small amount) to infuse an entirely new flavor into your home-made coleslaw.

Everyone in the household who tried this product liked it so you're not going to be stuck with something unwanted if you give it a try.

Recommended.

Taco Bell's Chipotle sauce is much better than their ranchero sauce which had a burnt taste that I didn't like at all. This sauce hits the taste buds with a sharp creamy pepper, vinegar, and smokey barbecue taste, and leaves a smooth barbecue and vegetable aftertaste with it. I know the thought of vinegar and barbecue sauce on mexican foods sounds strange but it actually compliments tacos quite well. It's a little too strong for dishes with plenty of flavor already like fajitas, and it might also be too much for a dipping sauce, but it adds a nice kick to tacos, nachos, burritos, and even cheese pizza.

If you don't like the kick of vinegar or prefer milder salsas or sour cream flavors, this is not the complimentary sauce for you, but in the ranks of chipotle in general, its definitely worth a try.

Taco Bell has always been a tasty treat, but not a very healthy snack choice. The Chipotle Sauce by Taco Bell is definitley tasty. I tried it on a homemade taco and it was great. I also tried it on a turkey sandwich and it added a much-needed zing. However it also added about 11g fat and 110 calories. That's like adding half a McDonald's Quarter Pounder to your taco in terms of fat content. [...]

That being said, I wouldn't eat this sauce every day. I would try it once in a while on an otherwise bland food choice, and probably on a workout day. It's truly bursting with flavor, so if you're not on a diet it's a nice change of pace.

This chipotle sauce is nothing too exciting to write home about. It doesn't taste bad, it just isn't anything super special, I "have to have" kind of sauce.
I enjoy it; the sauce is creamy - not as creamy as the Jalepeño, whose flavour I enjoy more - and it is flavourful. I use it on sandwiches, wraps, and pita pockets.
I have nothing bad to say, but I don't want to seem like I'm trying to spice up my review or give a false impression that I'd go out and buy this as often as I can.
I may or may not buy it again, but then again, I'm not the biggest chipotle fan; I just wanted to try it and see how it tasted. Not bad, but again: I prefer the jalepeño,
probably 'cause I love the taste of jalepeño a lot. I've tasted at least one other chipotle sauce, and this one isn't quite as good as that one, but, again, it's not bad, just not "the best."

I'm not a huge Mexican food buff; if I find myself in a Mexican restaurant with someone else, I can find something appealing, and if I'm in the home of someone who's serving Mexican food I can enjoy it, but never in my life have I requested a Mexican meal or a visit to a Mexican restaurant. The only exception is if I want fast food at a VERY low price and I'm tired of the same old burger-and-fries routine; then Taco Bell might come into the running, if I'm going to be passing one anyway.

The reason I bring this up is that I used this Taco Bell chipotle sauce on foods that might not necessarily be what you'd have in mind: a variety of sandwiches (it goes especially well with turkey and chicken) as well as bacon and eggs, meals which would not pack much of a kick without this sauce. With that you might think that the sauce would overpower the rest of the food, but it didn't. It was really a perfect complement: spicy, but not with enough of a kick to dominate the meal or make my eyes burn and mouth water, and with that smoky chipotle flavor, rich and full-bodied.

This is how it tastes on foods that pack minimal spicy kick on their own. I guess it might end up getting lost in a meal with other spices and peppers and whatnot. It may well work fine in such a dish, or it may not. For my purposes I was very pleased with this product.

I like Taco Bell. That may explain why I really like the taste of this Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce. It is good right from the bottle, two drips per chip, as a corn chip dip. Make nachos with a plate of chips, ladled with ground beef and onion mix, then pour on the Chipotle Sauce. What an appetizer; but unfortunately at the same calorie, fat, sodium, levels as most fancy restaurant dishes, or those huge multi-meat bacon cheese burgers. So for those who do not have to count calories or healthy nutrition, it's tasty. Spicy and flavorful without being HOT, at least to my liking, as I enjoy a bit of heat.

If you're not a Mexican fast-food fan, you might find this product a bit unsophisticated. In that case, if the supreme high-priced Tex-Mex restaurants are your cup of tea, then skip this product. But if you want to spice up the celery, carrots and green peppers on your ball game night snack food tray, this may be as good as Taco Bell delivering to your door.

Good also as a high calorie taco salad dressing. Unfortunately, I can't tell you if it is good on a taco because I ran the bottle dry before I got to trying it on a real taco.
If only they could reproduce the taste with heart healthy nutrition levels.
Oh well, I'll bet it's good on a cheeseburger.

This Chipotle Sauce is very tasty, and it can be used with many different things. However I loved it the most with vegetarian meat (I'm a vegetarian, living healthy and all *grins*), and this sauce is amazing in a veggie sandwich, or with cooked vegetarian meat. However this sauce is very fattening, hence why I took one star out, it contains 11 grams of fat in 2 tbsp. So one needs to be careful to have it in very small portions, or make sure to have a good workout session after indulging in a good hearty meal containing this sauce.

Overall I love this Chipotle sauce, very tasty.

I've tried using this on chicken and hamburgers and really liked it. It's a nice change from ketchup and BBQ sauces. The Chipotle has a spicy tang but it's overwhelming. It's probably even milder than the spicy sauces in an actual Taco Bell restaurant. It actually has a slightly sweet taste. It is a bit salty and creamy for those who are health conscious, but I find that even a small bit provides a lot of flavor and can be spread quite far over your meal. The bottle seems a bit smaller than you might expect, but other than that I'd recommend this.

This sauce had the consistancy of salad dressing. The taste was a bit smoky, with a hint of spice. Very mild flavored; the flavor could get lost if combined with another sauce. It was just OK, I'm not sure if I'd buy it.

I must admit that I am NOT a fan of Taco Bell. That is, unless I'm hungover. But since I'm not 99% of the time, I was reluctant to try this sauce. But, honestly, it's quite spicy and goes GREAT with chicken! I used it to cool some chicken breasts and they were quite flavorful. I also used this to top a Mexican salad, which also tasted nice. The sauce is very hearty and robust and gives off some good heat. I was thinking I wouldn't like it, but I must say that I look forward to picking it up at the grocery store!

I jumped at the opportunity to try out this sauce -- I'm a big fan of Taco Bell and I love chipotle mustard on sandwiches, so I figured this would be some good stuff.

I wasn't disappointed. It has that distinctive chipotle taste in a sauce that is slightly thicker than creamy ranch dressing. So far, I've used it on southwest chicken salad (romaine topped with grilled chicken, black beans, corn, diced red bell pepper, jack cheese, and some chopped fresh tomato). It compliments those flavors well. Because it's so thick, you don't need to use a lot to get the flavor spread around. I've also used it on sandwiches (turkey with provolone, roast beef with cheddar, ham with swiss), and it's very nice. Adds a slightly spicy touch without being overpowering.

Will I purchase again? I think so. Not sure I'd be able to use 6 bottles of the stuff, but a bottle or so once in awhile seems probable.

There's not a lot to say here. I like Chipotle sauce, and I like Taco Bell, so the sauce is great. I once listed Taco Bell among my 5 favorite restaurants in the United States on Facebook, which prompted some serious questioning of my taste buds, but I suspect that I'm not the only one who loves to munch on their various burrito concoctions.

I like the salsa that they sell, and the Chipotle sauce is excellent, too. Oh, it's not really hot; pretty mild. Enjoy!

My kids got ahold of this and took it all before I ever got the chance to taste it. They took it to their apartment. I had to take their word for it when they told it was "awesome sauce." They say they put it on everything. So you'll have to take their word for it. But I never got to try it.

I enjoyed the Taco Bell Bold and Creamy Chipotle sauce.  It tastes and smells good--and different--and doesn't have too much heat.  I used it as a dip for potato chips, and I'm looking forward to using it on tacos next time we have them.  I think the chips tempered the sauce's heat.

Taco Bell has outdone themselves this time. This chipotle sauce is just right. The sauce itself resembles French dressing, but milder. The pureed chipotle pepper is a mild but pleasant chile, so they blend perfectly. The oil used is soybean oil. There's just a tinge of garlic flavor, as well as red bell pepper, to even things out.

It contains 110 calories per serving size (two tablespoons), 300 mg. sodium, and the daily value of vitamin A is four percent.

This sauce would be great on a salad or a sandwich. It is also recommended for tacos, but I require more of a tomato-based salsa on my tacos. To each his own.

Yes, I will make this a permanent staple in my home. Not too hot, not too intrusive. Yet not dull. Pleasantly pleasing would be the words to best describe it.

We love all things spicy and Mexican but this sauce is not worth it. It is very mild and has little chipotle flavor. It looks like Thousand Island dressing but adds no flavor. Empty and flavorless calories. My recommendation (if you want a kick to your sauce) is the Frontera brand. Now that one has flavor and spice!

About what you might expect from Taco Bell sauce. It's middle-of-the-road in terms of spice and texture. Not too spicy - which was fine for me. The texture was very creamy which might not appeal to everyone. It was workable but nothing terribly exciting. In other words, it got the job done by adding some flavor without getting in the way. It you like your sauces with a bit more bite and more texture, you might want to look elsewhere. Otherwise, this won't disappoint.

This sauce works well as a sauce for Mexican and Tex-Mex recipes. It has subtle heat and smokey chipotle flavor. It will suit those who prefer hotter food, but won't be too overpowering for those who don't.

Another great plus is that it is not overly salty. Many processed sauces are, but this one is not.

I eat at Taco Bell all the time, and this tastes exactly the same as the Taco Bell sauce included in food sold at Taco Bell.

I'm not a huge fan of Chipotle Sauce, but for what it is, it's the best I've had.

Definitely glad I have it for whenever I make burritos from home :)

After trying both the Chipotle as well as the Spicy Ranchero sauces I was very happy that Taco Bell decided to branch out their at home selection.

When using this sauce with the Taco Belle taco seasoning you get a taco that is pretty close to the flavor that you would get if you went to the restaurant but it's not quite there.

Honestly this can be much better though for a few reasons. First you can use your own fresh ingrediants, you don't have to leave the house (just order it here or get during your normal grocery shopping), and lastly, you don't have to deal with the fast food experience; lines, rude cashiers, people that don't wash their hands, and you can save a little money.

All in all this is a great way to get a Taco Bell fix in your own kitchen. And if I had to choose one over the other I would easily pick the Chipotle sauce, Mmmm.
I use this sauce for pretty much everything mexican, and on my sandwiches as well it is really good I give it 5 stars.

Like most food products this will either fit your tastes or it won't. It has a nice smokey chipotle taste, a little bit of a kick but not all that hot. Very creamy but a slight texture of granularity can be felt, just like they ground up real chipotle peppers.  I like it.

I love spicy food, and chipotle is usually one of my favorites, so I thought this sauce from Taco Bell would be great. It was okay at best. It adds a little flavor to foods like quesadillas and burritos, but it just didn't wow me. It doesn't have much kick at all. I haven't tried it as a dressing for taco salad yet, and that may be a better way to use it as it has the texture of a salad dressing.

For the price ($20 for 6 bottles??), if I felt I had to have another bottle I'd shop locally rather than order it.

Taco Bell chipotle sauce has just enough "zing" to it to be interesting, but not overly hot.  It's great on taco salads, hamburgers, as a dipping sauce for hot wings, or anyplace you like a creamy, zesty sauce.  Taco Bell makes some pretty decent products, and this one will be at the top of my "favorites" list.  I love chipotle flavored anything, and this does not disappoint!

Taco Bell has built their reputation as a Mexican fast food restraunt, that is as successful in the Mid West as it in California.  This means that they make a product that is no thrills and bland enough that everyone will like it.  If you want authentic Mexican food Taco Bell is not for you.  Most Mexican food is very spicy and often has a little kick, I have seen Mexicans that use Tapatio hot sauce on hamburgers, rice and soups and Tapatio packs a kick.  The Chipotle sauce is nice and bland which is how most people like their food but it really does not pack the kick that a typical authentic Chipotle sauce has.  I tried it on tacos which was not good at all and nachos which actually was pretty good.  If Taco Bell is your choice for burritos and tacos than you will like the Chipotle Sauce.

What do I think about the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce?  Well, it wasn't terrible.  It had a mild chipotle taste with a taco bell take, which I prefer over spicier toppings.  However, It isn't something that I think I'll be picking up on every shopping trip.  The container is a nice size that should be fine for a few family dinners before running out.  If you are looking for a new sauce, I suggest trying this one. Taste is so subjective a thing that you just might like it!

Not really much to say except it can be best considered sour cream with a kick. I mix it in with my nachos along with chipotle flavored Tabasco sauce to give it a tangy boost. As for taste, if you had a Baja flavored chalupa from Taco Bell, imagine the Baja flavoring having a badass cousin who rides in on Vespa. One of my friends used it for a salad dressing for his taco salad, but I was more horrified than interested at that point. Like I said, it has the consistency of sour cream.

In summation, I love it for my nachos, especially now for football season. However, the bottle is small and you're lucky to get 10 servings from a bottle.

I used the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce in an enchilada casserole as part of the sauce. It gave a mellow smoky flavor to the dish, with just the slightest bit of kick. Planning on trying it as a condiment, as well. Tasting it straight out of the bottle, it did have just a touch of a metallic taste, but when added to the recipe I made, the metallic flavor was absent.

We eat a lot of Southwestern food, so I am happy to have a new product to experiment with.

These sauces are light and have a spicy edge. They mix well with meats, Mexican food, veggies, and some of them are good in salads. They are liquid, so blend well with other foods. Jalapeno is the lightest, Spicy Ranchero is like the original Taco Bell Hot Sauce Flavor the most. It goes well as a salad dressing if applied sparingly. The Chipotle one is the most mellow one, all with a bite. I will definitely buy again.

Taco Bell has outdone themselves.

I absolutely love Taco Bell, so I was excited to try their new Chipotle Sauce on my home-made Mexican food. I was a little disappointed by the taste, which is smokier than I would like, and not very spicy at all. It's a decent product, but after the initial test-run, the bottle has been sitting in the fridge, untouched, through many a Mexican meal.
This was a big hit when I made turkey sandwiches for my son and his friends. It's a little too spicy for my taste, but the kids loved it.

As a vegetarian, I'm always looking for a way to add zing to food. Luckily, I added the chipotle sauce from Taco Bell to my meal, and it was delicious. You only need a small amount to get a lot of flavor.

I cooked 1/2 cup of Morningstar crumbles and 1/2 cup of Rotel tomatoes in a skillet till the liquid was cooked. Then I removed from skillet, added 2 tblsp. chipotle sauce, added daiya non-dairy cheddar cheese and put in a tortilla wrap.

Goes great with a side of refried beans, black beans, or Mexican corn. Low in calorie, healthy, and filling. I definitely recommend. The only thing that would make it better is if the product were vegan.

I was pleasantly surprised by the taste of the Chipotle Sauce. It is kind-of like a spicy mayonnaise. I used this sauce in tuna salad, on sandwiches and as a salad dressing.

Similar to mayo, almost all of the calories come from fat. I think it is tastier than mayo and has a nice amount of spice. You can taste the pepper in the sauce but it doesn't leave your mouth burning. It's a good balance of flavors.

To give you an insight into how bold this sauce is, I recently bought some Kraft Chipotle Mayonnaise and the mayo was much spicier than this sauce. I like the taco sauce that you get in the restaurants and thought this would be similar, but it's a far cry from the packets. The smokiness is a little too fake and the aftertaste is off-putting. I know some may consider this a small thing to complain about, but the mouth of the bottle is the size of a salad dressing bottle, so you have to be careful when pouring or it gets all over. That is not something many people necessarily want, especially since the recommended two tablespoon serving size is 110 calories and 11 grams of fat.

From the look of it, Taco Bell's new "Bold and Creamy" Chipotle sauce looks like it may be a spicy-cheesy concoction fans of quick-serve Mexican food would enjoy. This is deceiving. The pastel orange color masks its true nature: it is essentially a remixed BBQ sauce. The BBQ-inspired taste is so strong that it actually drowns out the chili pepper, garlic, and other spices Taco Bell blended with its chipotle recipe.

This product is made to be used with tacos hard and soft. That being said, the reviewer tried it with a ham and cheese sandwich as well as a taco. It made no difference either way. The BBQ flavor will make itself fans or critics based solely on how the consumer feels about the southern staple's fusion into Mexican food.

The packaging is clean looking and attractive. The Taco Bell logo is at the top, with an appetizingly loaded hard taco taking up a good 60 percent of the label. My sole gripe is that while the name (chipotle) refers to smoke-dried jalapeno peppers, the sauce has no kick to it. Taco Bell ought to do more market research on consumer preferences for "bold" being synonymous with hotness in this style of cuisine. Fans of old school Mexican-American food should pass on the disappointingly one-dimensional Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce, 8-Ounce (Pack of 6).

This spread has a decent smokey flavor of Chipotle, but it isn't super spicy. I really liked the flavor, actually. It advertises as something to use on wraps, tacos, and Mexican salads, but I wouldn't suggest it for a salad dressing. It is essentially a flavored mayo or sandwich spread, so the base is thick like a mayo. I think it would be excellent on a sandwich, wrap, or even a taco or burrito, but it would probably be too heavy for a salad dressing.

Since this spread has enough spice on its own, I tried it on a prociutto and provolone wrap with sprouts. It gave it that great tang and zip without overpowering the sandwich. It was tasty and definitely added something to the sandwich. I am excited to try the other flavors put out by the Taco Bell line!

This sauce is spicy, and very tasty - with a hint of smokiness flavor. I used it as a dip for veggies and it was a hit, my son and his friends used it on sandwiches and they raved about it.  This is very tasty, and I think it would be delicious on pork or chicken.  Something I will buy again.

Taco Bell's sauce is indeed yummier!! We used it in our burgers, sandwiches and some meat dishes. The key is that the main things, the protein, still have to be seasoned and cooked right. Then add the sauce on top of it before serving.

Obviously, this does not replace anything that should make the steak/beef tasty. Use it like a ketchup, and not too much. Then the flavors will pop and taste well!

I am a big fan of the sauces from Taco Bell and assumed this was like them, but it isn't.  Not to say the sauce isn't good, its just not what I expected or had a taste for.  The flavor is not really chipotle, but somewhat dry and bland.  Not hot at all if you are looking for spice.  So far we have only tried on tacos and won't be buying another bottle.  It was different and worth trying, but again not typical Taco Bell.

I ordered the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce through Amazon Vine. We put the sauce on Taco Bell tacos and burritos. I thought the sauce was good. It tasted strong with a lot of spices. It was thicker than the sauce in the restaurant. It was thin but it must have many spices in it. My wife thought it was ok but found it to have a smoky flavor. I thought it was a tangy flavor.

John Navarra

This sauce was surprisingly good and delicious on fajitas. It is strong but compliments meats and fish very nicely. The ingredients include soybean oil, whey, vinegar, buttermilk, sugar and egg yolks, with less than 2 percent chipotle chile pepper puree.

I first tried chipotle sauce on a sandwich at subway and liked it. I will say it has an acquired taste. It's not hot hot-just a tad spicey. When I saw this offered on VINE, I thought i'd try it.

This taste great. I've used it on burritos that I have bought at taco bell. I also have used it as a salad dressing. Just get some lettuce, slice up a tomato, add some mexican cheese, black olives and pour some of this sauce on it and you got a taco bell-like salad! It's pretty good on veggie burgers, too!

If you like mexican and want to add some zest to mexican food, burgers, sandwich wraps or a salad, give it try for something different!

I used this on a London broil I had grilled, and it complemented the meat well.  Many will wonder how hot it is.  Tough question, since I really like peppers of all kinds, but I would call it pretty mild.  Your taste may vary!

This Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is a robust sauce with strong chipotle flavor and a creamy consistency. Ingredients include soybean oil, whey, vinegar, buttermilk, sugar and egg yolks, with less than 2 percent chipotle chile pepper puree.

I had some confused idea based on the packaging that this was a chipotle sauce mainly for salads. It's a bit too flavored and strong with chipotle flavor to go well with my typical summer salads consisting of arugula, lettuce, tomatoes, feta cheese, anchovies and nuts, with the produce items hand-grown and picked. If I subtracted the anchovies, the sauce harmonized better, but still, this definitely is not an all-purpose flavoring. I think there may be too many warring ingredients for a theme to come through for this sauce.

So I switched to adding it to homemade tacos consisting of queso fresco or Monterey jack cheese with chopped onions, homegrown grape tomatoes on fresh tortillas from the nearby tortilleria. Much better results. I'm a fan of strong flavors, but it's tricky to figure out the best use for a premade chipotle sauce.

I notice Allrecipes has recommendations for enchiladas, turkey wraps, chicken in chipotle sauce and chipotle sweet potatoes, so these may be the best way to go.

I like Taco Bell so I was anxious to try this sauce.  It's ok but also typical of a lot of sauces.  The flavor is good and the consistency is creamy but it's not as hot as I'd expected.  Taco Bell isn't associated with healthy food so not surprisingly there are 11g of fat in each serving.  The calorie count isn't too high (110) but the calories from fat are 100.  If you're looking for very hot or less fat (or both) there are a lot of better alternatives on the market.

we tried the product on tacos and on taco salad, and it did not impress. Too many artificial ingredients make it taste dull and not fresh. Oddly bacon-like. I prefer plain salsa, green chilies, fresh guacamole, or sour cream (I substitute Greek yogurt; just as creamy, but less fat). For the chipotle flavor, I will try a home-made from scratch sauce.

When I tried it on a salad the taste overpowered the salad and was too spicy. When tried on tacos the effect was greatly diminished and resulted in a passable substitute for a carry out meal from Taco Bell. I wouldn't give up going down to my local restaurant for this at home substitute.

We used this sauce on tacos and as a dipping sauce. Though I am a big fan of Mexican food, I found the smokiness of the sauce to be overwhelming to the rest of the food. I could not taste the rest of the food. I would imagine, however, that if diluted in sour cream, the smokiness would serve as a compliment to chicken. I have to admit that I experiment a lot with dressings, sauces, spices, etc of different brands, and it's possible that the strength of "chipotle" flavored ingredients is simply not appealing to me. If you do try this, I'd use only a bit, to test the waters-the flavor and smell went right up my nose.

"A perfect finishing touch for your, tacos, Mexican salads, and sandwich wraps." - from the label

The Food Police will undoubtedly squeal when confronted by Taco Bell's "Home Originals" BOLD & CREAMY CHIPOTLE SAUCE. Is the home not sacred? Do the fast-food purveyors of unhealthy meals have to invade Man's last refuge? That provocation in itself makes the condiment endearing to me in addition to the fact that it's a striking radioactive-orange color (especially after being dispensed from the plastic squeeze bottle that will probably persist in a landfill until the Sun goes supernova - another endearing goad of the politically correct).

For the chipotle experience, I've heretofore relied on Kraft Sandwich Shop Mayo Chipotle, 12-Ounce Squeeze Bottles (Pack of 6)). Compared to this, the Taco Bell offering has a bit more intense smoky chipotle bite to it, and there's an undertone of cheese to the flavor perhaps imparted by the dried buttermilk in the ingredients. In any case, I've so far tried this sauce on chicken, beef, cheese sandwiches, eggs, and tater tots and licked drips off my fingers. To the extent used, I prefer it to the Kraft product and would preferentially buy it.

Nutritionally, this product contains (per 2 Tbsp serving) 110 calories, 11g total fat, 1.5g saturated fat, and 300mg sodium - all of which means that my health and nutrition-conscious wife will likely leave it all for me; I won't have to share.

Taco Bell's Chipotle sauce is the texture of a weak ranch dressing. Possibly due to this texture, the flavor vaguely reminds me of ranch dressing with some Mexican spices added. It isn't very spicy hot. On a scale of 1 to 10 with 10 being the hottest thing I've eaten, I'd put this sauce around 3. It is about as spicy as a typical packaged taco seasoning from a kit.

I tried the sauce seperately, on a bit of taco meat, and buried in a taco. I can't say that it ever tasted good, but it wasn't too bad when it was only providing a hint of flavor to the taco. I'd much rather have salsa or any of the great liquid hot sauces available online or at the supermarket.

According to the label, it has 110 calories and 11g of fat in a 2-Tbsp serving. The top ingredient is soybean oil. It says "contain milk, egg" in the allergen section of the label.

I added the Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce to BBQ chicken, soft taco shells along with sauteed onions, lettuce and tomatoes. It bought out great flavor with an extra kick. I agree with the previous review that the caloric intake is high at 110 which 100 is Fat Calories for just 2 tbspa. Just like anything else use in moderation to add extra spice to my meals.
Not only does the spice enhance your meal but there is a distinct smoky flavor also. So for those of you who do not have a grill this is a excellent alternative as a baste or even a marinade. I loved that it was thick and not "runny" I would definitively use this product again.

Enjoy!

Tasted kind of like old Ranch dressing. Boring and fairly unoffensive. Unmemorable. Creamy? Yes. Bold? Not so much.

I'm not really sure where this item fits into your condiment selections. Salad dressing? Not really. Salsa? No. On tacos? Maybe soft tacos...? Creamy tacos? That doesn't really fit either. Might do alright on a hamburger. I wasn't able to try that out before the item expired. Not spicy enough to replace salsa or tabasco. I can't recommend this.

Better than the Ranchero sauce, but not by much.  If you do not like things too spicy or too hot, but with a little kick of flavor, these dressings might be the ones for you.  I am not a big fan of heat, but I found myself reaching for the Tabasco when I made a burrito with this, but it worked just fine in a taco with a lot of lettuce and tomato.

I love chipotle. And I love Mexican food. What I have my doubts about sometimes is pre-fab food bought on the shelf (in other words, anything other than the basics....canned chilis, fresh salsa, and canned beans --or when I'm feeling especially motivated, dried beans I can prepare myself). But the promise of chipotle flavor was enough to get me to give this a try.

I like it! I first tried it on Taco Bell's own food....a couple of Tacos Supreme. But I've also used it with the best tortilla chips around. The chipotle flavor is evident, but it's not overwhelming. Which is good, because too much chipotle also can be way too hot.

I personally would not use this everytime I craved either chipotle or cheese, because I like making my own stuff and because the 300 grams of sodium is too much for me (health wise, not taste wise). But as a once-in-a-while, easy alternative, this is a condiment worth having on hand.

My family liked this taco sauce and said to give it 5 stars. I made a hamburger dish with it, with hamburger, rice, this sauce, and crumbled corn chips. It was quickly gobbled up.

The picture on the bottle of this sauce, is that of a taco. I guess that means it was intended for use on a taco. However, I made a taco hamburger skillet dish. I'm sure there are probably lots of recipes somewhere in which you could use this sauce, or you can just create you own, such as I did. Mine was really simple indeed, but loved by my family.

I am used to taco sauce being red, but this is a brownish-orangy, so I guess that makes it unique! As long as my family liked it, and I didn't have to throw it out (which I didn't), I guess it is good.

This creamy sauce is ok but not great.  It tasted oily, more like emulsified soybean oil with spices and chipotle flavor.  It does taste OK on tacos and taco salad though, but I don't recommend it as a dip, it doesn't blend well.  I have to point out that I received this sauce on Oct 4th and the bottle said: "Best if used by 29Sep2011".  Might be a reason why this sauce does not have the best flavor.

This sauce tastes pretty good! It's creamy, spicy (but not overly so), and has a nice flavor that pairs well with burritos and other Mexican-style foods. That said, I think it's a little bit overpriced for what it is. The bottle is quite small. 8 fluid ounces is the two-thirds the size of a soda can, so the amount of sauce you get really isn't very much at all. They make the bottle wide and skinny so that it has the appearance of capacity. The concave curves on the side further deceive the eye. So in summary, what we have here is a tasty sauce offered for a high price. I would recommend perhaps looking for a single bottle at your local supermarket before committing to an entire six-pack, to see if the flavor is worth the cost for you.

I tried the Taco Bell Chipotle sauce on my tacos the other night and did not like the flavor at all.  Previously I had tried the Jalapeno sauce and enjoyed it for being different from my regular taco sauce.  Not something I would use a lot but maybe every once it a while.  The chipotle sauce, on the other hand, tasted like a ranch style dressing with a bit of smoke flavor added it.  I was hoping for more of a real chipotle flavor like I've tasted from other sauces like the Tabasco Chipotle sauce.  I doubt I will use this sauce again.

I'm not a hot hot pepper addict (I can tolerate an 8 or 9 out of ten, but prefer somewhere around a 7), but I am pretty addicted to the flavor of hot sauces, and put them on almost everything. My favorites are chipotle Tabasco and sriracha, but years ago I fell in love with a sauce from a San Jose restaurant that looks a lot like this, so I had high hopes.

My first impression was that this just tastes like mildly chipotle-flavored ranch dressing, and given that buttermilk is the first or one of the first ingredients, I guess that makes sense. It's about the same consistency as ranch dressing, too. I've had this over black eyed peas and on a burrito.

The chipotle flavor is not strong, and not very spicy -- maybe a five -- so I'm still tempted to add some chipotle Tabasco to augment this. But really, if I'm going to do that, I might as well just mix some ranch dressing and Tabasco, since I'm already stocking those.

And yes, as others have noted, this is mostly not a food product, but a chemical concoction you couldn't make at home. It tastes as much like artificial flavoring as it does like anything else. Buuuut, it does taste good, and if you (or your kids) like the chipotle flavor but aren't very heat tolerant, this could be a good option.

I have to say, well done Taco Bell. This sauce is quite delicious. It has a tangy, bold flavor that good as an addition to tacos, burritos, nachos, as well as other non traditional items, such as salads and sandwiches. I would definitely recommend it and I look forward to trying it out on other items as well as trying other Taco Bell sauce flavors.

A delectable sauce with Mexican flair.  Mildly spicy with excellent taste.  My family used it with different dishes, including salads. The 8-ounce bottle did not have a chance in my home, as it was quickly and joyfully consumed within two weeks.
This was pretty good and goes easily on many things such as hamburgers and hotdogs etc and wouldn't make a terrible salad dressing either. Its not necessarily healthy however.

Yeah, Taco Bell isn't exactly associated with healthy living. While it may say Taco Bell on the label the sauces are actually manufactured by Kraft Foods. They pay Taco Bell to slap their name on the label and voila you get a more recognizable brand. The sauce is pretty typical. It's tangy, creamy with a little spice to it. Great for dipping. Try it out if your a fan of the flavor.

Well, honestly i didnt know what chipotle was before i got this. But i like sauces and so i just decided to give this a try...but unfortunately this product hasnt left a good impression of chipotle in me.
The flavor is some weird mix between spicy and sweet. Your initial taste is of sweetness and then your left with a spicy aftertaste. I had liked the mild sweetness initially. Its also got a smoky flavor in the spicy aftertaste similar to BBQ sauces. But the taste overall is just weak and undistinguishable (unless you put a big chunk in there).
On top of the weak taste, it gives you a fair amount fat/calories per serving(110 calories and 11g fat for 2 tablespoons) for a sauce. Personally, i say stay away from this.

I tried three of Taco Bell's sauces (creamy jalepeno, chipotle, spicy ranchero) and have reviewed them all on Amazon. This was my least favorite. The flavor is very strong and overwhelmed food items like traditional beef tacos and fish tacos for me. However, if you are a true lover of "chipotle flavor" you may have a different opinion. I could taste the vinegar used in this sauce which is a flavor I do not enjoy which is why I do not like jarred salsas either.

I did some further experimenting and baked some cheese enchiladas. After they came out of the oven I drizzled some sauce over the final product and enjoyed the flavor combination. I also think it would be good in a cheese ball as the smokiness and bold flavors would add a spark to the traditional cheese ball.

This sauce is okay, but nothing to write home about.  In the past, my experience with chipotle was on a sub at Subway, which I absolutely loved.  Ever since then, I've been trying to find a close match.  If I'm buying Chipotle sauce in the future, I'll try other brands to see if I can match Subway's perfection.  If there are no other brands, I'll probably pass on buying any type of chipotle sauce.
Not too spicy, not too bland.  I love this stuff on a sandwich.  This sauce really makes sandwiches taste much better than using mayo or mustard.  Its a nice change from boring sandwiches for lunch.

Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce has a creamy texture, packed with a tangy taste that's perfect for tacos, chip dip, Chinese fried rice, pizza (yes, pizza) and even sandwiches. It's flavorful and spicy, but not in a hot way. The bottle is easy to open and the sauce itself has a thick consistency. It pours well out of the bottle. I'm sold on the taste and plan to buy more once this bottle is over. Highly recommended.

I love tacos.  I love chipotle sauce. I thought this would be the perfect combination of both.  While the sauce was good, it was spicier than I expected and it's creamier texture wasn't quite what I really like.  It was nice for a change in taste, but not something I would use all the time since I'm not a "spicy" person.  I personally will stick with my taco sauce, but if you like spicy and want a creamy texture on your next taco then you will enjoy this product by Taco Bell.

This sauce looks like an orange tinted thousands islands salad dressing and tastes similar as well. There is a hint of horseradish that smells stronger than it tastes. The sauce is more tangy than hot. It is fairly thick and after refrigerating the last quarter of the sauce doesn't flow out very easily even when the bottle is shaken. The bottle will give you maybe 6 servings.

If you like orange colored food and the taste of thousand island dressing you will like this sauce.

Chipotle is one of my favorite flavors in the world. I cook with them all the time, make chipotle sauces and marinades, and chipotle mustards. Because I usually make my own sauces and dips, I had pretty low expectations regarding this "Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce."

My low expectations were met.

The chipotle flavor is stronger than I was expecting, and the taste wasn't bad at all. Neither was it good. It has a distinct fast food flavor. This is basically a bottled version of the sauce fast food restaurants might put on their "chipotle burgers" or maybe a "chipotle dip" to each with French fries. Which is exactly what I used it for.

If you are craving that fast food taste at home, then this might be right up your alley. Me, I would rather just whip together a tin of canned chipotles and some mayonnaise to get roughly the same effect, and probably better.

This is the stuff they put in the baja gordita (I think).  It has the consistency of Mayo, but it has a little spice to it.  Now, if anyone has had the "hot" or "fire" sauce at Taco Bell, then you understand that they are not known for making things very hot at all, and this is exactly the same.  It is just slightly spicy, but not very hot at all.  I am currently using it on almost everything I eat, from eggs to hamburgers and, of course, tacos!

I've always ordered chipotle sauce on my sandwiches when I eat out but never could duplicate those sandwiches at home. I tried a chipotle mayo that's on the market, but it wasn't the same. And then I received a sample of this. This is exactly what I was looking for. It's got the same kick as the sauce at a major sandwich chain that I love. I tried this on more than just my sub sandwiches though. It's yummy on quesedillas, fajitas, and tacos. Plus, it's good for dipping veggies and fries. I'll definitely be buying more of this when my bottle runs out.

Yum a bit of Taco Bell right in my own home! Around my house we LOVE spicy and this really hits the spot whether it be a breakfast burrito, nachos or whatever we may fix, my children LOVE to put it on everything! Has a bit of a zing to it and I am so glad I got to try it! I am wanting to try the other sauces now as well!

Great addition to eggs in the morning, or any kind of wrap/burrito/chimichanga you are making. If you make some kind of mexican meatloaf this would be a wonderful addition, would give it a definite kick!!!

If you like spicy things, this is for YOU!

My family likes Taco Bell and we like this Chipotle Sauce okay. We eat Mexican-ish style dishes quite a bit at home, so it's nice to have a bottled sauce for a little extra kick. I do like the chipotle flavor in this particular sauce, but of course, not everyone has the same tastes. I also liked that it comes in a squeeze bottle with a flip lid with a small hole, rather than having to try to pour it out of the larger opening. That makes it convenient for adding just the amount you want. It can be used as a salad dressing, if you like thick dressings... or as a dipping sauce for tortilla chips, or on tacos, burritos, what-have-you.

I love Taco Bell products! This sauce is really good and goes well with many different things. I added some to our Taco night and it was a hit. If you like Chipotle, then you really need to try this sauce! It's good to add or to cook with!

Chipotle is one of my favorite flavors, and this Taco Bell Chipotle sauce does not disappoint.  The sauce is more the consistency of mayo rather than the runny hot sauce consistency of other chipotle sauces I've tried, which made it a tad milder, and also helped keep it on the food instead of running off.  Obviously, it goes great on tex-mex food, but I also put it on a whopper and loved it.  How about getting this sauce in the restaurants?

This is a good, classic chipotle flavor sauce. It has the thickness of a creamy salad dressing and delivers the chipotle flavor. I used it on a grilled chicken sandwich with avocado and cheddar cheese and this worked great. I could also see using on burgers, tacos, maybe even as a salad dressing. Taco Bell did a good job with this sauce.

It had this sharp taste to it that didn't agree with me somehow.  I tried it more than once to see if I could like it, but it had more of a bitter taste to it.  It could use some sweetness and some other spices.  I am not an expert on that.

I used this sauce on some chicken fajitas and quesadillas I made and they were DELICIOUS! I also used it as a dip for some other stuff...it is so yummy! It is a little spicy because of the chipotle but I like spice! It is a good substitute for ketchup too. It isn't too thick but it is very creamy, the consistency of a ranch dressing but the flavor is so much better. I really loved it!

Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce

Rich and creamy, extraordinarily tasty! :) Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is an extremely versatile sauce, whether served on tacos, with oven-warmed tortilla chips, or just as a dip for hard boiled eggs, cheese sticks or vegies.

Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce is sure to be a hit, no matter how you serve it.

Even Dad loves Taco Bell Chipotle Sauce, and he can be a really picky eater. Best to pick up a few extra bottles, just in case! 'nuf said! :) Highly Recommended! --Katharena Eiermann, 2011

Pretty versatile sauce, I have used it on tacos obviously, but it is also a good chip dipping sauce and mixed it with ranch dressing and put it on a salad.  It really gave it a BBQ Ranch dressing flavor that became pretty addictive.  It's pretty spicy but not overwhelming and left me with a tart after taste.  I believe it is that same sauce that taco bell uses on their quesadillas.

The thing with Taco Bell products is that though they are not really "Mexican" they are always a tasty delight and this no exception.
I love the intense Chipotle taste, a hint of Garlic (not over done) just just hot enough to please, and it goes with just about anything.
In my opinion it tastes best at room temperature or even warmed up rather than cold "out-of-the fridge" which seems to inhibit the taste somewhat though in my opinion salsas always taste better warm or even hot!

This won't disappoint at all and I just loved it!

I was really interested in trying this product one I saw it.  I usually like the taco bell products that come out at the store.  They make some decent products that are available in the grocery stores.  This one is a new chipolte sauce and Sounded great as a way to spice up your meals.  I added some of this to tacos and also to some hamburgers.  It added a good flavor and a nice change to the meals.  The sauce wasnt as spicy as i would like but overall it tasted good though.  I would recommend if you want a little something different to add to your meals though.

This might be ok for "taco night" for dinner but other than that this is nothing to write home about. I've tasted other chipotle sauces that are much better than this. This definitely needs some work if they want people to buy this on a regular basis. Why some reviewers are raving and giving this 5 star reviews I have no idea why they would praise something like this.

Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce is tasty, lending a smoky zing to whatever you happen to use it with.  The list of ingredients, however, is quite extensive, so don't anticipate that what comes out of the bottle is anything remotely akin to healthy.  Good for an occasional foray into the decandent and fatty world of fast-food-type condiments.

The additional spices, especially the hickory really add something special to this sauce. As with the Jalapeño sauce we've  used this on burgers, sandwiches, and Mexican meals at home. As much as we like the Jalapeño, this one tops it because of the awesome hickory note balancing the heat of the Chipotle. Two thumbs up and a big hit with our family.

A nice change of taste for a Taco.  I put a little sauce in with some canned roast beef, warmed it up and put in  a corn tortilla  just like I would for a taco with ground beef.  It had a delicious taste reminiscent of something I tasted in Mexico years ago.  I love the  smoked pepper chipotle taste but not having to make the sauce.  Much easier to buy this tasty condiment instead.  I bet it would be good with chicken or fish tacos too.

There really wasn't a lot of heat in this one for me, although I do like things hotter than most folks. I don't have Mexican food (or chips) in the house or eat it on regular occasions so I haven't been able to sample try this product out on them. I did try it as a condiment to my ever-so-boring turkey and it was OK, but I prefer the spicy mustards instead. I did try some today in a salad and that was OK, but not one I'd recommend or use again. The product has an oily texture/taste to it, and if I was going to go for something so fatty I think I'd prefer it to be a sour cream base instead of oil base.

If you aren't worried about fat and calories and eat a lot of Mexican food products this might suit, but otherwise I'd give it a pass. There's not enough flavor to make it worth the added calories for me.

Not a bad sauce but there does seem to be something I cannot quite pinpoint that seems to be missing in spice.  It is unexpectedly mild for a chipotle-based condiment giving the impression that it is a bit dull.  Spice is a matter of taste perhaps but I suspect this will be less than most would expect.  It may solve the problem of disguising leftovers once in a while but it is certainly nothing to get excited about.

In my personal opinion, this is basically an overly processed fatty salad dressing made from a soybean oil base. I love Mexican food generally and salads, but was put off by the label showing such a high fat content (11 grams for just a couple tablespoons) and also the chemical preservatives listed on the label that I cannot pronounce.  I tasted a wee bit on my finger and was kind of shocked by that strong "natural smoke flavor" and the vinegary, salty and bitter taste on my tongue. I noticed a little chili heat, which I like.  Since I was making homemade tostadas with fresh chopped lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, onions, guacamole, pico, sour cream and beans on a corn tortilla, I thought this would be the perfect compliment. All I can say is that for me it is not worth the dietary failings of the product as I don't like the strong smoke taste, even once tossed with alot of fresh ingredients, and it is high in fat and preserved.  I would much rather spice up my fresh guacamole with cayenne/chili and know that the fat I am getting is a more healthful type.  I will not be buying this product.

My first thought was that the Taco Bell sauce would be good as a dip. Since my garden is now producing cucumbers at a scary rate, I tried the sauce as a cucumber salad dressing as soon as I opened the bottle. It worked very well. The sauce is smooth, has some sharpness to it, but is not overly spicy. After the cucumber experiment, I placed the opened bottle in the refrigerator. I will try it again as a salad dressing when the tomatoes in the garden turn red, Right now they are still green. They will probably turn all at once, so I will have to figure out ways to consume them.

My impression of the Taco Bell sauce after refrigeration was that it has almost the same consistency as mayonnaise, This gave me another idea. I usually make tuna salad by mixing mayonnaise, hot sauce, and a few spices into the tuna. This time I mixed in only the Taco Bell sauce. Incidentally, the sauce has half the calories per tablespoon compared to the mayonnaise. The tuna salad turned out well. It was very similar to my mayonnaise-based version.

I was pleasantly surprised by my initial experiments with the sauce. I have tried both the Chipotle and Jalapeno versions. They both work equally well. That is, I find it hard to tell the differences in taste. The one negative is that they contain artificial coloring and flavoring. They lose a star on that account.
This sauce is very tasty!  My husband loves it too - it's slightly spicy, creamy, and delicious!

This Taco Bell Chipotle sauce is quite enjoyable and has the tangy yet not very spicy taste you would expect. I have used it on burritos and as a dip. There is no question that if you like the flavor of Chipotle sauce you will enjoy this. But it is high in calories which I expected and did not mind for you do not need a lot too enjoy the flavor.

Yet two tablespoons of this sauce contains 100 calories from fat and a total of 110 calories per serving size. The serving size is the aforementioned two tablespoons. It taste great just be aware of its high fat content and calories. When serving size is measured by the spoon full you know the calories are high. And even so, I would get this product again.

I liked this, but not enough to be a frequent purchase.  This is not a particularly spicy sauce, was flavorful but mild, so lacked real heat.  The consistency was thick and creamy, non-greasy.  Worth ocassional variety.  I do not eat Taco Bell enough to compare this to a menu item.

What a surprise this was! I have a love affair with chipotle sauce, so I was really looking forward to trying out Taco Bell's Chipotle Sauce and I have to say how much I enjoyed it! I tried it on some tacos we made for dinner last night and it really spiced them up! Changed the flavor and really brought out the ground beef we were using, they were so good that hubby asked if we could try it as a sandwich spread for lunch today. So how was that sandwich? As a spread I have to warn you not to add too much for it does make the bread a little soggy if you make your lunch the night before, but it really adds a flavor boost to your food. The flavor is a spicy and very slightly smoked bold chipotle taste. If I was ranking it between Taco Bell sauce packets I would have to say this is ranked between Hot & Fire. If you're a Mild type person then I would personally stay away from this sauce for it was not mild at all.

Can't wait to try it on many different things, up next is a chicken salad with corn salsa! Mmm we expect many great things out of our bottle!

This product is tasty, spicy, and carries a nice kick. I was surprised, as I expected something more bland coming from Taco Bell, but this was full up good.

I have found it makes an excellent dressing for a taco salad. It also makes an excellent filling for an omelet, turning a plain omelet into a Mexican treat. I can also imagine it would be good inside a home made cassadia.

In any case, I will definitely be keeping this as a staple in the refrigerator.

Taco Bell's Bold & Creamy Chipotle Sauce is perfectly described in its name. This is a thick sauce with a strong smoky flavor and although it is quite spicy, there is little heat. I first used it to spice up black beans being served as a side dish for tacos. The beans are so bland, they always need something, and this sauce was the perfect addition.

The sauce also worked beautifully with falafels - again, just the right amount of spice and it gave the pita bread sandwich stuffed with lettuce, tomato, cucumber and falafel balls a needed jolt. Finally, I used the sauce on a veggie burger and it also worked beautifully there, too. I was pleased with the results each time I used it, and found the sauce very versatile.

The only negative is it not low on calories - two tablespoons have 110 calories and 100 of those are fat calories - so I use it sparingly. That said, it is sufficiently spiced so that a little goes a long way.

My husband is a huge Mexican food fan, so I let him try this first. He liked it, said it was spicy, but not too much for him. He liked the flavor, and said it reminded him of the sauce they give with chicken fingers at Zaxby's. He said it would be great on a Taco salad, or even to eat with veggies on a snack tray for a party. So I tried it myself. I don't like spicy/hot foods, and this was not overpoweringly spicy. Just enough. I think it would be a good sauce to mix with a bit of sour cream and cheese for a dip, too. So Taco Bell, we love you. You did it again.

My whole family liked this product. It has a smoky chipotle flavor that (when tasted alone) leaves a slight burn on the back of your throat. We used it on tacos and the sauce gave them a very distinct taste that we all enjoyed (no burn :) ). My husband is incredibly picky and said he liked it and would eat it again. The Kid thought it would even taste good on a salad. I'm thinking it might also be good as a marinade.

I would definitely recommend it the next time you want to add something a bit different to your meal.

On a pure taste basis, this sauce gets 5 stars. (I am not going to address the nutritional aspect. Read the nutritional label and you can see that this is not "clean eating" or health food. But if you want healthy food, you're probably not reaching for something that says Taco Bell, anyway.)

I love spicy food, and I found that this sauce has a nice zip to it. For sensitive tongues, it may even be too spicy if too much is used. It's nice and creamy with that smokey chipotle flavor coming through the spice.

This sauce works well on tacos, sandwiches (although a bit runny), and nachos or layered taco dips.

Bold and spicy are good descriptors for this brightly colored chipotle sauce. It reminds me of the sauces at Taco Bell and thus does a great job of emulating them. I have used it on tacos, burittos and fajitas. Just spicy enough to be noticable but not too over the top.
